efforts.effort_name: Labor Reallocation, Care Bottlenecks & Offshoring Spillovers

wave1.lens_self_description: I answered purely as an outside-view reference-class historian: every number is a historical base rate over the widest defensible window, adjusted only for the mechanical arithmetic in the locked priors (weights, old-age ratios, starting yields), which forbade me from using any reasoning about AI capability trajectories, model releases, scaling, agentic diffusion speed, or any mechanism specific to this episode — I treated "AI" only as an unnamed general-purpose technology shock with a historical GPT diffusion base rate.
wave1.cq1_reasoning: Conjunct A (OECD-38 harmonised unemployment 2032-36 average <= 5.5%): REFERENCE CLASS = all OECD-area 5-year averages of the harmonised rate. FRED's OECD total-area annual series (LRHUTTTTO1A156S, 1999-2016, discontinued) prints 6.2% in 2000, ~8.3% in 2010, 6.3% in 2016 — not one 5-year window in that 13-window span averaged <= 5.5%; the G7 series (LRHUTTTTG7A156S, 1991-2016) bottoms at 5.4% (2007) and 5.5% (2016) in single years only. Adding the 1970s-80s (OECD 7-8%) and 1990s (~7%) gives a base rate of roughly 4-8 of ~52 overlapping windows, ~10-13%, essentially all of it the early-1970s pre-oil-shock windows. OBSERVED: the 2023-26 level (~4.9-5.0%) is a genuine record low, so I am being asked for the persistence of an unprecedented state for a further 6-10 years. INFERRED adjustment: the locked old-age ratio (31% -> 39-41%) mechanically shrinks the labour-force denominator and is a one-directional downward force on the measured rate (Japan's severe-aging analogue holds 2.4-2.8%); against that, the base rate of a 5-year window containing at least one OECD recession is ~50-55%, and a recession adds 1.0-3.0pp to the window average. Net marginal A = 0.40. Conjunct B (F+Q real median hourly wage growth beating J+K+M by >= 10.0pp cumulative, 2025-2036): REFERENCE CLASS = 11-year inter-sector real wage divergences in the pro-physical direction. The modal 1980-2015 OECD outcome is the OPPOSITE sign (skill-biased technical change: finance/professional real wages far outran construction and care). Pro-physical compressions of this size occur roughly in the 1940s US Great Compression, post-1945 European wage compression, and the 2020-24 low-wage surge (Autor-Dube-McGrew find ~10pp bottom-vs-top quartile over 4 years) — about 2-3 of ~8 non-overlapping 11-year windows since 1940, and F+Q is NOT the bottom quartile (F carries skilled trades, Q carries physicians) while J+K+M is not the top quartile. Decisive historical datum for my effort: OECD's own *Beyond Applause* finds LTC workers receive below-average wages compared with other workers of similar characteristics DESPITE shortages the OECD has been documenting since the late 1990s — a 25-year base rate of non-clearing, because care pay is fiscally administered (public scales, reimbursement rates) and 2A says that fiscal channel is already strained (China's subsidy at 10.1% of fiscal expenditure; global debt > 100% of GDP by 2029). Baumol closes the loop: *Who Cares?* needs +60% LTC workers by 2040 (13.5M OECD-wide; ~44%/≈9.9M pro-rated to 2036, ~5M if the report's technology-and-work-arrangement halving lands), with near-zero sectoral productivity growth, so a 10pp relative real wage gain must be paid from transfers rather than productivity. Marginal B = 0.20. CORRELATION: strongly positive and I used +0.35 — tight labour markets are exactly when bottom-sector real wages compress the gap (2021-24), and construction (F) is the single most cyclical sector, so a recession breaks both conjuncts at once. P(B|A) = 0.30. JOINT = 0.40 x 0.30 = 0.12. Cross-elasticity arithmetic behind the low B: reference classes for displaced-worker reallocation into care give ~5-8% of displaced US manufacturing workers (1999-2011) and ~2-4% of UK ex-miners (1984-94) re-employed in health/social care within five years, i.e. a direct stock-flow cross-elasticity of roughly 0.05-0.10 (one care entrant per 10-20 displaced cognitive workers), with new-RN-licensee shares aged 40+ historically ~6-8%, a 1-year LPN / 2-4-year RN licensing queue, a ~85-90% female care workforce against a ~55-60% male displaced J/K/M pool, and nursing-assistant musculoskeletal injury rates roughly 3x the all-worker BLS rate for a median displaced worker in their mid-40s.
wave1.cq2_reasoning: Conjunct A (OECD-38 GDP-weighted core inflation >= 2.50%/yr average 2027-2036): REFERENCE CLASS 1 = all OECD 10-year windows since 1960: roughly 1960-1999 windows all clear 2.5% (1970s ~8-9%, 1980s ~5-6%, 1990s ~3%) while 2000-2019 windows do not (2000s ~1.9-2.1%, 2010s ~1.4-1.6%), giving ~60-65% unconditional. REFERENCE CLASS 2 (narrower, structurally honest) = credible inflation-targeting-era windows, 1995-2026: almost all print 1.6-2.3%, with only the most recent windows pulled to ~2.3-2.6% by the 2021-23 shock, giving ~20-25%. I weighted the IT-era class ~60/40 because the regime break (independent central banks, explicit 2% targets) is mechanical rather than mechanism-specific, landing at 0.35. Conjunct B (China headline CPI < 1.50%/yr average 2027-2036): REFERENCE CLASS = China CPI 10-year windows since 1980: decade averages ~7% (1980s), ~7.7% (1990s), ~1.9% (2000s), ~2.3% (2010-19), ~0.6% (2020-26); only a handful of ~37 rolling windows (late-1990s deflation windows, 2015-24, 2017-26) land below 1.50%, ~15-20% unconditional. But the governing class is persistence out of a post-property-bust demographic-contraction trap, where the reference set is essentially Japan 1995-2020: CPI averaged ~0.1%/yr for 25 years and the base rate of exiting within a decade is 0 of 2 decades. Conditional on the locked 2A state (CPI ~0-0.5%, -60M population 2026-35, worker/retiree 4.4 -> 2.8), B = 0.58. CORRELATION: the conjunction requires a SUSTAINED OECD-vs-China inflation DIVERGENCE, and OECD/EM inflation co-moves positively through commodities and traded goods, which argues for a discount; offsetting that, the OECD-vs-Japan analogue shows exactly this ~2pp divergence held for 25 years, and it held in precisely the demographic-contraction-plus-balance-sheet case. I therefore used a correlation near zero-to-slightly-negative, P(B|A) = 0.52. JOINT = 0.35 x 0.52 = 0.182 -> 18. Note the two-sided 2A content I did NOT resolve by mechanism: Goodhart-Pradhan aging-as-inflationary (labour scarcity, dissaving) versus BIS AER 2026 Box C aging/automation-as-demand-shortfall. The historical record contains both signs, which is itself a reason not to sharpen.
wave1.cq3_reasoning: REFERENCE CLASS = PPP-weighted 5-year averages of combined OECD + China real growth since 1960, reconstructed from OECD area growth (1960s ~5%, 1970s ~3.5%, 1980s ~3%, 1990s ~2.6%, 2000s ~1.8%, 2010s ~2.0%) and China (1980s ~9.8%, 1990s ~10%, 2000s ~10.4%, 2010s ~7.7%, 2020s ~5%) at contemporaneous PPP weights. UNCONDITIONAL DISTRIBUTION: essentially every 5-year window since 1960 landed above 2.6% — my arithmetic puts 2010-14 at ~4.3%, 2015-19 at ~3.6% (OECD 2.3%, China 6.7%, weights ~0.71/0.29), and 2020-24 at ~2.54% (OECD 1.5%, China 4.76%, weights ~0.68/0.32). So the honest unconditional base rate for CQ6-A's >= 2.6% band is roughly 90%+, for B roughly 5-10%, for C and D roughly 0%. I DEVIATE FROM IT DELIBERATELY, and this is the one place my lens permits it, because the series is non-stationary in an arithmetically transparent way: the aggregate has fallen almost exactly 1pp per decade for three decades, and the fall is pure weight-times-growth arithmetic driven by China's convergence ending, not by any episode-specific mechanism. Trend-extrapolating that monotone decline 10 years from the last-known 2.54% gives ~1.8-2.0%. BOTTOM-UP CHECK ON LOCKED PRIORS ONLY: OECD per-capita 0.6%/yr (2A) + OECD population growth ~0.2-0.3%/yr = OECD ~0.8-0.9%; China ~2.5-3.5% with the locked -2.7pp aging drag already embedded; China PPP weight rising to ~0.38-0.40 by mid-window gives 0.61x0.9 + 0.39x3.0 = 1.72%, or 0.61x1.5 + 0.39x3.5 = 2.28% if an OECD productivity offset arrives. P50 1.95% sits between those. SECOND REFERENCE CLASS for the downside: advanced economies after a demographic/balance-sheet peak — Japan's post-1991 5-year windows ran 1.4%, 0.7%, 1.0%, 0.5%, and the base rate of recovering to pre-peak growth within 15 years is 0 of 4. DISPERSION: historical 5-year-average dispersion for this aggregate is roughly +/-0.8-1.0pp around trend; a window containing a synchronised recession (base rate ~50% per 5-year window) subtracts ~0.8-1.2pp from the average. P10 1.0% is the one-recession path, P90 2.95% respects how rarely this series has printed low and leaves A reachable.
wave1.cq4_reasoning: REFERENCE CLASS = G7 10y real yields by decade. Approximate GDP-weighted decade averages: 1970s negative (roughly -1% to -2% ex post, US 10y ex-post real ~-1%); 1980s ~+4.5-5.0% (Macrobond puts US 10y real near 5% and calls it the best decade); 1990s ~+3.5-4.0%; 2000s ~+2.0% (US TIPS 1999-2007 ~2.2%); 2010s ~+0.3% (QIC: US 10y real averaged 0.3% post-GFC, with Germany and Japan near or below zero); 2020-2026 ~+0.3-0.8% GDP-weighted (deeply negative 2020-21, +1.5-2.6% 2023-26). The IMF's global series falls from ~6% (1983) to ~0% (2012); Schmelzing/Bank of England's eight-century study finds a suprasecular decline with temporary reversals and a long-run safe real rate well under the 1980s level. STARTING LEVEL (mechanical, from the locked prior): US 10y TIPS 2.60% (DFII10, Oct 30 2026); applying G7 GDP weights (~US 0.50, Japan 0.11, Germany 0.11, UK 0.07, France 0.07, Italy 0.06, Canada 0.05) to the plausible cross-section (Japan and Germany ~0.8-0.9%, UK/Italy/Canada ~1.8%, France ~1.3%) gives a G7-weighted start of ~1.90%. BASE RATE OF A DECADE-AVERAGE REAL YIELD STAYING NEAR ITS STARTING LEVEL: real-yield regimes persist in multi-decade cycles (1950s-1981 up, 1981-2021 down), so the current level is the best single predictor, but the frequency of a 5-year average landing within +/-50bp of the starting level is only ~30-35% — the distribution is wide, not sticky. I therefore center on the starting level (P50 2.0%, a 10bp mean-reversion tilt toward the long-run ~1.5-2.5% advanced-economy mean) with historically-sized dispersion. RIGHT SKEW: 2A's arithmetic (global public debt > 100% of GDP by 2029, net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP, +1.0pp worse global r-g, 3-year P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117% of GDP) and the eroding-convenience-yield/basis-trade plumbing push the upper tail, giving P90 3.3% — which would still be below every 1980s and 1990s decade average, so it is not an extreme call by base rate. LEFT TAIL: the base rate of financial repression and central-bank/pension demand capping G7 real yields during a fiscal stress episode is high (1940s-50s, 2010s), and a recession in the window is a ~50% event, so P10 0.8% is well inside the historical record.
wave1.cq5_reasoning: Conjunct A (MOVE 2027-2036 average >= 105): REFERENCE CLASS = MOVE history. Secondary sources put the long-run average at 93.6 since 1988 (ICE's own data page says history from 1996, so the start date is contested — flagging that), the 10-year average at ~75 (Carmignac), the 2017-2019 average at ~55, and the 2022 cycle at ~130. A threshold of 105 is therefore materially ABOVE the full-history mean. Reconstructing 10-year window averages: the late-1980s/1990s windows (~105-115) clear it, the 2000s (~95) borderline-fail, the 2010s (~70-80) fail badly, and 2017-2026 (~95-100) is borderline. That is roughly 6-8 of ~28 windows, ~22-28%. Adjusting up for the purely arithmetic content of 2A (far larger duration supply, net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP, levered basis-trade absorption replacing price-insensitive convenience-yield demand — all mechanical, not AI-specific), marginal A = 0.35. Conjunct B (>= one MSCI World >= 25% peak-to-trough drawdown in 2027-36 WITH G7 10y nominals failing to fall >= 50bp, or rising >= 25bp, in that window): REFERENCE CLASS = world-equity drawdowns >= 25% since 1970: 1973-74, 1980-82, 1987, 1990, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020, 2022 — about 8 in 56 years, roughly one per 7 years, so P(at least one in a 10-year window) ~0.80-0.85 and the Poisson intensity is lambda ~1.4 per decade. CONDITIONAL FREQUENCY THAT BONDS FAILED TO RALLY >= 50bp: the correlated regime is 1973-74, 1980-82 and 2022 (yields rose through the drawdown) versus the flight-to-quality regime in 1987, 1990, 2000-02, 2008-09 and 2020 — 3 of 8, ~38%. Compounding over the decade: 1 - exp(-1.4 x 0.38) = 0.41, so marginal B = 0.40. CORRELATION: strongly positive, and I used ~+0.5 — a high-MOVE decade IS the inflation/term-premium regime in which sovereigns stop hedging equities, so P(B|A) rises from 0.40 to ~0.62. JOINT = 0.35 x 0.62 = 0.217 -> 22. OBSERVED vs INFERRED: the drawdown and conditional-failure frequencies are observed history; the +0.5 correlation and the upward tilt on A are inferred.
wave1.cq6_reasoning: CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED, in lexical-priority order, against my own CQ3 and CQ2. Step 1, A = P(CQ3 growth >= 2.6%). From my CQ3 distribution (P10 1.0, P50 1.95, P90 2.95, mild right skew), P(>= 2.6%) = 0.155, so A = 15. I did NOT apply A's qualitative clauses (debt stabilisation, broad wage gains) because the lock makes rule 1 purely a growth test; had I applied them, A would be lower, and the 15 is thus an upper bound. Residual mass 85 is distributed over C, D, B. Step 2, C = P(growth < 2.0% AND OECD core inflation 2032-36 >= 2.7%). From CQ3, P(growth < 2.0%) = 0.52. For the inflation leg I used the same distribution that produced my CQ2 conjunct A (P(10yr 2027-36 core >= 2.50%) = 0.35): for the shorter, higher-variance 2032-36 window I take P50 core ~2.3%, P(>= 2.7%) = 0.23 — necessarily below 0.35 because the threshold is higher, which is the consistency link to CQ2. Independent product 0.52 x 0.23 = 0.12, raised to 0.15 for the historically real positive co-occurrence of low growth with high inflation under supply constraints (the 1970s stagflation cell plus 2A's grid/care supply walls and the Baumol care-cost channel from my effort). C = 15. Step 3, D = P(growth < 1.7% AND core < 2.0%), disjoint from C by construction. From CQ3, P(growth < 1.7%) = 0.37; P(core < 2.0%) ~ 0.30. Independent product 0.11, raised to 0.16 for the positive low-growth/low-inflation correlation that dominates the Japan-post-1991 reference class and is exactly the BIS Box C labour-income-deficit cell. D = 16. Step 4, B = residual = 100 - 15 - 15 - 16 = 54. B is the correct modal regime here not because I find the barbell story compelling but because the lock makes B the residual cell, absorbing all of growth 1.7-2.5% at any inflation plus the low-growth/moderate-inflation leftover, and my CQ3 P50 of 1.95% sits inside it. Sums to exactly 100. CROSS-CHECK AGAINST CQ2: my CQ2 of 18 is a JOINT (OECD hot AND China cold) and so must be below my OECD-only 0.35 marginal and is not directly comparable to C's 15, which conditions on low growth and a higher threshold; the two are mutually consistent. BASE-RATE DISCLOSURE: the unconditional historical distribution of this growth aggregate since 1960 puts ~90%+ of 5-year windows in band A and ~0% in C or D, so my A of 15 is an enormous deviation from the naive outside view, justified solely by the monotone weight-times-growth arithmetic in CQ3 and by the Japan-after-the-demographic-peak class, which has never reverted.

hypothesis_critique.a: The failing word is SMOOTHLY, and secondarily SUPPLY. Reference classes for mid-career cross-occupational reallocation: ~5-8% of displaced US manufacturing workers (1999-2011) and ~2-4% of UK ex-miners (1984-94) were re-employed in health/social care within five years — many exited the labour force or went onto disability instead — implying a direct cross-elasticity of roughly 0.05-0.10, one care entrant per 10-20 displaced cognitive workers. Every friction in my brief points the same way and none offsets: a 1-year LPN / 2-4-year RN licensing queue with new-licensee shares aged 40+ historically ~6-8%; a reservation-wage gap (aide pay near the bottom decile against a mid-career J/K/M wage); an ~85-90% female care workforce against a ~55-60% male displaced pool; nursing-assistant musculoskeletal injury rates roughly 3x the all-worker BLS rate for a median displaced worker in their mid-40s; and geographic immobility, since care demand is where the old live and housing costs are where the displaced live. Scale check: OECD's Who Cares? needs +60% LTC workers by 2040 (13.5M OECD-wide, ~9.9M pro-rated to 2036, ~5M if its technology-and-work-arrangement halving lands) against an OECD J/K/M employment base in the tens of millions — so even the arithmetic ceiling requires a cross-elasticity an order of magnitude above anything in the record. Note the plank is not quite false in sign: some reallocation will occur. It is false in rate, and SMOOTHLY is a claim about rate.
hypothesis_critique.b: The failing words are SEVERELY and BLOCKS. BLOCKS fails on reference class: the base rate of 'automation will destroy offshoring' claims resolving true within a decade is about 0 of 3 — the post-Y2K 2001-02 prediction preceded Indian IT-BPM going from roughly $8B to the locked ~$280B scale, and the 2015-2020 RPA wave coincided with Philippine BPO headcount rising from ~1.0M to the locked 1.7M+. The base rate of a traded-services export category declining in nominal USD over 11 years is on the order of 10%; growth-rate compression from ~8-9%/yr to ~2-4%/yr is the modal maturing-export outcome (UK financial-services exports post-2008, Irish call centres post-2005). BLOCKS also ignores the opposite-signed physical leg entirely, which is the point of this effort. SEVERELY fails on remittances: annual remittance receipts to India and the Philippines have declined in only about 2-3 years since 1990 and recovered within a year each time. QUANTIFIED LEGS, central case: virtual leg = a level shortfall of ~25-45% versus the no-compression counterfactual by 2036, i.e. roughly -$90B to -$160B/yr for India and -300k to -550k Philippine jobs versus counterfactual (NOT versus the 2025 level, which likely still rises). Physical leg = an OECD LTC gap of ~5-10M by 2036, but historically supply-constrained by OECD immigration policy rather than source-country supply: the foreign-born share of OECD nurses rose only from ~14% to ~16% over 2010-2020, and the 2015-2025 base rate is political tightening DESPITE documented shortages, so even an aggressive +10pp foreign-born share yields only ~1.0-1.5M additional migrant care workers, of which India plus the Philippines plausibly 30-40%, i.e. +300-600k, plus skilled trades. Remittance value per migrant care worker runs roughly 3-6x per-worker BPO wage income, so the physical leg's gross gain is on the order of $10-25B/yr by 2036 for the two combined. NET versus counterfactual: negative, roughly -$70B to -$140B/yr, but NOT 'severe' against 2025 levels. Add a ~1-in-3 base rate of a GCC oil-fiscal remittance shock within the decade (2015-16 cut Gulf-to-India flows by roughly 9%), which is demographically unrelated to OECD aging and is the real tail risk for both countries.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failing words are THEN FALLS — specifically the implied single smooth hump. The direction is the base-rate-correct part (inflation mean-reverts, and inflation-targeting-era 10-year windows cluster at 1.6-2.3%), which is why this plank scores far above the others. What fails is the shape: of the five G7 inflation episodes above 5% since 1945 (1947, 1951, 1974, 1980, 2022), about three had a second wave within ten years (1947->1951, 1974->1980, 1951->1956 mildly), so the base rate of a clean one-and-done disinflation is only ~40-50%. The plank's front half is also already partly spent — on the locked 2A reading, the hot phase is largely behind rather than ahead, so 'the next few years' is mis-timed. And the plank is silent on the cross-section: the locked priors make the interesting fact a DIVERGENCE (OECD versus China) rather than a level path, which is what CQ2 actually asks.
hypothesis_critique.d: The failing words are EVENTUALLY and WINS. EVENTUALLY makes the plank unfalsifiable within the 2036 horizon, which is the only horizon being scored; on a 40-year view it may well be true, and that residual is most of the 18. WINS is undefined — against what counterfactual, on what measure, and for whom. The base rate kills it on timing: electrification took roughly 40 years from commercial availability to measured productivity payoff (David 1990), IT roughly 25 years to the 1995-2004 TFP blip which then faded after about 9 years, so the frequency of a general-purpose technology adding >= 0.5pp to TFP growth within 11 years of commercial diffusion is about 0-1 of 4. The base rate of 'technology will offset demography' claims resolving true is the sharpest cut: Japan has led the world in industrial robot density for 30 years and averaged ~0.8%/yr real growth since 1991; Germany ran Industrie 4.0 through 2005-2025 at ~1.3%. Neither offset arrived. Against the locked -1.1 pp/yr global aging drag (-2.7 pp/yr in China) and the arithmetic that raises the Baumol-heavy, zero-productivity-growth care share of employment, the base-rate outcome by 2036 is that the offset partially cushions and does not win.

key_drivers: The monotone weight-times-growth arithmetic of the OECD+China aggregate: 5-year averages fell from ~4.3% (2010-14) to ~3.6% (2015-19) to ~2.54% (2020-24), roughly 1pp per decade for three decades, driven by China's PPP weight rising while its growth converges. Extrapolating that mechanical trend, not any AI mechanism, is what puts my CQ3 P50 at 1.95% and collapses CQ6-A to 15 against a ~90% unconditional historical base rate.

A 25-year OECD record of care-sector shortages NOT clearing through wages: OECD Beyond Applause finds LTC workers earn below-average wages compared with similar workers despite shortages documented since the late 1990s, because care pay is fiscally administered and Who Cares? requires +60% LTC workers by 2040 (13.5M) against near-zero sectoral productivity. This is the single biggest suppressor of CQ1's second conjunct and of hypothesis plank (a).

Stock-flow and credentialing arithmetic: a measured cross-occupational reallocation elasticity of ~0.05-0.10 into health/social care from displaced-worker reference classes (US manufacturing 1999-2011, UK coalfields 1984-94), a 1-4 year licensing queue, ~6-8% of new RN licensees aged 40+, an ~85-90% female care workforce versus a ~55-60% male displaced pool, and nursing-assistant injury rates ~3x the all-worker rate.

Unprecedentedness of the CQ1 unemployment conjunct: the OECD total-area harmonised rate never averaged <= 5.5% over any 5-year window in the 1999-2016 FRED series (6.2% in 2000, ~8.3% in 2010, 6.3% in 2016), so the question asks a record-low state to persist 6-10 more years against a ~50-55% per-window recession base rate, with the shrinking-labour-force denominator as the only mechanical offset.

Real-yield and bond-vol regime persistence versus mean reversion: a G7 GDP-weighted start of ~1.9% (derived from the locked 2.60% US TIPS print), decade averages spanning -1% (1970s) to +5% (1980s) to +0.3% (2010s), and only a ~30-35% frequency of a 5-year average landing within +/-50bp of its starting level — which forces wide CQ4 bands rather than a confident fiscal-dominance call. MOVE's long-run mean of ~93.6 since 1988 (contested start date) similarly makes the >= 105 threshold an above-mean call, capping CQ5.

The opposite-signed Indian/Philippine legs and their asymmetric base rates: ~0 of 3 'automation destroys offshoring' claims resolved true within a decade, while OECD migrant-care absorption is policy-constrained (foreign-born share of OECD nurses only ~14% -> ~16% over 2010-2020 despite shortages), so the virtual leg's counterfactual loss (-$90B to -$160B/yr for India, -300-550k Philippine jobs) dwarfs the physical leg's gain (~$10-25B/yr combined) without producing an absolute collapse.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD Earnings/Health at a Glance data show the OECD-average real hourly wage of personal-care and LTC workers rising >= 12% cumulatively ABOVE the whole-economy average between 2025 and 2030, reversing the Beyond Applause below-average finding.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Directly falsifies my central claim that administered care wages cannot clear without a fiscal transfer 2A says is strained. CQ1's wage-divergence conjunct moves from 0.20 to ~0.40 and CQ1 from 12 to ~25-28; hypothesis plank (a) moves from 5 to ~20; CQ6-C gains ~3pp from B on the Baumol-cost channel.

falsification_signposts.signpost: In any OECD country-year, the share of new RN or LPN licensees aged 40+ exceeds 15% (versus a historical ~6-8%), or a national statistical agency publishes a flow showing >= 10% of workers exiting ISIC J/K/M entering ISIC Q within three years.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies the stock-flow mismatch and the ~0.05-0.10 cross-elasticity that drive my low CQ1 and my 5 on plank (a). Plank (a) moves to ~25-30, CQ1's second conjunct to ~0.32, CQ1 to ~16-18, and CQ3's P50 rises ~0.15pp because the care supply wall is the main non-AI constraint in my growth arithmetic.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Philippine BPO headcount (IBPAP/PSA) prints a year-over-year decline >= 5% in any single year, OR Indian IT-BPM export revenue (NASSCOM, nominal USD) declines in two consecutive years.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Breaks the ~0-of-3 base rate on which I rest my 14 for plank (b). Plank (b) moves from 14 to ~35-40, the virtual leg's loss moves to the upper end (-$160B/yr India, -550k Philippine jobs), and because the displaced pool widens, my J/K/M-side compression assumption strengthens: CQ1's wage conjunct falls further to ~0.15 and CQ1 to ~9.

falsification_signposts.signpost: The OECD-38 harmonised unemployment rate prints no monthly value above 5.5% in any month from Jan 2027 through Dec 2030, and the 2027-2030 average is <= 5.2%.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Shows my ~50-55% per-window recession discount is too heavy and that the shrinking-labour-force denominator dominates. CQ1 conjunct A moves from 0.40 to ~0.65 and CQ1 from 12 to ~20; CQ3's P10 rises from 1.0 to ~1.3; CQ6-D falls ~4pp into B.

falsification_signposts.signpost: The ICE BofA MOVE index averages >= 110 for both calendar 2028 and calendar 2029 while the G7 GDP-weighted 10y real yield averages >= 2.75% over the same two years.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my mean-reversion-and-repression anchor on CQ4 and my below-mean read of MOVE. CQ4 P50 moves from 2.0% to ~2.6% with P90 to ~3.9%; CQ5 moves from 22 to ~40 (conjunct A to ~0.65); CQ6-C gains ~5pp and CQ6-A loses ~3pp on the debt-service arithmetic.

wave1.coupling_tension: The sharpest tension is between AI-Q2 and AI-Q1, and endogenising demographics widens rather than closes it. Once 2A's old-age ratio (31% -> 39-41%) and China's -60M are endogenous, they act as a labour-cost DEMAND PULL for adoption, and the historical base rate for adoption accelerating under labour scarcity is strong and one-directional (Japan, Korea and Germany led industrial robot density precisely as their workforces aged). AI-Q2's 21.3% for >= 50% firm-level adoption by 2036 is therefore too LOW once demographics are coupled — the comparable diffusion base rate (EU enterprise cloud adoption roughly 19% in 2014 to ~45% in 2023) says a quadrupling of a firm-adoption measure in twelve years is close to a coin flip, and labour scarcity adds to it. I would move AI-Q2 UP by roughly +7 to +10pp, to ~28-31%. But AI-Q1's 23.0% for a >= +0.50 pp/yr TFP lift must NOT rise with it, and if anything falls: the same demographic arithmetic mechanically shifts employment into the Baumol-zero-productivity care and physical sectors that OECD's Who Cares? sizes at +60%/13.5M LTC workers by 2040, so the marginal worker lands where measured productivity growth is near zero, and the licensing/reservation-wage/injury frictions in my effort mean the reallocation happens through non-employment and output forgone rather than through a smooth transfer. Coupling therefore drives a WEDGE between adoption and measured TFP — adoption up, measured TFP flat-to-down — which is Hulten's ceiling arriving through demography rather than through anything about the technology. The direct consequence for 2B is that AI-Q6's standalone Transformative Breakout at 16.2% is too high once demographics are endogenous (I would put it nearer 10-12%) and the Hulten Ceiling cell too low. A second, smaller tension runs the other way on AI-Q4: endogenous dissaving retirees and the locked +1.0pp worse global r-g raise the financing cost of the buildout, and the outside view on announced capex supercycles is far harsher than 66% — UK railway mania 1845-50, US nuclear 1974-84 (roughly 120 of ~250 ordered plants cancelled), telecom/fibre 1999-2002 (the great majority of laid fibre dark), Japan 1986-91, and US shale 2014-20 (~$300B of write-downs) give something like 5 of 5 episodes impaired >= 20%, so AI-Q4 at 66% is LOW on base rate and I would put it at 78-84%. Note the one place my own numbers are in tension with a locked marginal rather than with 2B's framing: AI-Q5's 38.2% for a >= 3.5pp fall in J/K/M labour compensation share is hard to reconcile with my CQ1 wage conjunct at only 0.20, since both describe the same cognitive-sector compression — the resolution is that a falling J/K/M labour share is compatible with J/K/M real median wages still outpacing administered F+Q care wages, which is exactly the barbell that keeps CQ6-B as the residual mode at 54.

wave1.lens_self_description: I answered purely by arithmetic and physical decomposition — growth-accounting sums, stock-flow conversion rates, conjunct multiplication, and conditional algebraic bounds on quantities and shadow prices — which forbade me from using any base rate, historical frequency, or reference-class analogy as evidence (e.g. "N% of 10-year windows contain a 25% drawdown"); every probability below is built from a decomposed mechanism with stated units, and where a quantity had to be translated into income or asset terms I state the utilization, service-life, residual-value and discount-rate assumptions rather than asserting the arithmetic settles it.
wave1.cq1_reasoning: CONJUNCT A: OECD-38 harmonized unemployment averages <=5.5% over 2032-36. Additive decomposition from the ~5.0% 2025 level: (i) shrinking-denominator pull. OECD-38 working-age (20-64) headcount growth, PPP-weighted across members (US +0.1 x 0.43, JP -0.7 x 0.093, DE -0.5 x 0.07, KR -1.3 x 0.046, IT -0.6 x 0.04, MX +0.9 x 0.045, TR +0.6 x 0.055, rest) = -0.10%/yr; with participation +0.25%/yr from the locked healthy-aging capacity gain and hours/worker -0.2%/yr, net hours -0.05%/yr. A labour force contracting ~0.1%/yr against flat employment mechanically removes ~0.1 pp/yr, i.e. -0.7 pp by the window. (ii) AI stock-flow mismatch. J+K+M is ~14% of 610M OECD-38 employed = 85M; an AI-Q5-consistent 10% displacement over 11 yr = 8.5M (0.77M/yr), of which ~50% carry non-employment spells >2 yr: 0.14 x 0.10 x 0.50 = +0.56 pp. (iii) at least one OECD-wide downturn inside a 5-year averaging window at +1.5 pp for ~2 of 5 years = +0.6 pp. Sum: 5.0 - 0.7 + 0.56 + 0.6 = 5.46%, sitting on the threshold. The denominator term is the most mechanically reliable and a 5-year mean is forgiving, so MARGINAL A = 0.52. CONJUNCT B: F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >=10.0 pp cumulatively, 2025-36 = +0.87%/yr relative drift for 11 years. Demand side supports it: Q must add 0.145 x 610M - 0.115 x 610M = 18.3M workers (1.66M/yr) as 65+ rises ~27% and 80+ ~40%+. But three arithmetic facts kill the PRICE response. (1) Rationing substitutes for price: Q is 70-80% publicly financed and 2A locks net interest rising 2%->3% of GDP with global debt >100%, so the clearing transfer is not funded; the observable analogue is that OECD LTC vacancy rates of 10-20% through 2015-24 produced NO relative real care-wage gain — quantity rationing (waiting lists, acuity thresholds, informal family care) absorbed the excess demand instead. (2) The migration valve caps the OECD care wage: if OECD imports 25-40% of the 1.66M/yr need, that is 400-650k/yr of care and skilled-trade slots filled at origin wage plus a migration premium, which truncates the domestic bid. (3) SELECTION BIAS IN THE MEDIAN — the decisive point. AI exit is concentrated in the lower half of J+K+M, so the surviving J+K+M median hourly wage RISES by composition even as sectoral employment and compensation share fall. The measured J+K+M median is therefore a biased (upward) estimator of incumbent wage change, which raises the bar B must clear rather than lowering it; note AI-Q5's 38.2% is about the COMPENSATION SHARE of GVA, a different object, and a share can fall while the median rises because the denominator is inflated by hyperscaler rents booked in ISIC J. To actually clear by price you would need, at an occupational own-wage supply elasticity of 0.6-1.0 for the marginal entrant, a relative wage rise of 26%/0.8 = ~32% — i.e. the required number is 3x the question's threshold, which is exactly why the system rations instead. MARGINAL B = 0.18. CORRELATION: mildly positive (+0.15) — tight labour markets both suppress unemployment and bid scarce-sector wages — but partly self-cancelling, because the configuration most favourable to B (hot care bidding) arrives with the AI displacement that damages A. P(B|A) = 0.18 x 1.15 = 0.21. MULTIPLICATION: 0.52 x 0.21 = 0.109 -> 11. (Simulation refused for CQ1 per adapter: "not representable - no unemployment, no ISIC sectors, no sectoral median wage". No figure above comes from the model.)
wave1.cq2_reasoning: CONJUNCT A: GDP-weighted OECD-38 core averages >=2.50%/yr over 2027-36. Additive build off a 2.00% target anchor, each term in pp/yr: +0.20 care/construction Baumol relative-price term (F+Q services and housing-maintenance are ~13-15% of the core basket; a 1.5 pp relative-price wedge x 0.14 = 0.21); +0.25 fiscal-dominance tolerance as the net interest claim goes 2%->3% of GDP (the realized historical tolerance band is 0.2-0.5 pp of target overshoot under that kind of interest burden); +0.25 non-tradable labour scarcity (labour supply -0.1%/yr against in-person service demand +1.5%/yr pushes service ULC ~0.4 pp above the 2%-consistent path, x the ~0.6 service weight); +0.08 grid/power pass-through (the 635 TWh OECD+China datacenter increment implied by AI-Q3 P50 raises industrial/retail power, ~3% of core directly and indirectly); -0.09 AI deflation in tradable services (if AI cuts the price of the ~6% of the basket that is outsourceable back-office/support by 15% over 10 yr); -0.15 imported goods deflation from Chinese excess capacity, which is the SAME object as conjunct B. Sum = 2.54%. Over a 10-year mean, sigma ~0.35, so P(>=2.50) = ~0.55. MARGINAL A = 0.55. CONJUNCT B: China headline CPI averages <1.50%/yr over 2027-36. Decomposition: start point 0.0-0.3% (2024-26 run rate). Structural suppressors are quantified in 2A: worker/retiree falls 4.4->2.8 and pension subsidies already absorb 10.1% of fiscal expenditure, so the pre-retirement cohort faces an underfunded system and raises precautionary saving (a direct demand suppressor), on top of property deleveraging and manufacturing excess capacity. Arithmetic test: a linear path from 0.3% in 2027 to 2.0% in 2036 gives a 10-yr mean of 1.15%; reaching a 1.50% mean requires hitting target well before 2033, i.e. a decisive reflation (large hukou/safety-net transfer, or RMB depreciation importing inflation, or a food shock). MARGINAL B = 0.66. CORRELATION: NEGATIVE, rho ~ -0.20, and this is the structural heart of the conjunction. The -0.15 pp term I used in conjunct A IS Chinese exported deflation; the mechanism that satisfies B (Chinese demand deficiency) mechanically pushes OECD core DOWN, while a world of global cost-push (energy, fragmentation, commodities) that lifts OECD core to 2.5%+ would also lift Chinese CPI toward 1.5%+. The question asks for a divergence, and the divergence is partly self-undermining. P(B|A) = 0.66 x 0.85 = 0.56. MULTIPLICATION: 0.55 x 0.56 = 0.308 -> 31. The conjunction discount here is modest in size but correctly signed: the naive product of the two "obvious" marginals (both individually more-likely-than-not for B) is pulled down by the negative dependence, not up. (Simulation refused for CQ2 per adapter: "not representable - the model has no price level". The model is entirely real; no number above comes from it.)
wave1.cq3_reasoning: PPP WEIGHT RECONCILIATION (explicit, as required). OECD-38 PPP GDP ~$72T and China ~$41T in 2025 (combined ~$113T), so China's share is ~0.36; with China compounding ~3.5%/yr vs OECD ~1.6%/yr to 2031 the share drifts to ~0.385. I use w_China = 0.38, w_OECD = 0.62 for 2032-36. The adapter's own weights (0.629 / 0.371 at 2031) agree to within 1 pp despite a different regional partition, so the weighting is not where the model and I diverge. CHINA LEG AND THE -2.7 pp ARITHMETIC. w_China x locked China aging drag = 0.38 x (-2.7) = -1.03 pp of coupled growth. That single term is larger in absolute value than every AI channel in this payload combined, and it is the answer's dominant arithmetic. Bottom-up China 2032-36: labour -0.63 pp (working-age 20-64 contracting ~1.15%/yr as the 1962-68 cohorts cross 65 against small replacement cohorts; population -60M over 2026-35 and worker/retiree 4.4->2.8 per 2A; labour share 0.55 x -1.15); capital deepening +2.00 pp (K/Y ~3.2, I/Y falling from ~40% as residential investment stays ~30% below its 2021 peak, K growth decelerating to 4.5-5.0%/yr, alpha ~0.45); TFP +1.10 pp (~0.7 baseline plus ~0.4 AI); property/credit/pension-claim drag -0.50 pp (the 2.9T RMB / 10.1%-of-expenditure subsidy is a direct claim on fiscal capacity for productive complements). Sum = +1.97%/yr. CROSS-CHECK: a frictionless China counterfactual of ~4.7%/yr less the locked -2.7 pp = 2.0%. The two routes agree, so I adopt China = 2.0%/yr. OECD-38 LEG. Hours -0.05%/yr (headcount -0.10, participation +0.25 from the locked healthy-aging capacity gain, hours/worker -0.20). Labour quality/composition +0.15 pp. Baseline capital deepening +0.35 pp. INCREMENTAL AI/GRID CAPITAL DEEPENING +0.06 pp — and this is the quietest important number here: AI-Q3 P50 implies a 635 TWh increment over 2024, which at 70% IT utilization is ~104 GW of IT load, at $30-35M/MW all-in is ~$3.2-3.6T cumulative, ~$270-300B/yr net plus a 3-5 yr GPU replacement cycle giving ~$400-500B/yr gross, plus ~$250B/yr of grid, i.e. ~0.55 pp of extra I/Y on a ~$130T PPP base; at K/Y = 3.0 that lifts K growth by 0.55/3.0 = 0.18%/yr and at alpha = 0.35 contributes only +0.06 pp/yr to GDP growth. A capex boom enormous in dollars is near-trivial in growth-accounting terms because the existing capital stock is vast, alpha is a third, and short GPU service lives mean most gross spend is replacement rather than deepening. TFP +0.60 pp = 0.30 baseline (2015-22) plus +0.304 AI, where the AI term is taken from AI-Q6's own regime mix: 0.162 x 0.70 + 0.472 x 0.35 + 0.365 x 0.07 = +0.304 pp. OECD pre-coupling = 1.11%/yr. COUPLING ADJUSTMENTS (both directions, as the brief demands): -0.12 fiscal consolidation (~1% of GDP over the window at a 0.6 multiplier, forced by the 2%->3% net interest claim); -0.02 higher hurdle rate on long-duration grid/datacenter projects; -0.03 Baumol composition (moving 3 pp of hours from a 1.0%-productivity-growth economy into a ~0.15% care sector: 0.03 x 0.85); +0.05 automation demand-pull from labour scarcity. OECD coupled = 0.99%/yr. INDEPENDENT CHECK AGAINST 2A: the locked prior gives OECD per-capita growth at 0.6%/yr absent productivity offsets; with OECD-38 population +0.15%/yr that is 0.75%/yr aggregate, plus my +0.30 pp AI offset = 1.05%/yr. My bottom-up 0.99% reproduces the locked marginal to within 6 bp, so the OECD leg is 2A-consistent by construction. ASSEMBLY: 0.62 x 0.99 + 0.38 x 1.97 = 0.61 + 0.75 = 1.37%/yr; I round P50 to 1.5%/yr to allow for the capital-deepening term being my least-anchored estimate on both legs. INTERVAL: P10 0.7 (coupled AI-capex bust resolving AI-Q4 in 2027-32 leaving 2032-36 as the digestion window, -0.4 pp, plus a China property/pension accident, -0.4 pp); P90 2.5 (AI-Q6 Transformative Breakout at 16.2% mass adding +0.4 pp to the coupled TFP term, plus China capital deepening at the top of its range). MODEL DISAGREEMENT (rule 3 — the payload). The adapter returns coupled 2032-36 growth of 2.95% (baseline), 2.95% (central-path), 3.03% (ai-energy-boom), 2.30% (tech-stagnation), 2.29% (tech-plateau), 1.67% (debt-populism), 2.62% (ssp3-70), 3.68% (tech-breakthrough), 3.90% (net-zero). My 1.5% sits BELOW the model's entire ordinary range and only debt-populism (1.67%) comes near it. THE EXPLANATION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CALIBRATIONAL, and it has a clean internal diagnostic. (a) The model's production function is Ayres-Warr with gamma = 0.55 on useful energy — CLAUDE.md documents this as a deliberate heterodox choice against a mainstream cost-share gamma of 0.05-0.08 — so growth there is overwhelmingly a useful-energy-and-efficiency story in which labour enters only through beta. The documented dominant GDP dial is serviceEfficiencyGrowth (~1.8x per plausible range), i.e. a second-law efficiency parameter, not a demographic outcome. (b) THE DIAGNOSTIC: the adapter discloses the model's demographic path tracks the UN WPP LOW variant (~18% below medium by 2100), which should bias its labour force and growth DOWN relative to 2A's baseline. That it nonetheless prints 2.95% tells you aging is nearly irrelevant to this model by construction — a low-fertility labour path coexisting with ~3% growth is proof that the energy/efficiency channel is swamping the labour channel, not evidence that growth will be high. Every bound I read off it is therefore LOW-FERTILITY-CONDITIONAL and simultaneously labour-insensitive. (c) The model has no care sector, no ISIC split, no Baumol composition term, no licensing constraint, no fiscal crowding-out of public complements, and no China pension-subsidy claim — i.e. none of the five mechanisms that produce my -1.03 pp China term and my -0.17 pp of OECD coupling drag. (d) China at 3.81%/yr (2.85% in tech-stagnation, 5.29% in net-zero) simply does not implement the locked -2.7 pp/yr aging drag; its 3-cohort fertility-convergence demographics feed a high-alpha capital-deepening engine with no property deleveraging and no fiscal claim. (e) Datacenter load: baseline world 1,884 TWh in 2036 vs the locked AI-Q3 P90 of 1,574 TWh for OECD-38+China. Since world is a SUPERSET, 1,884 world is roughly 1,200-1,300 for OECD+China at a 60-70% share, i.e. comfortably INSIDE the locked distribution and not actually a contradiction in baseline. The real conflict is ai-energy-boom at 4,180 TWh world (~2,700 OECD+China), far above the locked P90 — which identifies what the locked AI-Q3 prior implicitly assumes: a willingness-to-pay ceiling on the electricity-bill share of GDP. Fermi check of that equivalence: 1,573.8 TWh x $80/MWh = $126B/yr against ~$130T PPP = 0.097% of GDP, so AI-Q3's P90 is approximately a 0.10%-of-GDP power-bill ceiling, about 2x the model's own 0.05% default. The locked prior and the model agree on the MECHANISM (price-capped load) and differ only on the ceiling's level. (f) USABLE CONDITIONAL BOUND I DO TAKE from the model, with its translation published: robotsPer1000 (world, all sectors) reaches 3.92 in baseline, 6.09 in automation-boom, 6.63 in ai-energy-boom by 2036; divided by 1000 that is 0.39-0.66% of workers' worth of installed robot stock, and physical care robots are a small subset of that. TRANSLATION: this bounds the "robots fill the elder-care gap" channel at under ~0.7% of the labour force by 2036 even under the model's most aggressive automation scenario, against a care need of 18.3M workers (3.0% of OECD-38 employment). That channel is arithmetically closed inside the resolution horizon — low-fertility-conditional, and conditional on the model's endogenous marginal-value-versus-marginal-cost deployment rule rather than on any hard saturation cap. I adopt the model's BOUND on robots and reject its growth level.
wave1.cq4_reasoning: DECOMPOSITION r = r* + real term premium - financial-repression wedge, all in pp, G7 GDP-weighted. r* BUILD: base 1.15 (post-2022 HLW-style range 0.8-1.5). + 0.10 life-cycle dissaving: the old-age ratio rises 9 pp (31%->40%); at a 2-4 bp-per-pp elasticity that is +18 to +36 bp gross, but 2A explicitly states the frictionless r* EASES (longevity raises target wealth and extends horizons) and resolves the net as (r-g) worsening by +1.0 pp driven mostly by g falling, so the demographic term on r itself is small and I keep only +10 bp. + 0.40 public dissaving: G7 debt/GDP rising ~15 pp by 2033 (2A: >100% global by 2029, 142% US and 127% China by 2031) at 2-4 bp per 10 pp. + 0.20 eroding sovereign convenience yield, named directly in 2A as a shrinking safe-asset premium. + 0.20 AI/grid capex demand for savings: the ~0.55 pp of GDP increment computed in CQ3, which in a loanable-funds frame with saving elasticity ~0.3 and investment elasticity ~1.0 per pp gives 0.55/1.3 = +42 bp mechanically, which I HALVE to +20 bp because AI-Q4 at 66% says much of that demand is impaired or cancelled before 2032-36 — if the bust lands the sign of this term flips negative. - 0.15 precautionary saving (AI job insecurity in J/K/M; recycled East Asian and Chinese surplus saving from the same aging block). - 0.15 cognitive-labour compression: the BIS Box C channel — capital-concentrated income carries a higher saving propensity, so AI-Q5-style compression is a DEMAND SHORTFALL and therefore a negative for r*, which is the most-missed sign in this question. r* = 1.75. REAL TERM PREMIUM +0.75 (range +0.25 to +1.50): duration supply rising with the deficit, 3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk at 117% of GDP (+2.4 pp under a 20% AI-led equity shock), and 2A's levered hedge-fund basis-trade absorption meaning the marginal duration buyer is the relative-value complex, which is the same object CQ5 prices. FINANCIAL-REPRESSION WEDGE -0.40, GDP-weighted over repression capacity (JP, euro area high via LDI/Solvency II/bank LCR and central-bank reinvestment; US low): weights 0.50 US / 0.11 JP / 0.10 DE / 0.08 UK / 0.08 FR / 0.07 IT / 0.06 CA. r = 1.75 + 0.75 - 0.40 = 2.10%. CRITICAL LEVEL CHECK — the question asks for a G7 GDP-WEIGHTED yield, and the locked 2.60% TIPS print is a US-ONLY number. Applying my weights to current 10y real levels (US 2.60, JP -0.20, DE 0.70, UK 1.30, FR 0.60, IT 1.50, CA 1.80) gives 1.71% TODAY, not 2.60%. A panelist who anchors on 2.60% has mis-specified the object by ~90 bp. My 2.10% is therefore +40 bp above today's weighted level, decomposed as: Japanese normalization alone (-0.20 -> +0.80) contributes 0.11 x 1.00 = +11 bp, debt and convenience-yield terms +60 bp, repression -40 bp, remainder in the term premium. INTERVAL: P10 1.1 (repression wedge widens to -1.00 pp under arriving fiscal dominance plus a term premium at +0.25 and the AI-capex-bust branch flipping the capex term negative); P90 3.1 (no repression, term premium +1.50, convenience yield erodes faster). MODEL USE — REFUSED AS A POINT ESTIMATE, PUBLISHED AS DIRECTION ONLY. The adapter self-reports: "NOT IDENTIFIED (CQ4): capital.interestRate is an economy-wide REAL interest rate... no 10-year sovereign benchmark, no term premium (no termPremium anywhere in src/), and no inflation swap or breakeven." Its readings are 6.09% (baseline), 6.09% (central-path), 6.12% (ai-energy-boom), 5.99% (tech-stagnation), 5.99% (tech-plateau), 6.96% (debt-populism), 6.08% (ssp3-70), 6.12% (net-zero), 6.18% (tech-breakthrough), with debt risk premia of 1.13-2.50 pp. TRANSLATION I REFUSE TO MAKE: 6.09% is a marginal product of capital, and the ~400 bp gap to my 2.10% sovereign yield is an equity/credit risk premium plus a convenience yield, neither of which exists in the model. THE DIRECTIONAL CONTENT I DO USE: across its scenarios the model's rate moves +0.87 pp for a fiscal/political-stress scenario (debt-populism 6.96 vs baseline 6.09, with the debt risk premium moving +1.08 pp to 2.50) but only +0.09 pp for the strongest technology scenario (tech-breakthrough 6.18, with the premium FALLING 0.22 pp). Even inside a model built around an energy-technology engine, the fiscal leg moves the cost of capital roughly 4-10x more than the technology regime does. That supports placing my CQ4 variance in the repression and term-premium terms rather than in r*-from-aging, and it is low-fertility-conditional like every other reading.
wave1.cq5_reasoning: CONJUNCT A: ICE BofA MOVE averages >=105 over 2027-36. MOVE is 1-month implied Treasury yield vol in annualized bp, so it scales roughly as k x (nominal yield level) x (policy-path dispersion). LEVEL ARITHMETIC: at my CQ4 P50 of 2.1% real the G7-weighted nominal 10y is ~4.3-4.7%; scaling the 2015-19 MOVE mean of ~65 by 4.5/2.5 = 1.8 gives ~117. But the observed 2024-26 run-rate of ~85-100 at comparable yields shows k has FALLEN (QT completed, policy path less dispersed), so the level term alone overstates. Raising k back requires the 2A plumbing terms: eroding convenience yields, $650B of AI-related debt issuance against $300B of equity creating correlated repricing risk, and basis-trade leverage that amplifies yield vol in a deleveraging. Central 10-yr mean 100-105, so MARGINAL A = 0.48. CONJUNCT B: at least one episode in 2027-36 with MSCI World -25% peak-to-trough WHILE G7 weighted 10y nominal fails to fall 50 bp (or rises 25 bp) in the drawdown window. Split into B1 (a >=25% drawdown occurs) and B2 (it is a bonds-do-not-hedge episode). B1 BY MECHANISM, NOT FREQUENCY: AI-related names are ~35-40% of MSCI World capitalization; 2A locks ~$1.4T of circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on a ~$300B equity base (~2.2x leverage on that base) and AI-Q4 at 66% for >=20% impairment or revenue <0.5x compute D&A for 2 consecutive years. A 50% derating of that bloc alone is -17 to -20% on the index, and the earnings read-through to the remainder closes the gap to -25%. P(B1 | AI-Q4 resolves) = 0.62 (orderly multi-year digestion without a single 25% index drawdown is genuinely possible); P(B1 | not AI-Q4) = 0.25. 0.66 x 0.62 + 0.34 x 0.25 = 0.49, lifted to 0.58 for non-AI triggers that 2A separately names (sovereign Debt-at-Risk at 117% of GDP P95, a China property/pension accident, a Japan or UK duration accident). B2 CONDITIONAL ON B1, BY SHOCK TYPE — and here my own two legs pull against each other, which is the real reason this conjunction is low. If the drawdown IS the AI-capex bust, that is DISINFLATIONARY and bonds rally hard, so B2 fails: branch weight 0.45, P(B2) = 0.10. Fiscal/inflation/supply shock: weight 0.25, P(B2) = 0.90. Hybrid where the window contains both a yield-up shock and a later rally: weight 0.20, P(B2) = 0.50. Geopolitical/energy: weight 0.10, P(B2) = 0.60. P(B2|B1) = 0.045 + 0.225 + 0.100 + 0.060 = 0.43. P(B) = 0.58 x 0.43 = 0.25. CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho ~ +0.45, because one regime (fiscal dominance plus duration instability plus eroded convenience yield) generates both a high MOVE mean and a non-hedging bond leg. P(B|A) = 0.25 x 1.5 = 0.37. MULTIPLICATION: 0.48 x 0.37 = 0.178 -> 18. The structural point the conjunction forces: the single most likely generator of a >=25% equity drawdown in this window (the AI capex bust, 66% on AI-Q4) is the generator LEAST likely to satisfy the bond leg, because a capex bust is deflationary. The question is quietly asking for two things from opposite shock families. (Simulation refused for CQ5 per adapter: "not representable - no asset prices, no volatility index". No number above comes from the model.)
wave1.cq6_reasoning: I need the joint of (CQ3 growth, GDP-weighted OECD-38 core inflation over 2032-36) and must apply the lexical lock strictly.
