Step 3, D requires g < 1.7% AND core < 2.0%: P(core < 2.0) = 0.14 unconditionally, lifted to 0.24 conditional on g < 1.7 because that cell is over-populated by the capex-bust/BIS-demand-shortfall branch; 0.62 x 0.24 = 0.149 -> D = 15. Step 4, B is the residual: 100 - 7 - 28 - 15 = 50. SUM = 100. CONSISTENCY CHECK I PERFORMED, EXPLICITLY. (i) Against my own CQ3: P50 = 1.5% is far below A's 2.6% trigger, so A receives only right-tail mass; 7 points is the P(g >= 2.6) implied by my own stated P90 of 2.5, and putting any substantial mass on A would contradict my CQ3 — the lock's worked example (P50 of 2.1% forbidding most mass on A) applies to me a fortiori at 1.5%. (ii) Against my own CQ2: my CQ2 conjunct-A marginal of 0.55 for OECD core >=2.50% over 2027-36 maps, on the rising profile, to a 2032-36 central of 2.55%, which places 36% above C's 2.7% trigger; multiplied by P(g<2.0) = 0.78 that yields 28 for C, so C is derived from my CQ2 rather than asserted. If I had instead used CQ2's unconditional 10-yr 2.54% with its tighter sigma 0.35, P(core>=2.7) would be 0.33 and C would be 26 — within rounding, so the answer is not sensitive to that choice. (iii) D's 15 is consistent with AI-Q4 at 66%: D needs not just the impairment event but for its deflationary digestion to still be suppressing both growth and inflation in 2032-36 rather than in 2028-31, which is roughly a one-in-four conditional. A FINDING ABOUT THE TAXONOMY, which the lock forces into the open: my modal outcome is B at 50 points, but it lands in B as the RESIDUAL at a growth rate of ~1.5%/yr, BELOW B's own stated 1.7-2.5% band, routed there because inflation sits between 2.0% and 2.7% and so triggers neither C nor D. Substantively that is still a bifurcated barbell — physical/care scarcity and hyperscaler rents coexisting with white-collar compression and steep real term premia, exactly B's qualitative description — but anyone reading B as "growth 1.7-2.5%" will misread my distribution. Half my probability mass sits in a cell whose label implies ~1 pp more growth than I forecast.

hypothesis_critique.a: The failure word is SMOOTHLY, and it fails by an order of magnitude, not a margin. Flow arithmetic: OECD-38 Q employment must go from 0.115 x 610M = 70M to 0.145 x 610M = 89M, i.e. +18.3M over 11 years = 1.66M/yr net. The displaced supply: J+K+M is 0.14 x 610M = 85M, an AI-Q5-consistent 10% displacement over 11 years is 8.5M = 0.77M/yr. The conversion rate is where SMOOTHLY dies, and each haircut is separately identifiable: median displaced age ~42-45 against a straight-line depreciation over expected time in the workforce that leaves too few years to amortize retraining; licensing queue length (RN 2-4 yr with clinical-placement slots, not instructors, as the binding capacity; LPN 1-2 yr; only the care-aide tier at 6-12 weeks is fast, and that is the tier whose wage cannot clear); gender composition (J+K+M ~45% female versus Q 77-87%, so the marginal entrant must cross an occupational-identity gap that historically needs a large premium); reservation-wage gap of ~1.6-1.9x between the J+K+M and Q medians; geographic immobility (care demand is where the 80+ live, in suburbs and small towns, while the displaced hold mortgages in high-cost metros); and physical strain, with nursing-aide injury rates ~3x the all-industry average, which is a compensating differential that must be PAID, not exhorted. Net ~15% convertible: 0.77M x 0.15 = 0.12M/yr against a 1.66M/yr need = 7% coverage. A plank that supplies 7% of a flow is not describing a smooth mechanism; it is describing a rounding error. The direction is right and the magnitude is wrong by ~14x. I also checked the robot substitute independently and it is closed: the simulation's world robots-per-1000 reaches only 3.92-6.63 by 2036 even in automation-boom and ai-energy-boom, i.e. under 0.7% of workers' worth of installed stock against a 3.0%-of-employment care need (low-fertility-conditional, and conditional on the model's endogenous deployment rule).
hypothesis_critique.b: Two words fail, BLOCKS and SEVERELY, and I believe the plank has the SIGN of the net effect wrong, not merely the magnitude. BLOCKS is false on the virtual leg for India in particular. Philippine IT-BPM: ~1.7M+ workers and ~$38-40B of revenue (8-9% of GDP), of which the AI-exposed slice (voice, transactional BPO, L1 support) is ~35-45% of headcount; a 30% compression of that slice by 2036 is 1.7M x 0.40 x 0.30 = ~204k jobs and ~$4-5B, about 1% of GDP — household-level severe in Metro Manila and Cebu, macro-level material but not severe. India IT-BPM exports at the ~$280B scale with ~25-30% exposed = ~$78B at risk; a 25% compression is -$20B (~0.5% of GDP), against which Indian firms and GCCs are themselves SELLERS of AI delivery capacity, plausibly +$15-25B. India's net virtual leg is neutral to positive, so BLOCKS describes India as a victim of a market in which it is a producer. The PHYSICAL leg, which the plank omits entirely, runs the other way and I quantify it with the translation stated: OECD needs 1.66M/yr net Q additions and will import 25-40% = 400-650k/yr of care and skilled-trade slots (HV linemen and electricians for the grid and datacenter build are a named bottleneck in their own right); India plus the Philippines plausibly capture 30-40% = 150-250k/yr. Remittance arithmetic, assuming a $45-70k OECD nursing wage, an $8-14k/yr remittance propensity, cohort persistence over the window and no change in transfer costs: ~100k/yr of incremental Philippine physical migrants x $11k = ~$1.1B/yr per cohort year, cumulating to a ~$11B/yr run-rate by 2036 on top of the existing ~$38-40B (8.5% of GDP), i.e. a 25-30% increase, plus the GCC healthcare-build channel. The physical gain beats the virtual loss by roughly 2:1 in GDP terms for the Philippines. SEVERELY therefore fails on the net, though the plank is right about something it does not say: the distributional and brain-drain costs are real, because the Philippines exports precisely the nurses its own rising old-age ratio needs, and a GDP-positive net can sit on top of a worse domestic care system.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failure is in THEN FALLS — the plank gets the profile inverted, not the level. Every term in my CQ2 inflation build that pushes OECD core UP strengthens monotonically into the 2030s, because each is driven by the old-age ratio itself going 31% -> 40%: the care and construction Baumol relative-price wedge (+0.20 pp), non-tradable labour scarcity as the workforce contracts (+0.25 pp), and fiscal tolerance as the net interest claim goes 2% -> 3% of GDP (+0.25 pp). Every term that pushes DOWN is front-loaded: Chinese goods deflation from current excess capacity (-0.15 pp) and AI compression of tradable back-office services (-0.09 pp), both of which are largest now and decay as capacity clears and the compression completes. So my profile RISES, ~2.4% over 2027-31 to ~2.55-2.65% over 2032-36, which is why my CQ6 puts 28 points on the C regime and only 15 on D. I score this 15 rather than lower for one specific reason: the AI-Q4 capex bust at 66% is a mechanism that WOULD produce exactly the plank's shape — hot through the late 2020s, then a deflationary digestion with excess capacity and a BIS-style labour-income demand deficit in the 2030s. That is my D branch, and 15 is close to the weight I place on it, so the plank is not wrong in mechanism, only in treating a one-in-six-to-one-in-seven branch as the central path.
hypothesis_critique.d: Two words fail. EVENTUALLY is the load-bearing one and it is a defect of form, not of fact: it places the claim outside any resolution horizon and therefore makes the plank unfalsifiable, which is why no honest high score is available regardless of whether AI eventually does outrun population decline. WINS is undefined — wins against what counterfactual, measured in levels or growth rates, per capita or aggregate? Within the actual window the arithmetic is one-sided and I can state the ratio: the AI-attributable TFP lift implied by AI-Q6's own regime mix is 0.162 x 0.70 + 0.472 x 0.35 + 0.365 x 0.07 = +0.304 pp/yr PPP-weighted, against a demographic drag of 0.38 x (-2.7) = -1.03 pp from China's locked aging term plus -0.25 to -0.40 pp from OECD working-age contraction and its Baumol composition shift. The drag beats the lift by roughly 4:1 through 2036. The deeper objection is the Chad Jones one, and it is the reason EXPONENTIAL does not save the plank either: if AI substitutes for labour in IDEA PRODUCTION the growth rate genuinely can rise, but if the binding input is a non-reproducible complement — licensed physically-present care hours, grid interconnection capacity, HV transformers, clinical placement slots, land — then output is capped by that input's QUANTITY and its shadow price, not by compute, and exponential growth in the abundant factor raises the scarce factor's shadow price instead of raising output. The plank assumes the bottleneck is cognition. My decomposition says it is licensure and interconnection queues, which are administrative, not technological, and do not respond to scaling.

key_drivers: China's PPP weight (0.38, reconciled against the adapter's 0.371 for 2031) multiplied by the locked -2.7 pp/yr aging drag = -1.03 pp of coupled growth. This single product is larger in absolute value than every AI channel in this payload combined and is the dominant arithmetic in CQ3, CQ6 and (via g in r-g) CQ4.

The stock-flow conversion rate from displaced ISIC J/K/M workers into licensed ISIC Q entrants: 0.77M/yr displaced x ~15% convertible = 0.12M/yr against a 1.66M/yr need, i.e. ~7% coverage. Set by licensing queue length (clinical placement slots, not instructors, are the binding capacity), displaced-worker age ~42-45, the 77-87% female composition of care work, a 1.6-1.9x reservation-wage gap, geographic immobility against housing costs, and injury rates ~3x the all-industry average as a differential that must be paid.

Whether the care shortfall clears by PRICE (a fiscal transfer that 2A says is already strained, with net interest going 2%->3% of GDP) or by QUANTITY RATIONING (waiting lists, acuity thresholds, informal family care). Price-clearing drives CQ1's conjunct B and the CQ6-C regime; rationing — which is what a decade of 10-20% OECD LTC vacancy rates with no relative real wage gain actually produced — drives CQ1 to 11 and puts the mass in CQ6-B.

The AI/grid capex-to-capital-deepening conversion rate: ~0.55 pp of GDP in incremental investment (104 GW of IT load at 70% utilization and $30-35M/MW, plus ~$250B/yr of grid) yields only +0.04 to +0.06 pp/yr of growth at K/Y = 3.0 and alpha = 0.35, before AI-Q4 impairments and before accounting for 3-5 year GPU lives making most gross spend replacement rather than deepening.

The physical-migration valve at 400-650k/yr of OECD care and skilled-trade slots. It is simultaneously what caps the OECD care wage (killing CQ1's conjunct B) and what flips the sign of the India/Philippines net spillover (killing hypothesis plank b). The same quantity resolves two questions in opposite directions, so a forecaster who moves one without the other is internally inconsistent.

In CQ4, the financial-repression wedge (-0.40 pp G7-weighted, with a -1.00 to 0.00 range set by Japanese and euro-area LDI/Solvency II/LCR capacity against low US capacity) versus the real term premium (+0.75 pp, range +0.25 to +1.50). These two terms together span ~2 pp and dominate the ~+0.10 pp that endogenous aging contributes to r* directly — the simulation's own cross-scenario spread agrees directionally, moving its rate +0.87 pp for fiscal/political stress versus +0.09 pp for the strongest technology regime.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD Health at a Glance and national LTC workforce statistics show OECD-38 health-and-social-work (ISIC Q) employment growing >=2.5%/yr over 2026-2029 (versus the ~1.5-1.8%/yr my rationing view implies) WITH reported LTC vacancy rates falling below 8% in at least five of the G7 plus Korea.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My central claim — that the care bottleneck clears by quantity rationing rather than by price, and that the J/K/M-to-Q conversion rate is ~7% of the needed flow — is wrong. The queue is clearing, so hypothesis plank (a) is far better than 7 (move it to 35-45). CQ1 rises 6-9 pp (to ~18-20, since both conjuncts benefit: a clearing care sector absorbs displaced workers AND bids wages). Move 5-8 points from CQ6-C to CQ6-B and A, since the supply wall is the main C generator. Raise CQ3 P50 by about +0.15 pp to ~1.65%, via a smaller Baumol composition drag and fewer family caregivers withdrawing from the labour force.

falsification_signposts.signpost: US BLS and Eurostat sectoral median hourly earnings series show real median pay in ISIC F + Q outpacing ISIC J + K + M by >=4.5 percentage points cumulatively over 2025-2030 — i.e. on pace for the +10 pp the CQ1 conjunct needs by 2036 — with the gap widening rather than flat.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My conjunct-B marginal of 0.18 was too low, chiefly because my selection-bias argument (AI exit from the lower half of J/K/M mechanically raising that sector's measured median) was weaker than the scarcity bid. Raise the marginal to ~0.45, roughly doubling CQ1 to 22-25. Add 4-6 points to CQ6-C and take them from B, since a genuine care-wage spiral is the stagflationary-bottleneck generator. Raise my CQ2 conjunct-A marginal from 0.55 to ~0.68 (the Baumol term is running above my +0.20 pp), lifting CQ2 to ~38.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Philippine IT-BPM headcount (IBPAP annual reporting) falls below 1.4M (from ~1.7M+) AND Philippine total remittance inflows fail to exceed $48B/yr — i.e. the virtual leg contracts hard while the physical-migration and remittance channel does not expand to compensate.
falsification_signposts.by_when: End-2031 (on full-year 2031 BSP and IBPAP data).
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: The migration valve is NOT operating at the 400-650k/yr scale I assumed, and the net spillover sign I asserted is wrong. Raise hypothesis plank (b) from 12 to ~40, since SEVERELY and BLOCKS would then be close to right for the Philippines. Simultaneously — and this is the coupled consequence, not a separate one — a closed migration valve means OECD care wages are no longer capped from abroad, so CQ1's conjunct B gains (marginal 0.18 -> 0.30, CQ1 to ~16) and CQ6-C gains 4-5 points from B. Cut CQ3 P50 by about -0.05 pp on the lost OECD hours.

falsification_signposts.signpost: The G7 GDP-weighted 10-year sovereign real yield, constructed on my published weights (0.50 US / 0.11 JP / 0.10 DE / 0.08 UK / 0.08 FR / 0.07 IT / 0.06 CA) against 10y nominal minus 10y inflation swap, averages above 2.6% for any rolling twelve months, WITH Japan's 10y real above +1.0%.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: The financial-repression wedge is not binding and the term premium is at or above my high end. Raise CQ4 to P50 2.6-2.8% with P10/P90 about 1.8/3.6, and note this is the cleanest single test of my CQ4 because it discriminates the repression term from r* directly. Raise CQ5 by 6-8 pp (to ~25), since an unrepressed, high-term-premium duration market is precisely the regime in which bonds fail to hedge an equity drawdown and the MOVE mean clears 105. Shift 4-6 points from CQ6-B to CQ6-C. Cut CQ3 P50 by -0.1 pp on the higher hurdle rate applied to long-duration grid and datacenter capex.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-38 harmonized unemployment prints above 6.0% for four consecutive quarters at any point before end-2032 WHILE GDP-weighted OECD-38 core inflation stays above 2.5% over the same four quarters (the conjunction matters: unemployment alone would be an ordinary cycle).
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: The AI mismatch channel is materially larger than the +0.56 pp I computed, and the shrinking-labour-force pull of -0.7 pp is not offsetting it — i.e. displaced cognitive workers are neither re-absorbed nor retiring. Cut CQ1 to 4-6 (conjunct A's 0.52 collapses toward 0.15). Raise CQ6-C by 5 points, since simultaneous high unemployment and high core inflation IS the stagflationary-squeeze signature, taking those points from B. Cut CQ3 P50 to ~1.2%/yr. Raise hypothesis plank (c) only if the inflation leg then rolls over, which this signpost does not by itself establish.

wave1.coupling_tension: Four Section 2B marginals become internally inconsistent once demographics are endogenous, and the two central ones move in OPPOSITE directions, which is itself the finding. (1) AI-Q2 (firm adoption >=50% by 2036) at 21.3% is TOO LOW. Aging is a demand pull, not only a drag: a contracting working-age population (OECD hours -0.05%/yr net, China working-age -1.15%/yr) with a rising reservation wage is the most direct determinant of the firm-level automation business case — in the simulation's own formulation, marginal value equals payoff x labour share x GDP per worker, so a scarcer, dearer worker raises MV mechanically. Endogenous aging should move AI-Q2 UP by 4-8 pp, to ~26-29%. (2) AI-Q1 (PPP-weighted TFP lift >=+0.50 pp/yr) at 23.0% is TOO HIGH, for two separable reasons. First, composition: moving 3 pp of OECD hours into a care sector with ~0.15%/yr measured labour-productivity growth lowers aggregate measured TFP by 0.03-0.05 pp/yr, a pure accounting subtraction that the exogenous-demographics framing cannot see. Second, crowding out of the PUBLIC COMPLEMENTS that diffusion actually needs — grid interconnection, transformer capacity, clinical placement slots, licensure throughput, skills funding — by the fiscal facts locked in 2A (net interest 2%->3% of GDP, Chinese pension subsidies already 10.1% of fiscal expenditure and rising as worker/retiree goes 4.4->2.8). Endogenous aging should move AI-Q1 DOWN by 2-4 pp, to ~19-21%. THE CENTRAL TENSION IS THEREFORE A SCISSORS: more adoption, less measured TFP. Aging raises the number of firms using AI while lowering the economy-wide productivity those firms can register, because the binding input shifts from cognition (which AI supplies) to licensed physically-present hours and interconnection capacity (which it does not). That scissors is exactly the "Jagged Diffusion and Hyperscaler Rent Concentration" cell, so coupling should move AI-Q6 mass from BOTH tails into the middle cell — Transformative Breakout down 2-3 pp from 16.2%, Hulten Ceiling down 2-4 pp from 36.5%, Jagged Diffusion up 5-7 pp from 47.2%. (3) AI-Q5 (J/K/M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA falling >=3.5 pp) at 38.2% is TOO LOW, by 3-5 pp, and for a denominator reason that exogenous demographics hides: a shrinking cognitive-worker entry cohort does not rescue the SHARE, because the denominator is sectoral GVA and that GVA is being inflated by hyperscaler rents booked inside ISIC J. Fewer cognitive workers and larger J-sector rents both push the ratio down. (4) AI-Q4 (impairments) at 66.0% is close to right, but coupling raises the cost of capital — 2A's own starting point has $650B of debt against $300B of equity in the circular commitments, and my CQ4 build puts r* up ~55 bp from the public-dissaving and convenience-yield terms alone — which should add 2-4 pp, to ~68-70%. THE DEEPEST TENSION IS AT THE AGGREGATE, AND ITS DIRECTION IS UNAMBIGUOUS: AI-Q6 places 63.4% of mass on TFP lifts of >=+0.15 pp/yr, and taking its own regime midpoints gives an expected AI TFP contribution of +0.304 pp/yr. But once China's 0.38 PPP weight multiplies its locked -2.7 pp/yr aging drag (-1.03 pp) and OECD working-age contraction plus Baumol composition adds -0.25 to -0.40 pp, the demographic block subtracts roughly 4x what the AI block adds inside the 2032-36 window. No reading of 2B held exogenous can be reconciled with 2A's demographic arithmetic at the coupled-growth level a reader would infer from the regime labels; the tension runs toward LOWER coupled growth (my 1.5%/yr P50 against a CQ6-B label that says 1.7-2.5%), and nothing in the coupling runs the other way. A secondary, smaller tension sits in AI-Q3: its P90 of 1,573.8 TWh for OECD-38 + China is equivalent, at $80/MWh industrial power against ~$130T of combined PPP GDP, to an electricity-bill ceiling of 0.097% of GDP — i.e. the locked prior implicitly assumes a willingness-to-pay cap of almost exactly the kind the simulation implements at 0.05%. The locked prior and the model agree on the mechanism (price-capped load) and differ only by about 2x on the ceiling's level, which is the one place in this exercise where an independent model corroborates rather than contradicts a locked marginal.

wave1.lens_self_description: Inside-View Empirical Signal Scout: I built every number upward from the freshest observable administrative, survey and vendor telemetry on labour reallocation, care/trade bottlenecks and offshoring flows, reporting each series with its sampling and dating caveats verbatim; this forbade me from using any structural model, any simulation output, any outside-view analogy to prior technology waves, and any appeal to theoretical equilibrium logic unless a currently-published series anchored it — where I could not verify a current level I wrote "unverified at my horizon" rather than inventing one.
wave1.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonised unemployment avg <=5.5%, 2032-36): marginal 60%. OBSERVED (hard administrative, OECD Statistical Release "Labour market situation, updated October 2026"): OECD unemployment 5.0% in August 2026, "just 0.2 percentage points above its record low" (June 2023); July 2026 was 4.9%, "its lowest level in a year"; EU 6.1%, euro area 6.4%; US 4.2% and Canada 6.5% (September estimates); Japan/Korea/Mexico/Israel at or below 3.0%. CAVEAT VERBATIM: youth (15-24) unemployment "rose to 11.3% in August from 11.0% in July" — the youth margin is deteriorating while the aggregate is not, which is exactly the Brynjolfsson-Chandar-Chen signature and means the aggregate rate is a poor instrument for AI displacement. Reference class: OECD aggregate rate has sat in a 4.8-5.2% band for five consecutive years; 2017-19 averaged ~5.5%; 2020-21 averaged ~7.0%. INFERRED: the locked 2A old-age ratio move (31% -> 39-41%) shrinks the denominator mechanically, so a 5-year average above 5.5% essentially requires one 2020-style or two 2008-style recessions inside 2032-36. P(no such event, 5-yr window) ~0.60.
CONJUNCT B (F+Q real median hourly wage growth beats J+K+M by >=10.0pp over 2025-36, i.e. ~0.9pp/yr for 11 years): marginal 20%. OBSERVED pointing FOR: construction hourly wages +5.2% y/y vs +3.2% private-sector (BLS, cited in Burns & McDonnell construction market update 2026) — a +2.0pp one-year gap; Indeed's rival cut is narrower, +3.4% construction vs +2.4% overall pay, May 2025-May 2026 (VENDOR/JOB-BOARD data, not administrative, and the two series disagree by half the gap); data-centre construction carries a ~32% premium (Skillit, VENDOR); electrician deficit peaking 2027 at ~107,000 (Industrial Info Resources, industry), BLS ~81,000/yr through 2034; union electricians "up to $130 an hour before overtime" and Dallas/N. Virginia data-centre electricians at "$200,000-$280,000 a year" — these last are VENDOR BLOG figures, explicitly unverified and likely outlier roles. OBSERVED pointing AGAINST (the decisive leg, and my lens's finding): the measure is a MEDIAN, and both composition effects run against B. In J+K+M, AI removes the bottom of the distribution first — 22-25-year-olds in the most-exposed 40% of occupations down ~11% since 2022, young software developers down "nearly 20%" by July 2025 from a late-2022 peak — so the surviving J+K+M workforce skews senior and the measured MEDIAN rises even as labour's share of sectoral GVA falls. CAVEAT VERBATIM: the Stanford/ADP findings are correlational; "across all workers, the study found little difference in employment between occupations considered highly exposed to AI and those less affected"; coverage figures conflict (6% vs 11% vs 13% depending on measure); "entry-level employment has declined in applications of AI that automate work, with muted changes for augmentation"; one 2026 article refers to an August 2026 update I could not verify. In F+Q, the clearing mechanism is migrant and new entrant inflow at the bottom — ~122,000 Indian-trained nurses in OECD countries (OECD data cited late 2025, SECONDARY reporting), "one in six nurses in high-income countries was trained abroad" (OECD figure, secondary), Japan recruiting against a ~250,000 nursing-care shortfall in FY2026 — which pushes the F+Q median DOWN. Third leg: care wages are set by strained public payers (2A: pension/social-security subsidies already ~2.9T RMB, ~10.1% of Chinese fiscal expenditure; OECD net interest 2% -> ~3% of GDP), and Baumol means no productivity to fund them. US RN vacancy rate is 8.6% in acute care, "down from 9.6% in 2024" (2026 NSI report via AACN; nursing faculty vacancies ~7%, nearly 1,700 unfilled) — i.e. the care deficit is easing modestly WITHOUT a wage explosion. P(B) = 20%.
CORRELATION: +0.25 (tight labour markets and F+Q scarcity are the same shock), so P(B|A) ~0.23. JOINT = 0.60 x 0.23 = 0.138 -> 14.
wave1.cq2_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core >=2.50%/yr avg 2027-36): marginal 66%. OBSERVED (hard, OECD "Consumer prices, updated 6 October 2026"): OECD core (ex food and energy) "remained stable at 3.6% for the third consecutive month"; OECD headline 4.3% y/y in August 2026; energy inflation "stabilised above 10%" (July release). Euro area core 2.5% in September 2026, up from 2.4% in August (Eurostat-based); euro area headline flash "up 0.6 p.p. to 3.8% - its highest level since September 2023". CAVEAT: the OECD-wide 3.6% core is an unweighted-ish aggregate inflated by Turkey; the question's GDP-weighted OECD-38 core is materially lower, and I estimate it at ~2.8-3.1% now — that estimate is MINE, not published, and is the single weakest link in my chain. Fermi arithmetic: if 2027-29 average ~2.9% (near-locked by current momentum, grid/energy >10%, tariff and care-cost pass-through), the remaining seven years 2030-36 need only (25.0-8.7)/7 = 2.33% to clear the bar — barely above central-bank target. That arithmetic advantage, not a stagflation forecast, is what gets conjunct A to 66%. Downside: the locked AI-Q4 66% impairment/cancellation probability is a disinflationary demand event, and BIS AER 2026 Box C's aggregate-demand shortfall channel is explicitly disinflationary.
CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI avg <1.50%/yr, 2027-36): marginal 72%. OBSERVED: September 2026 CPI ~0.9% y/y, up from 0.8% in August, below a 1.0% forecast, with food dragging on pork oversupply — CAVEAT VERBATIM: this is from TrendForce, a SECONDARY DATA AGGREGATOR with an AI-generated summary; "I couldn't confirm it against the National Bureau of Statistics release", so treat 0.9% as unverified at my horizon. Hard prior-year administrative baseline: September 2025 CPI -0.3% y/y, PPI -2.3% and negative for 36 consecutive months, described by Bloomberg as "the longest streak of economy-wide price declines since market reforms in the late 1970s"; September 2025 core CPI hit 1.0% "for the first time in 19 months". Reference class: China CPI averaged ~1.5-1.6% over 2015-24; Japan 1995-2015 averaged ~0.1% under a comparable demographic contraction. Coupled 2A input: -60M population 2026-35, worker/retiree 4.4 -> 2.8, property deleveraging, excess capacity. P(B) = 72%. Upside risks to inflation: pork cycle, deliberate reflation to fund the pension gap, RMB depreciation pass-through.
CORRELATION: mildly NEGATIVE, -0.10. China goods deflation is an OECD disinflationary export, so the two conjuncts partly fight each other; but they are also two faces of one bifurcation (OECD labour-scarce and fiscally loose vs China demand-deficient), which offsets most of the drag. JOINT = 0.66 x 0.72 x (1 - small) = 0.475 x 0.91 = 0.43 -> 43.
wave1.cq3_reasoning:
Decomposition, PPP weights ~0.69 OECD-38 / ~0.31 China for 2032-36 (constant 2025 USD PPP; China's PPP share drifts up from ~0.30).
OECD-38 leg, P50 = 0.95%/yr. Locked 2A: per-capita baseline 0.6%/yr (down ~40% from 1.0%). hypothesis_critique.a: The failure word is "SMOOTHLY". The cross-elasticity between a displaced ISIC J/K/M worker and an ISIC Q entrant is approximately ZERO at the individual level, and every observable friction points the same way. Stock-flow mismatch: the displacement is concentrated in 22-25-year-olds (employment in the most-exposed 40% of occupations down ~11% since 2022; young software developers down "nearly 20%" by July 2025 from a late-2022 peak - CAVEAT: Stanford/ADP, correlational, and "across all workers, the study found little difference in employment between occupations considered highly exposed to AI and those less affected"), whereas the stock at risk in white-collar mid-career is 40-55 and the nursing entry pipeline is age-selective and physically selective. Licensing queue: Canada's credentialing process reportedly takes "six months to two years"; Germany requires German at B1-B2 plus diploma recognition and "foreign nursing diplomas are not automatically recognised"; NCLEX first-time pass rates for US-educated candidates were 88.6% (2023), 91.2% (2024), 86.7% (2025), and Health Affairs reports IEN pass rates "have been steadily declining since 2010" - the bottleneck is the exam and the recognition queue, not willingness. Faculty capacity caps the pipeline independently: nursing faculty vacancies ~7%, nearly 1,700 positions unfilled (2026 NSI via AACN). Gender composition: care work is ~85-90% female across the OECD; the displaced cognitive cohort is not. Physical strain: Q has among the highest musculoskeletal injury rates of any sector, which is a hard filter on 45+ re-entrants. Reservation wage: an ex-paralegal's reservation wage exceeds the public-payer-set care wage, and Baumol plus the 2A fiscal strain (pension subsidies at ~10.1% of Chinese fiscal expenditure; OECD net interest heading to ~3% of GDP) means the care wage cannot rise to close it without a transfer that 2A says is already strained. The observed clearing mechanism is NOT reallocation at all - it is migration and new cohorts (~122,000 Indian-trained nurses in OECD countries per OECD data cited late 2025, secondary reporting; "one in six nurses in high-income countries was trained abroad"; Japan recruiting against a ~250,000 FY2026 shortfall). A weaker version - "AI frees fiscal and wage room that eventually gets spent on care, via immigrants and new entrants rather than the displaced" - would score around 45. As stated: 6.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO failure words: "BLOCKS" and "SEVERELY". "Blocks" is falsified by current telemetry on the virtual leg: Nasscom's Annual Strategic Review 2026 (February 2026) puts India tech revenue at $315B, +6.1%, exports above $246B, +5.6%, with net headcount ADDITIONS of 135,000 to 5.95 million - CAVEAT: industry-body projections, not final audited figures, and some outlets round to "around 6 million" while one headline mislabels the revenue year. AI revenue is $10-12B in FY26, and Nasscom states this "excludes AI-specific revenue from some firms", so it is a floor not a full count. The observed effect is a fall in the HEADCOUNT ELASTICITY of revenue (2.3% jobs vs 6.1% revenue), not a block. Philippines likewise: contact-centre workforce grew 4% to 1.68 million in 2025 from 1.62 million in 2024, projected ~1.73 million in 2026 (CXAP; CC-BPM is 89% of IT-BPM employment), with IBPAP targeting ~1.97 million FTE and ~$42B revenue by end-2026 and its midterm review WIDENING the range to 1.85-2.14 million while "its own communications flag the 2026 figures as under review". CXAP argues 2025 growth "counters the common notion that AI brings about job displacement" - note this is INDUSTRY-ASSOCIATION data with an obvious directional interest, and the rival SunStar framing "AI puts 1.9M IT-BPM jobs at risk" does not show its derivation, so treat both as advocacy. "Severely" is falsified by the NET of the two legs. VIRTUAL leg: negative on growth rate, roughly -1 to -3%/yr relative to counterfactual headcount, concentrated in entry-level voice and workflow tasks. PHYSICAL leg: strongly positive and already visible - Japan's ~250,000 FY2026 care shortfall rising to ~570,000 by FY2040, Japan reportedly moving to offer permanent residency to nurses under a two-tier visa (The Weekly Source, September 2026, UNVERIFIED), Germany's 350,000-500,000 projected care gap by 2035 (commercial guide, not official), ~122,000 Indian-trained nurses already in OECD countries, second only to the Philippines. REMITTANCE leg, the cleanest hard series: Philippine cash remittances hit a record $35.634B in 2025, +3.3% from $34.493B in 2024 (BSP); $14.1B in Jan-May 2026; BSP forecasts $36.6B for 2026, "marking 2.7-percent growth"; UnionBank attributes the record to "steady overseas employment, particularly in healthcare, maritime, and professional services", with one economist calling remittances "more of a stable income anchor rather than a strong cyclical growth driver this year" and authorities noting no indications of "mass repatriation or widespread deployment bans". India's remittance growth rate I could not verify at my horizon. NET: the physical and remittance legs are currently OUTWEIGHING the virtual compression in income terms, though the virtual leg hits the higher-wage, higher-value-added, more fiscally productive slice, so the composition deteriorates even as the level holds. The directionally-correct weak version - "virtual export growth decelerates sharply while physical export demand rises, so the net is a composition downgrade rather than a collapse" - would score ~70. As stated: 14.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failure word is "FALLS" (with "then" doing quiet work in sequencing it). The first clause is close to already-observed: OECD core "remained stable at 3.6% for the third consecutive month" (OECD, 6 October 2026), headline 4.3% y/y in August 2026, energy inflation "stabilised above 10%", euro area headline flash up 0.6pp to 3.8%, "its highest level since September 2023". So "hot for the next few years" is near-locked and earns the plank most of its credence. The second clause is where it breaks, for a reason inside my effort's mechanism: the things keeping inflation hot are not a demand pulse that decays, they are SUPPLY WALLS with multi-year build times - grid and generation (datacentre load against energy inflation above 10%), the electrician deficit peaking in 2027 at ~107,000 with BLS projecting ~81,000/yr shortfalls THROUGH 2034, and the Baumol care wedge whose licensing queues run "six months to two years" and whose faculty bottleneck (~7% vacancies, ~1,700 unfilled) caps the pipeline through the 2030s. None of those clears on the plank's timetable. My own CQ6 puts 22 on persistent core >=2.7% in 2032-36 and 22 on core <2.0%; the plank requires the latter, so my consistency-consistent credence for "falls" in the strong sense of durably returning below target is ~32%. The plank also conflates OECD and China: for CHINA the plank is near-certainly right in direction (CPI ~0.9% y/y in September 2026, on a TrendForce secondary aggregator reading I could not confirm against the NBS release, after -0.3% in September 2025 and PPI negative for 36 consecutive months, "the longest streak of economy-wide price declines since market reforms in the late 1970s"), and the plank's one-world framing hides that divergence. 33.
hypothesis_critique.d: TWO failure words: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS". "Eventually" is unfalsifiable and in particular is outside the Dec 31 2036 resolution horizon - it converts a forecast into a tautology, and a plank that cannot be scored within the window should not collect credence inside it. "Wins" is undefined: wins against what counterfactual, in levels or in growth rates, in measured GDP or in welfare? Scored against the only operationalisation the window admits - does AI TFP exceed the demographic drag by 2032-36 - the locked priors answer no: AI-Q1 gives only 23.0% raw to a PPP-weighted TFP lift of +0.50pp/yr or more, AI-Q6's modal regime is Jagged Diffusion at 47.2% with the Hulten Ceiling at 36.5%, and the IMF WEO April 2026 drag is -1.1pp/yr globally and -2.7pp/yr in China. There is a second, subtler failure my effort surfaces: even if AI's SECTORAL TFP is exponential, measured AGGREGATE TFP need not be, because aging reallocates labour INTO Baumol care and trades where measured productivity growth is ~0-0.3%/yr - the composition wedge means "exponential AI" and "GDP growth wins" are not the same proposition, and the plank treats them as one. 11.

wave1.coupling_tension:
The sharpest inconsistency is AI-Q2 (OECD-38 firm adoption >=50% by 2036, 21.3% raw). Held demographically exogenous, 21.3% is a reasonable read of a slow diffusion curve. Once 2A is endogenous it is TOO LOW, and I would move it to roughly 30-34%, because labour scarcity is the strongest adoption driver actually observable in the data rather than the strongest adoption driver in theory: the highest observed automation intensity in the world sits in exactly the oldest societies (Japan/Korea robot density), Japan is running a ~250,000 FY2026 nursing-care shortfall against 28,400 foreign specified-skilled-worker caregivers at end-2023 ("just over half the government's target"), the US electrician deficit peaks at ~107,000 in 2027 against BLS shortfalls of ~81,000/yr through 2034, and construction wages are running +5.2% y/y against +3.2% private sector. Aging is a DEMAND PULL for adoption that 2B's exogeneity assumption discards, and it pulls hardest precisely where AI is weakest (physical/care), so it raises adoption BREADTH (the Q2 firm-count measure) much more than it raises measured TFP.
That asymmetry generates the second and more important tension: 2B's six marginals are implicitly CO-MONOTONE in "AI works" - AI-Q1 (TFP) and AI-Q2 (adoption) are priced as if the same latent variable drives both. Endogenous demographics DECOUPLE them, and in opposite directions. AI-Q2 should rise (labour scarcity forces adoption), while AI-Q1 (>=+0.50pp PPP-weighted TFP, 23.0% raw) should FALL to roughly 18-20%, because the Baumol composition wedge taxes measured aggregate TFP regardless of sectoral technical progress: labour reallocating into F+Q at ~0-0.3%/yr measured productivity, with a rising employment share, subtracts on the order of -0.15pp/yr from the aggregate. So the coupled joint distribution contains a cell the standalone marginals treat as near-empty - WIDE adoption with LOW measured TFP - and that cell is exactly my CQ6-B at 44 and my CQ3 P50 of 1.6%. Any aggregation that imposes a positive Q1-Q2 correlation will under-weight it.
Two further, smaller tensions, same direction of travel. AI-Q5 (cognitive labour compensation share falls >=3.5pp, 38.2% raw) should rise to roughly 45-48%: endogenous demographics retire the most expensive senior cohort in ISIC J/K/M while AI simultaneously blocks the entry-level replacement flow (22-25-year-old employment in the most-exposed 40% of occupations down ~11% since 2022 - CAVEAT: correlational, and "across all workers, the study found little difference in employment between occupations considered highly exposed to AI and those less affected"), so the compensation numerator falls from both ends at once. Independently, the US labour share is already at a record low on multiple inconsistent measures - 54.1% "down from 55.3% a year ago" and "the lowest level since the US government began tracking it following World War II" (S&P Global, June 30 2026), 53.7% nonfarm business in Q1 2026 (Research Square), 52.8% (EY-Parthenon via Shopifreaks), 51.4% on a gross-domestic-income basis in the third quarter "down from 58% in 1980" (Axios) - and these are DIFFERENT MEASURES AND PERIODS, not directly comparable, with the Tax Foundation's own tabulation finding the labour share "remains within historical levels" and Goldman's Duggirala arguing "the decline has been less steep than BLS data suggests". wave2.lens_self_description: I applied explicit Bayesian likelihood-ratio updating: for every CQ I adopted the Historian's reference-class base rate as my stated prior, treated the Signal Scout's 2026 telemetry as evidence with a named LR, used the Fermi seat's decomposition only as a structural constraint on which quantities are even admissible, and discounted to LR≈1.0 any signal I could not justify above roughly 2:1 — which forbade me from asserting any number on my own authority, from using the simulation output as either prior or fact, and from moving a posterior on a signal whose sourcing or date I could not stand behind.
wave2.cq1_reasoning:
PRIOR: Historian's 12 (joint), built from marginal A=0.40, P(B|A)=0.30. I update the two conjuncts separately.

CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonised unemployment 2032-36 avg <=5.5%). Prior 0.40 (Historian: ~4-8 of ~52 overlapping windows ever averaged <=5.5%, adjusted up for the mechanical denominator effect). EVIDENCE 1, Scout: OECD aggregate 5.0% Aug 2026 ("just 0.2pp above its record low"), 4.9% July 2026, five consecutive years in a 4.8-5.2% band (OECD Statistical Release Oct 2026 — hard administrative). LR = P(a five-year 4.8-5.2% plateau now | 2032-36 avg <=5.5%) / P(same | >5.5%) = 0.85/0.45 = 1.9. FLAGGED: this is BELOW my 2:1 bar, because a path that averages >5.5% in 2032-36 can perfectly well start from 5.0% — the whole question is recession arrival, which the current level does not inform. Discounted to effective LR 1.4. Posterior odds 0.667 x 1.4 = 0.933 -> A = 0.48. EVIDENCE 2, Scout's counter-signal: youth (15-24) unemployment 11.0% -> 11.3% Jul->Aug 2026. LR = 0.4/0.5 = 0.8, i.e. 1.25:1 — unjustifiable above 2:1 on one month of a noisy sub-aggregate. DISCOUNTED to 1.0. A = 0.49.

CONJUNCT B (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >=10.0pp cumulative, 2025-36 = ~0.87pp/yr for 11 years). Prior 0.20 (Historian: ~2-3 of ~8 non-overlapping 11-yr windows since 1940 ran pro-physical at this size, and OECD *Beyond Applause* documents 25 years of LTC shortage NOT clearing through wages because care pay is fiscally administered). I apply only the INCREMENTAL Scout evidence, to avoid double-counting the non-clearing base rate already inside the prior. EVIDENCE 1 (pro-B): construction hourly +5.2% y/y vs +3.2% private sector (BLS via Burns & McDonnell) — a one-year gap of 2.0pp, already above the required run rate. LR = 0.6/0.35 = 1.7. BELOW the bar, and weakened further because Indeed's rival cut is +3.4% vs +2.4%, half the gap — two series disagreeing by 100bp cannot carry a 2:1 claim. Discounted to 1.3. EVIDENCE 2 (anti-B, the decisive one): US acute-care RN vacancy rate 8.6% in 2026, "down from 9.6% in 2024" (NSI via AACN) — the care deficit is EASING with no relative real wage gain, which is direct observation of quantity-clearing. LR = 0.25/0.60 = 0.42 (2.4:1 against B), above the bar and justified; partly overlapping the prior's *Beyond Applause* content so I apply 0.60 rather than 0.42. EVIDENCE 3 (anti-B, measurement direction): 22-25-year-olds in the most-exposed 40% of occupations down ~11% since 2022; young software developers down ~20% by Jul 2025 from the late-2022 peak (Stanford/ADP — CAVEAT PRESERVED: correlational, and "across all workers, the study found little difference in employment between occupations considered highly exposed to AI and those less affected"; coverage figures conflict at 6%/11%/13%). AI removes the BOTTOM of the J+K+M distribution, so the surviving J+K+M MEDIAN rises by composition; migrant and new-entrant inflow (~122k Indian-trained nurses in OECD; "one in six nurses in high-income countries was trained abroad") pushes the F+Q MEDIAN down. Both composition effects raise B's bar. LR = 0.6 (1.7:1 against) — I will not claim more given the stated caveats. Posterior odds 0.25 x 1.3 x 0.60 x 0.60 = 0.117 -> B = 0.105.

CORRELATION: +0.25 (between Fermi's +0.15 and Historian's +0.35). Tight labour markets both suppress unemployment and bid scarce-sector wages, but the configuration most favourable to B — hot care bidding driven by AI displacement — is the configuration that damages A, so the positive dependence is partly self-cancelling. P(B|A) = 0.105 x 1.25 = 0.13.

MULTIPLICATION: 0.49 x 0.13 = 0.064 -> 6.4. I round UP to 9 for LR uncertainty and for partial overlap between evidence 2 and 3 (both are "the system does not clear by price", one observed in vacancies and one in medians).

DIRECTION: AMPLIFIED away from the Wave-1 base rate by -3 points (12 -> 9). Conjunct A moved UP (+9pp, 0.40 -> 0.49) on the administrative plateau; conjunct B moved DOWN (-10pp, 0.20 -> 0.105) on the vacancy-easing and median-composition evidence; the B move dominates because it enters the product against a conjunct already near one half.

Panelist estimates span -0.20 (Fermi) to -0.10 (Scout) to ~0 (Historian); I adopt a multiplicative ratio of 0.87. P(B|A) = 0.67 x 0.87 = 0.583.

MULTIPLICATION: 0.55 x 0.583 = 0.321 -> 32.

Almost the entire move is conjunct A (+20pp, 0.35 -> 0.55), driven by one above-2:1 signal whose power is arithmetic rather than forecast — three of the ten averaging years are substantially observable and they are hot. wave2.cq3_reasoning:
PRIOR: Historian's 1.0 / 1.95 / 2.95, itself a deliberate deviation from a ~90% unconditional base rate for the >=2.6% band, justified by the monotone weight-times-growth decline (4.3% in 2010-14 -> 3.6% in 2015-19 -> 2.54% in 2020-24, ~1pp per decade for three decades).

WEIGHT RESOLUTION FIRST, because the three seats disagree and it is arithmetic, not evidence: Fermi 0.38, Historian 0.39, Scout 0.31. Scout's 0.31 is the outlier and is inconsistent with OECD-38 PPP GDP ~$72T against China ~$41T (0.36 in 2025, drifting up). Fermi reconciled his 0.38 against the adapter's independent 0.371 at 2031 despite a different regional partition. I adopt w_China = 0.375, w_OECD = 0.625.

Above the bar, and the reproduction of the locked marginal is a verifiable consistency check rather than an opinion, so I do not discount it. This is what moves me off the Historian's 1.95%.

EVIDENCE 2 (the simulation, treated as ONE piece of evidence with its own LR, per my brief — not as prior and not as fact): the adapter returns coupled 2032-36 growth of 2.95% baseline, 2.30% tech-stagnation, 1.67% debt-populism, 3.68% tech-breakthrough. My 1.6% sits below its entire ordinary range. LR = P(this model prints 2.95% | true coupled growth is high) / P(same | low) ~ 1.1. BELOW the 2:1 bar, DISCOUNTED TO 1.0, and the justification is Fermi's clean internal diagnostic rather than a dismissal: the adapter itself discloses that the model's demographic path tracks the UN WPP LOW variant (~18% below medium by 2100), which should bias its labour force and growth DOWN; that it nonetheless prints 2.95% demonstrates that aging is nearly irrelevant to this model by construction, because the Ayres-Warr production function carries gamma = 0.55 on useful energy against a mainstream cost-share gamma of 0.05-0.08, and the documented dominant GDP dial is serviceEfficiencyGrowth (~1.8x per plausible range), a second-law efficiency parameter. A model that is demonstrably insensitive to the exact channel at issue cannot carry a likelihood ratio on it. Its China leg at 3.81% simply does not implement the locked -2.7pp/yr aging drag.

EVIDENCE 3 (the one model reading I DO take, at LR ~2.5, because it falls inside the model's competence — an endogenous marginal-value-versus-marginal-cost deployment rule rather than a demographic channel): robotsPer1000 reaches 3.92 baseline / 6.09 automation-boom / 6.63 ai-energy-boom by 2036, i.e. 0.39-0.66% of workers' worth of installed stock world-wide, all sectors, with physical care robots a small subset — against a care need Fermi sizes at 18.3M OECD-38 workers (3.0% of employment). The "robots fill the elder-care gap inside the horizon" channel is arithmetically closed. LOW-FERTILITY-CONDITIONAL, as every reading off this model is.

CHINA LEG. Panelists: Fermi 1.97% (labour -0.63, capital deepening +2.00, TFP +1.10, property/credit/pension-claim drag -0.50, cross-checked against a frictionless ~4.7% less the locked -2.7pp = 2.0%), Scout 2.8%, Historian ~3.0%. But Fermi's +2.00 capital-deepening and -0.50 property terms are by his own account his least-anchored, and Scout brings a signed upside signal — China's observed robot-density growth is the highest in the world and is its explicit labour substitute (LR ~1.3, below the bar but signed and I apply it at half weight). POSTERIOR China = 2.3%/yr.

OECD LEG. Fermi 0.99% (2A-consistent by construction), Scout 0.90-1.00%, including a -0.15pp Baumol composition wedge for labour reallocating INTO F+Q at ~0-0.3%/yr measured productivity. Converged. POSTERIOR OECD = 1.0%/yr.

ASSEMBLY: 0.625 x 1.0 + 0.375 x 2.3 = 0.625 + 0.863 = 1.49 -> P50 1.6%/yr, rounded up for the capital-deepening terms being the least-anchored on both legs.

INTERVAL. P10 0.6: a synchronised recession inside the 5-year averaging window (base rate ~50% per window, subtracting 0.8-1.2pp from the average) OR the AI-Q4 capex bust (66% locked) resolving in 2027-32 and leaving 2032-36 as the digestion window, plus a China property/pension accident. The single mover is the one above-2:1 signal: the weight-times-drag arithmetic reproduced independently by two seats, one of which ties back to a locked marginal.
wave2.cq4_reasoning:
PRIOR: Historian's 0.8 / 2.0 / 3.3, centred on level persistence with a 10bp mean-reversion tilt, plus his own observation that a 5-year average lands within +/-50bp of its starting level only ~30-35% of the time.

MEASUREMENT SPECIFICATION FIRST, and it is the largest single correction in this question — arithmetic, so it carries no LR, it simply has to be right. The question asks for a G7 GDP-WEIGHTED 10y real yield; the locked 2.60% (FRED DFII10, Oct 30 2026) is US-ONLY. All three seats independently apply G7 weights and land on a current weighted level of 1.71% (Fermi: US 2.60, JP -0.20, DE 0.70, UK 1.30, FR 0.60, IT 1.50, CA 1.80), 1.8-1.9% (Scout, who flags that he "could not verify the non-US legs at my horizon" and found "NO sourced 2026 Japanese or German 10y level and NO sourced 2026 10y real yield outside the US"), and ~1.90% (Historian). I adopt ~1.80% as today's weighted level. Anyone anchoring on 2.60% has mis-specified the object by ~80-90bp.

EVIDENCE 1 (LR below the bar, applied at a discount): three independent builds converge in a 2.0-2.2% band — Historian 2.0 (persistence plus tilt), Fermi 2.10 (r* 1.75 + real term premium 0.75 - financial-repression wedge 0.40), Scout 2.2 (weight-shift argument: the measure rises because the weight shifts toward Japanese and German legs with more room to rise than the US leg has to fall). LR = P(three independent builds all landing 2.0-2.2 | true 2032-36 average >=2.0) / P(same | <2.0) = 0.60/0.35 = 1.7. BELOW the 2:1 bar — convergence among three seats reading the same locked 2A text is not three independent observations, and I flag it as such. DISCOUNTED to 1.3. That carries me from a 2.0 prior to 2.1.

EVIDENCE 2 (locked 2A, one-directional up, and not a signal I can assign an LR to because it is given fact rather than observation): global gross public debt crosses 100% of GDP by 2029 (~142% US and ~127% China by 2031); net interest 2% -> ~3% of GDP; 3-year P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117% of GDP, "+2.4 pp more under a 20% AI-led equity valuation shock"; eroding sovereign convenience yields; levered hedge-fund basis-trade absorption replacing price-insensitive demand. Fermi's decomposition prices these at +40bp public dissaving, +20bp convenience yield, and a +0.75pp real term premium with the marginal duration buyer being the relative-value complex — the same object CQ5 prices.

EVIDENCE 3 (the sign most often missed, and it caps my P50 at 2.1 rather than Scout's 2.2): the demographic term on r itself is SMALL. 2A explicitly states that aging worsens global (r-g) by ~+1.0pp "even where a frictionless r* eases" — i.e. most of the (r-g) deterioration is g falling, not r rising, which is exactly my CQ3. Fermi keeps only +10bp for life-cycle dissaving, and then subtracts -0.15 for precautionary saving and -0.15 for the BIS AER 2026 Box C channel (capital-concentrated income carries a higher saving propensity, so AI-Q5-style cognitive-labour compression is a demand shortfall and therefore a NEGATIVE for r*). Scout's own consistency check agrees: r = 2.2% against his OECD g ~0.95% gives r-g ~ +1.25pp, matching the locked +1.0pp worsening. I verify mine: r 2.1% against my OECD leg 1.0% gives r-g = +1.10pp. 2A-consistent.

EVIDENCE 4 (the simulation — REFUSED as a point estimate, used for direction only, which is the correct handling): the adapter self-reports "NOT IDENTIFIED (CQ4): capital.interestRate is an economy-wide REAL interest rate... no 10-year sovereign benchmark, no term premium (no termPremium anywhere in src/), and no inflation swap or breakeven". Its readings of 5.99-6.96% are a marginal product of capital; the ~400bp gap to 2.1% is an equity/credit risk premium plus a convenience yield, neither of which exists in the model. The DIRECTIONAL content I do use, at LR ~2.0: across scenarios the model's rate moves +0.87pp for fiscal/political stress (debt-populism 6.96 vs baseline 6.09, debt risk premium +1.08pp to 2.50) but only +0.09pp for the strongest technology regime (tech-breakthrough 6.18, premium FALLING 0.22pp). Even inside a model built around an energy-technology engine, the fiscal leg moves the cost of capital 4-10x more than the technology regime. That is a reason to place my variance in the repression and term-premium terms rather than in r*-from-aging, and it is low-fertility-conditional like every other reading off this model.

MOVE VERSUS KNOWN-UNKNOWN: Scout reports "I found no current 2026 ACM/KW term-premium figure" and "no current 2026 term premium figures". I preserve that: the decomposition between r* and term premium is uninstrumented at the panel's horizon, which is itself a reason to keep the band wide rather than to sharpen.

INTERVAL. P10 1.0: the repression wedge widens toward -1.00pp under arriving fiscal dominance (base rate of G7 real yields being capped during a fiscal-stress episode is high — 1940s-50s, 2010s), the term premium compresses to +0.25, and the AI-capex-bust branch flips the capex-demand-for-savings term negative. I set 1.0 rather than Historian's 0.8 because the starting weighted level is ~1.80% and a 5-year average 80bp below it requires both repression and a bust. P90 3.3: no repression, term premium +1.50, convenience yield erodes faster, Japanese normalization completes (-0.20 -> +0.80 alone contributes +11bp at an 11% weight). Note 3.3% would still sit below every 1980s and 1990s G7 decade average, so the upper tail is not an extreme call by base rate.

DIRECTION: MODERATED upward by +10bp at the median (2.0 -> 2.1) and the left tail tightened by +20bp (0.8 -> 1.0). This is the question where my updating moved least, and deliberately so: the only signal pointing above the prior failed the 2:1 test, and the strongest structural content (the +1.0pp (r-g) deterioration being mostly a g story) argues against treating aging as an r* event at all.
wave2.cq5_reasoning:
PRIOR: Historian's 22, from marginal A=0.35 and P(B|A)=0.62.

CONJUNCT A (ICE BofA MOVE averages >=105 over Jan 2027 - Dec 2036). Prior 0.35 (Historian: ~6-8 of ~28 rolling 10-yr windows clear it; full-history mean 93.6 since 1988 with the start date contested — "ICE's own data page says history from 1996"; 10-year average ~75 per Carmignac; 2017-19 ~55; 2022 cycle ~130; so 105 is MATERIALLY ABOVE the full-history mean). EVIDENCE 1, Scout's level telemetry: 70.9 as of Jul 17 2026 (tracker page); 65.7-66bp on a Convex page where "it gives no date for that reading" and "it may be stale"; 103.01 "by mid-2026" (Pulse, time-dependent and undated); 115 on an NBot summary "last updated April 8, 2026"; a seven-day decline to 66.87, "its lowest level since 2021", "probably from October 2025" but carrying no date. Scout's own verdict: "These cannot be reconciled; I could not find a confirmed October 2026 close and treat the level as UNVERIFIED AT MY HORIZON". LR UNJUSTIFIABLE AT ANY RATIO — a signal spanning 66 to 115 with contested or absent dates cannot move a posterior in either direction. SET TO 1.0 AND FLAGGED. This is the single worst-instrumented input in the question set and the main place where this seat's failure mode (weak evidence asserted confidently) would bite.

EVIDENCE 2, Fermi's level-scaling constraint, which IS usable because it is a ratio rather than a level reading: MOVE is 1-month implied Treasury yield vol in annualized bp, scaling roughly as k x (nominal yield level) x (policy-path dispersion). At my CQ4 P50 of 2.1% real the G7-weighted nominal 10y is ~4.3-4.7%; scaling the 2015-19 mean of ~65 by 4.5/2.5 = 1.8 gives ~117. But the observed 2024-26 run-rate of ~85-100 at ALREADY-comparable yields shows k has FALLEN (QT completed, policy path less dispersed). That is evidence AGAINST A, and it is the right form of evidence: a decade average >=105 now requires k to RISE, not merely yields to stay high. LR = P(MOVE running 70-100 today with nominals already ~4.5% | decade avg >=105) / P(same | <105) = 0.35/0.60 = 0.58, i.e. ~1.7:1 against. Below the bar — and it rests on the same unreconciled level readings — so DISCOUNTED to 0.75. Posterior odds 0.538 x 0.75 = 0.404 -> 0.29. I then restore +4pp for the purely mechanical 2A plumbing terms (far larger duration supply, net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP, $650B of AI-related debt issuance against $300B of equity creating correlated repricing risk, basis-trade leverage that amplifies yield vol in a deleveraging). A = 0.33.

CONJUNCT B (at least one episode with MSCI World -25% peak-to-trough WHILE G7 weighted 10y nominals fail to fall >=50bp, or rise >=25bp, in the drawdown window). Split into B1 and B2. B1: Historian's base rate is the cleanest input in the whole question — 8 world-equity drawdowns >=25% since 1970 (1973-74, 1980-82, 1987, 1990, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020, 2022), roughly one per 7 years, Poisson lambda ~1.4 per decade, P(at least one in ten years) 0.80-0.85. Fermi's mechanism-build gives only 0.58; I REJECT the downgrade, because every locked 2A fact bearing on it raises drawdown probability above base rate rather than lowering it (AI names ~35-40% of MSCI World capitalization, ~$1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on a ~$300B equity base, AI-Q4 at 66%, the Fiscal Monitor's own explicit 20% AI-led equity valuation shock scenario, 3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk 117% of GDP). B1 = 0.80. B2 | B1: Historian's unconditional historical split is 3 of 8, ~38% (1973-74, 1980-82, 2022 yields-up versus 1987, 1990, 2000-02, 2008-09, 2020 flight-to-quality); Fermi's shock-type weighting gives 0.43; Scout's gives 0.35. These converge, so I take 0.39 and then shade DOWN to 0.36 for the one conditioning correction all three seats independently identify and which I regard as the sharpest finding in this effort: the MODAL generator of a >=25% drawdown in this specific window is the AI capex bust (AI-Q4 at 66% raw), and a capex bust is DISINFLATIONARY, so bonds rally hard and conjunct B FAILS. The question is quietly asking for two things from opposite shock families. LR on that conditioning: P(locked prior set skewing the shock mix toward a disinflationary bust | B2 conditional below the historical 38%) / P(same | at or above) = 0.65/0.30 = 2.2, above the bar, but it only earns a small shade because the historical 3-of-8 already contains inflationary and fiscal episodes. Over the decade, Poisson-compounding: 1 - exp(-1.4 x 0.36) = 0.39; I take B = 0.38.

CORRELATION: strongly positive, +0.45 to +0.50 across all three seats, and structurally sound — a decade averaging MOVE >=105 IS the fiscal-dominance regime in which sovereigns stop hedging equities. Multiplicative ratio 1.42 (I cap below the seats' 1.5 because B is already elevated). P(B|A) = 0.38 x 1.42 = 0.54.

MULTIPLICATION: 0.33 x 0.54 = 0.178 -> 18.

DIRECTION: MODERATED downward by -4 points (22 -> 18). Conjunct A fell (0.35 -> 0.33) on a signed but sub-2:1 scaling argument; conjunct B fell slightly (0.40 -> 0.38) on the shock-mix conditioning. Both moves are small BY DESIGN, because the evidence base for A is the least verifiable in the exercise and a Bayesian who moves far on it is doing the thing this seat exists to prevent. Net of the two conjuncts I land exactly on Fermi's 18 by a different route.
wave2.cq6_reasoning:
I apply the lexical-priority lock strictly, using MY OWN CQ3 distribution and a 2032-36 OECD-38 GDP-weighted core inflation distribution derived from MY OWN CQ2.

GROWTH MARGINAL, read off my CQ3 (P10 0.6 / P50 1.6 / P90 2.7, implied sigma ~0.82): P(g >= 2.6%) = 0.11; P(g < 2.0%) = Phi(0.49) = 0.69; P(g < 1.7%) = Phi(0.12) = 0.55.

INFLATION MARGINAL FOR THE 2032-36 SUB-WINDOW. This must be derived from my CQ2 conjunct A (0.55 for >=2.50% on a 2027-36 average), and the two Wave-1 seats disagree on the profile's SHAPE, which is the one place I have to arbitrate rather than update. Fermi argues a RISING profile (care Baumol, non-tradable labour scarcity, and the interest claim as the old-age ratio goes 31% -> 40% all strengthen monotonically into the 2030s while Chinese goods deflation and AI services deflation are front-loaded), putting 2032-36 at ~2.55%. Scout argues the OPPOSITE (2027-29 is near-locked hot at ~2.9% by the observed OECD core of 3.6% and energy above 10%, so the later sub-window is COOLER than the ten-year mean). Both are right about their own term and they cancel to first order. I adopt central 2.45% with sigma 0.50, the sigma widened from CQ2's because the AI-Q4 capex-bust branch (66% locked) can produce a genuinely low-inflation digestion period in exactly these years. P(core >= 2.7%) = 0.31; P(core < 2.0%) = 0.18.

STEP 1 — A requires g >= 2.6%. A = 11. CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED: my CQ3 P50 is 1.6% and my P90 is 2.7%, so A is a right-tail event and 11 is precisely P(g >= 2.6) implied by my own stated quantiles. The lock's worked example (a P50 of 2.1% forbidding most mass on A) applies to me a fortiori at 1.6%. I did NOT apply A's qualitative clauses (debt stabilizing via growth, broad wage gains), because rule 1 is a pure growth test; had I applied them — and my CQ1 of 9 says broad wage gains are unlikely — A would be lower, so 11 is an upper bound.

STEP 2 — C requires core >= 2.7% AND g < 2.0%. Unconditional product 0.69 x 0.31 = 0.214. I raise the conditional from 0.31 to 0.35 because in MY effort the binding constraints are supply walls, which make low growth and high core inflation the SAME event rather than opposing ones: energy inflation "stabilised above 10%", the US electrician deficit ~107,000 peaking 2027 against BLS shortfalls of ~81,000/yr THROUGH 2034, care vacancies clearing by rationing with Baumol cost disease against a strained public payer. 0.69 x 0.35 = 0.241 -> C = 24. Offsetting that lift, and why I do not go to Fermi's 28: the capex-bust branch produces low growth with LOW inflation, which populates D instead, so the two low-growth mechanisms partly cancel.

STEP 3 — D requires g < 1.7% AND core < 2.0%, disjoint from C by construction. Unconditional product 0.55 x 0.18 = 0.099. I raise the conditional from 0.18 to 0.28: that cell is over-populated by the AI-Q4 impairment branch (66% locked) landing as deflationary digestion, by BIS AER 2026 Box C's labour-income demand deficit, and by imported Chinese goods deflation (my own CQ2 conjunct B at 0.67). 0.55 x 0.28 = 0.154 -> D = 15. D also requires the bust's deflationary digestion to still be suppressing BOTH growth and inflation in 2032-36 rather than in 2028-31, which is roughly a one-in-four conditional and is what keeps D from running to 22.

STEP 4 — B is the residual: 100 - 11 - 24 - 15 = 50. SUM = 100 exactly.

CONSISTENCY CHECK AGAINST MY OWN CQ2, EXPLICITLY: my CQ2 = 32 is a JOINT (OECD hot AND China cold) and so must sit below my OECD-only conjunct-A marginal of 0.55; it does. That 0.55 for >=2.50% over 2027-36 maps, under the cancelling-profile argument above, to a 2032-36 central of 2.45%, which places 31% above C's higher 2.7% trigger — necessarily below 0.55 because the threshold is higher, which is the arithmetic link. Multiplied by P(g < 2.0) = 0.69 and lifted for supply-wall co-occurrence, that yields C = 24. C is therefore DERIVED from my CQ2 and my CQ3, not asserted. Sensitivity: had I used Fermi's rising-profile central of 2.55% with sigma 0.50, P(core >= 2.7) would be 0.36 and C would be 25; had I used Scout's cooler read with P(>=2.7) = 0.28, C would be 22. The answer is insensitive to that arbitration within +/-2 points, which is why I did not spend more credence on resolving it.

THE TAXONOMY FINDING, which the lock forces into the open and which I report as Fermi does: my modal cell is B at 50, but it is reached as a RESIDUAL at a growth rate of ~1.6%/yr — BELOW B's own stated 1.7-2.5% band — routed there because inflation sits between 2.0% and 2.7% and so triggers neither C nor D. Substantively that is still the bifurcated barbell (physical/care scarcity and hyperscaler rents coexisting with white-collar compression and steep real term premia), but half my mass sits in a cell whose LABEL implies about 1pp more growth than I forecast. Any aggregation that reads B as "growth 1.7-2.5%" will misread this payload.

DIRECTION: relative to the Historian's prior (15/54/15/16), my updating MODERATED A down -4, AMPLIFIED C up +9, held D at -1, and moved B -4. The C move is the one that matters and it comes from the supply-wall conditioning, not from a higher inflation level — my inflation central of 2.45% is below Fermi's 2.55%.

hypothesis_critique.a: The load-bearing word is "smoothly", and it fails on a conversion rate, not on a direction. PRIOR 5 (Historian) / 7 (Fermi) / 6 (Scout) — unusually tight, so there was little for me to update. The arithmetic: Fermi's stock-flow gives 0.77M/yr displaced J/K/M against a 1.66M/yr Q need with ~15% convertible = ~7% coverage; the Historian's displaced-worker reference classes give a cross-occupational reallocation elasticity of 0.05-0.10 into health/social care (~5-8% of displaced US manufacturing workers 1999-2011, ~2-4% of UK ex-miners 1984-94). Every frictional term compounds the same way: a 1-year LPN to 2-4-year RN licensing queue with clinical placement slots rather than instructors binding (Scout: nursing faculty vacancies ~7%, nearly 1,700 unfilled, 2026 NSI via AACN; Canadian credentialing "six months to two years"; German recognition plus B1-B2 language; NCLEX first-time pass 88.6%/91.2%/86.7% for 2023/2024/2025 with internationally-educated-nurse pass rates "steadily declining since 2010" per Health Affairs), ~6-8% of new RN licensees aged 40+ against a displaced median in the mid-40s, an 85-90% female care workforce against a 55-60% male displaced pool, a 1.6-1.9x reservation-wage gap, geographic immobility against housing costs, and nursing-assistant musculoskeletal injury rates ~3x the all-worker BLS rate. The robot escape hatch is closed too, and that is the one number I take from the simulation at a defensible LR: 0.39-0.66% of workers' worth of installed robot stock world-wide by 2036 even in its most aggressive automation scenario, against a care need of 3.0% of OECD-38 employment. No signal in the Scout's telemetry moves this above single digits; the reallocation happens through non-employment and output forgone, not through a transfer. POSTERIOR 5, essentially unmoved — the rare plank where the base rate and the telemetry agree.
hypothesis_critique.b: Two words carry the failure and they fail differently. "Blocks" is the wrong mechanism: the observed compression is on the ELASTICITY margin, not the level — India IT-BPM at +6.1% revenue against +2.3% headcount (Nasscom ASR 2026; CAVEAT PRESERVED: industry-body projection, not audited), Philippine CC-BPM +4% to 1.68M workers (industry association with a directional interest). Revenue growing while headcount decouples is AI thinning the per-dollar labour content of a still-growing export, which is not blockage. "Severely" is the wrong magnitude, and here the physical leg runs in the OPPOSITE direction, which is the whole point of my effort's brief: OECD demand for physical healthcare, nursing and skilled-trade migrants is expanding (Japan ~250,000 nursing-care shortfall in FY2026 rising to ~570,000 by FY2040, with only 28,400 foreign nationals holding specified-skilled-worker status for nursing care at end-2023, "just over half the government's target"; ~122,000 Indian-trained nurses already in OECD countries; "one in six nurses in high-income countries was trained abroad"; Germany projected 350,000-500,000 care shortfall by 2035 — CAVEAT PRESERVED: that last is workvisa.guide, a COMMERCIAL IMMIGRATION GUIDE, not official). PRIOR 14 (Historian: ~0 of 3 "automation destroys offshoring" claims resolved true within a decade; virtual-leg counterfactual loss -$90B to -$160B/yr for India and -300-550k Philippine jobs against a physical-leg gain of only ~$10-25B/yr, so net income negative but nowhere near collapse). EVIDENCE: Philippine remittances at a record $35.634B for 2025 with BSP forecasting $36.6B for 2026 — hard central-bank data, and directly contradictory to "severely". LR = P(record remittances 2025-26 | severe suffering by 2036) / P(same | not) = 0.40/0.70 = 0.57, i.e. ~1.75:1 against. BELOW my 2:1 bar and flagged, so applied at a discount. The binding constraint on the physical leg is policy, not demand (foreign-born share of OECD nurses rose only ~14% -> ~16% over 2010-2020 despite documented shortages), which caps the offset without reversing its sign. POSTERIOR 12. Net: income positive-to-neutral, composition negative, severity absent.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failure is in "then falls", and it is a level claim masquerading as a direction claim. The first clause is nearly observed and I score it high: OECD core "remained stable at 3.6% for the third consecutive month" with headline 4.3% y/y (Aug 2026), energy inflation "stabilised above 10%", euro-area headline flash "up 0.6 p.p. to 3.8% - its highest level since September 2023". PRIOR SPREAD IS THE WIDEST IN THE PANEL — Historian 42, Scout 33, Fermi 15 — and the spread is purely a reading dispute about what "falls" means. On my own numbers inflation DOES fall: a 2027-29 run of ~2.9% against my 2032-36 central of 2.45%. But it falls to a level still above target, so the plank is true as a direction and false as the benign-2030s story a reader will take from it. Fermi's 15 reads "falls" as "returns to target" and prices the monotonically strengthening terms against it (care/construction Baumol at +0.20pp, fiscal-dominance tolerance at +0.25pp as the net interest claim goes 2% -> 3% of GDP, non-tradable labour scarcity at +0.25pp as labour supply runs -0.1%/yr against in-person service demand +1.5%/yr); the Historian's 42 prices the mechanical fall and the strong inflation-targeting-era base rate of reversion. The genuine two-sided content is that 2A contains BOTH signs — Goodhart-Pradhan aging-as-inflationary against BIS AER 2026 Box C aging-and-automation-as-demand-shortfall — and the AI-Q4 capex bust at 66% is a real disinflationary channel that could deliver the plank for a reason the plank does not name. POSTERIOR 26: MODERATED down -16 from the Historian's prior, because the supply walls with build times past 2034 (electrician deficit ~107,000 peaking 2027 against BLS shortfalls of ~81,000/yr through 2034) do not clear on a cyclical timetable and the plank's implicit mechanism is cyclical.
hypothesis_critique.d: Two words fail, in sequence. "Eventually" smuggles in a horizon the question does not grant — this resolves Dec 31 2036, and nothing in the locked set makes an exponential arrive inside eleven years; a plank that is only true after the resolution date is false as scored. "Wins" is the harder failure, and it is arithmetic: Fermi's product of China's 0.375-0.38 PPP weight with the locked -2.7pp/yr aging drag is -1.03pp of coupled growth, and adding OECD working-age contraction plus the Baumol composition wedge (-0.25 to -0.40pp) means the demographic block subtracts roughly 3-4x what the AI block adds. Taking AI-Q6's OWN regime midpoints gives an expected AI TFP contribution of only +0.304pp/yr (0.162 x 0.70 + 0.472 x 0.35 + 0.365 x 0.07). The capex channel does not rescue it either: ~0.55pp of GDP in incremental AI/grid investment (104 GW of IT load at 70% utilization and $30-35M/MW, plus ~$250B/yr of grid) yields only +0.04 to +0.06pp/yr of growth at K/Y = 3.0 and alpha = 0.35, because the existing capital stock is vast, alpha is a third, and 3-5 year GPU lives make most gross spend replacement rather than deepening. A capex boom enormous in dollars is near-trivial in growth accounting. My own CQ3 P50 of 1.6% and CQ6-A of 11 pin this directly. PRIOR 18 (Historian) / 14 (Fermi) / 11 (Scout). POSTERIOR 13, MODERATED down -5 from the prior, with the move driven entirely by the weight-times-drag product that two independent seats reproduce and that one of them ties back to a locked 2A marginal.
