wave2.coupling_tension:
The sharpest coupling tension is a SCISSORS between AI-Q2 and AI-Q1, and I report it with a likelihood ratio rather than as an assertion, because the three Wave-1 seats reached it from three mutually exclusive evidence bases: the Historian from a one-directional historical base rate (Japan, Korea and Germany led industrial robot density precisely as their workforces aged; EU enterprise cloud adoption ~19% in 2014 to ~45% in 2023 makes a quadrupling of a firm-adoption measure in twelve years close to a coin flip before any scarcity push), Fermi from a mechanism (marginal value = payoff x labour share x GDP per worker, so a scarcer and dearer worker raises MV mechanically, with OECD hours at -0.05%/yr and Chinese working-age at -1.15%/yr), and the Scout from 2026 telemetry (Japan running a ~250,000 FY2026 nursing-care shortfall against 28,400 foreign specified-skilled-worker caregivers at end-2023, "just over half the government's target"; US electrician deficit ~107,000 peaking 2027 against BLS shortfalls of ~81,000/yr through 2034; construction wages +5.2% y/y against +3.2% private sector). LR = P(three independent lenses converge on the same signed wedge | the wedge is real) / P(same | not real) = 0.60/0.15 = 4.0. This is the only likelihood ratio in my payload comfortably above 4:1 and it is the one place I update hard.

DIRECTION AND SIZE. AI-Q2 (OECD-38 firm adoption >= 50% by 2036, 21.3% raw) is TOO LOW once demographics are endogenous; the three seats recommend 28-31, 26-29 and 30-34, and I adopt ~30. AI-Q1 (PPP-weighted TFP lift >= +0.50pp/yr, 23.0% raw) is TOO HIGH and must NOT rise with it; I adopt ~19-20. The mechanism is that aging raises the NUMBER of firms using AI while lowering the economy-wide productivity those firms can register, because the binding input shifts from cognition, which AI supplies, to licensed physically-present hours and grid interconnection capacity, which it does not. Two separable subtractions: composition, where moving ~3pp of OECD hours into a care sector at ~0.15%/yr measured labour productivity subtracts 0.03-0.05pp/yr of aggregate TFP as pure accounting that the exogenous-demographics framing cannot see; and crowding-out of the PUBLIC COMPLEMENTS diffusion actually needs — grid interconnection, transformer capacity, clinical placement slots, licensure throughput, skills funding — by the fiscal facts locked in 2A (net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP; Chinese pension subsidies already ~2.9T RMB, ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure, rising as worker/retiree goes 4.4 -> 2.8). Coupling therefore drives a WEDGE: adoption up, measured TFP flat-to-down. That is Hulten's ceiling arriving through demography rather than through anything about the technology, and it is precisely the "Jagged Diffusion and Hyperscaler Rent Concentration" cell — so AI-Q6 mass should move from BOTH tails into the middle: Transformative Breakout from 16.2% down to ~11-12, Jagged Diffusion from 47.2% up to ~52-53, Hulten Ceiling from 36.5% to ~35-36. Note the Wave-1 seats DISAGREE on the Hulten direction (the Historian raises it, Fermi lowers it); I split toward flat and flag that this is arbitration, not updating.

THREE SMALLER TENSIONS, all in the same direction of travel. AI-Q5 (J/K/M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA falling >= 3.5pp, 38.2% raw) is TOO LOW, to ~45, for a DENOMINATOR reason that exogenous demographics hides: a shrinking cognitive-worker entry cohort does not rescue the SHARE, because the denominator is sectoral GVA and that GVA is inflated by hyperscaler rents booked inside ISIC J, while endogenous demographics retire the most expensive senior cohort at the same time AI blocks the entry-level replacement flow — the numerator falls from both ends. CAVEAT PRESERVED: the US labour-share telemetry supporting this is a mess of non-comparable measures and periods (54.1% "down from 55.3% a year ago" and "the lowest level since the US government began tracking it following World War II", S&P Global Jun 30 2026; 53.7% nonfarm business Q1 2026; 52.8% EY-Parthenon; 51.4% on a gross-domestic-income basis "down from 58% in 1980"), with the Tax Foundation finding the labour share "remains within historical levels" and Goldman's Duggirala arguing "the decline has been less steep than BLS data suggests" — so I cap this revision at +7pp rather than the Scout's +10. AI-Q4 (impairments, 66.0% raw) should rise to ~73: the Historian's capex-supercycle base rate is the strongest single piece of evidence here (UK railway mania 1845-50; US nuclear 1974-84 with roughly 120 of ~250 ordered plants cancelled; telecom/fibre 1999-2002 with the great majority of laid fibre dark; Japan 1986-91; US shale 2014-20 with ~$300B of write-downs — about 5 of 5 episodes impaired >= 20%), and coupling adds to it through the cost of capital, since 2A's own starting point is $650B of debt against $300B of equity in the circular commitments and the public-dissaving plus convenience-yield terms alone put r* up ~55bp. The Scout's counter — that scarcity-forced adoption is demand-validated by a wage bill it actually replaces — applies only to the physical/care slice, the smallest part of the ~$1.4T stack, so I hold short of the Historian's 78-84. AI-Q3 is the ONE place an independent model corroborates a locked marginal rather than contradicting it: its P90 of 1,573.8 TWh at $80/MWh against ~$130T of combined PPP GDP is an electricity-bill ceiling of 0.097% of GDP, almost exactly the willingness-to-pay cap the simulation implements at 0.05%; the locked prior and the model agree on the MECHANISM (price-capped load) and differ only ~2x on the level.

THE AGGREGATE TENSION, whose direction is unambiguous and runs toward LOWER coupled growth. AI-Q6 places 63.4% of mass on TFP lifts of >= +0.15pp/yr and its own regime midpoints imply an expected AI contribution of +0.304pp/yr. But China's 0.375 PPP weight times the locked -2.7pp/yr drag is -1.03pp, and OECD working-age contraction plus the Baumol composition wedge adds -0.25 to -0.40pp, so inside the 2032-36 window the demographic block subtracts roughly 3-4x what the AI block adds. No reading of 2B held exogenous reconciles with 2A's demographic arithmetic at the coupled-growth level a reader would infer from the CQ6 regime labels, and nothing in the coupling runs the other way at the aggregate. The operational consequence for downstream aggregation: the coupled joint contains a cell the standalone marginals treat as near-empty — WIDE adoption with LOW measured TFP — and any aggregation that imposes a positive AI-Q1/AI-Q2 correlation will systematically under-weight it. That cell is my CQ6-B at 50 and my CQ3 P50 of 1.6%, and because the lock routes me into B as a RESIDUAL at a growth rate BELOW B's own stated 1.7-2.5% band, half my probability mass sits in a cell whose label overstates my growth forecast by about 1pp.

wave2.lens_self_description: I answered only as a premortem red-teamer: I took the three Wave-1 payloads as the object of attack rather than as evidence, hunted for the assumption all three shared and never tested, and wrote both tails as completed histories — which forbade me from building any independent base-rate table, any fresh telemetry scan, or any growth-accounting sum of my own except where it was needed to show that a Wave-1 number double-counts, mis-specifies its measurement object, or applies a locked prior in only one direction.
wave2.cq1_reasoning: THE SINGLE STRONGEST SHARED ASSUMPTION ACROSS ALL THREE WAVE-1 PANELISTS, and the thing none of them questioned: that the OECD care shortfall clears by QUANTITY RATIONING rather than by price, evidenced by 25 years of documented shortages with no relative real wage gain. P1 calls it "a 25-year base rate of non-clearing"; P2 makes it the hinge ("the system rations instead"); P3 makes it driver #5. All three then infer marginal B = 0.18-0.20. THE ATTACK: the 1998-2024 non-clearing record is a record of a regime in which the employer had a LEGAL OPTION to run short. That option is being closed inside the resolution window by binding minimum-staffing law — CMS nursing-home staffing minima, EU and national nurse-to-patient ratio statutes, Japanese and Korean kaigo ratio rules. A ratio mandate converts a quantity constraint into a PRICE OBLIGATION: if you must legally hold N licensed hours per bed and the licensing queue means you cannot recruit them, you bid for incumbents or you close beds, and closing beds is politically unavailable at a 40%+ increase in the 80+ cohort. Rationing was an equilibrium because it was legal; the premortem question is whether it stays legal, and Wave 1 never asked. SECOND ATTACK — ASYMMETRIC USE OF THE COMPOSITION ARGUMENT. P2 (point 3, "the decisive point") and P3 (driver #1) both argue AI removes the bottom of J+K+M, so the surviving J+K+M MEDIAN rises, raising B's bar. Correct, and both then apply the symmetric logic to F+Q in ONE direction only (migrant and new-entrant inflow pulls the F+Q median down). Within-F+Q composition runs the other way over 2025-36 and they discarded it: in Q the acuity mix shifts from low-paid aide hours to credentialed hospital/skilled-nursing hours as 80+ grows fastest, and the licensing queue they both invoke GUARANTEES the marginal F+Q hire is credentialed rather than an aide — a queue cannot be cleared by unskilled inflow by construction; in F, P3's own telemetry (construction +5.2% y/y vs +3.2% private, ~32% data-centre premium, electrician deficit ~107k peaking 2027 against ~81k/yr BLS shortfalls through 2034) is a within-F upward median shift driven by the electrification build. A median-of-median differential is a composition race, and Wave 1 ran it with the F+Q leg handicapped. THIRD ATTACK — CONJUNCT A IS MIS-ESTIMATED DOWNWARD, worst in P1 (0.40) and P2 (0.52), best in P3 (0.60). P1's reference class is the OECD total-area series 1999-2016, which prices in pre-reform continental European unemployment regimes that no longer generate the data; and the test is a FIVE-YEAR MEAN, which is forgiving. Arithmetic: from a 5.0% level drifting to ~4.7% on the locked denominator shrinkage, a window containing a 2020-severity event (OECD annual peak ~7.1% for ONE year) prints 4.7/4.7/6.8/5.8/5.0 = 5.40%, i.e. it still CLEARS. Only two recessions, or one recession plus a persistent displacement shelf, breaks A. MARGINAL A = 0.65. MARGINAL B = 0.33 (ratio-mandate price obligation + two-sided composition + the AI-Q5-consistent displacement wage signal). CORRELATION: Wave 1 used +0.15 to +0.35; I use +0.55, because the single state that drives both is binding labour scarcity under a shrinking denominator, and the ratio mandate makes the F+Q bid countercyclical (statutory minima do not relax in a downturn). P(B|A) = 0.40. JOINT = 0.65 x 0.40 = 0.26 -> 26, roughly 2x the Wave-1 centre of 12.3, with the whole deviation attributable to one legal-regime change and one discarded composition leg.
wave2.cq2_reasoning: Wave 1 is widest here (18 / 31 / 43), so there is no unanimous assumption to destroy — but there is a shared STRUCTURAL claim held by all three with the same sign: that the two conjuncts fight each other via Chinese exported deflation (P1 near-zero-to-negative, P2 explicitly rho = -0.20 and "the divergence is partly self-undermining", P3 -0.10). ATTACK ON THE CORRELATION SIGN: the pass-through from Chinese producer deflation to OECD core requires an open trade channel, and the channel is being closed by exactly the policy regime that 2A's fiscal stress makes more likely, not less. Tariff walls, CBAM-style border pricing, de-risking content rules and reshoring subsidy decouple the two price levels mechanically: Chinese excess capacity then clears into non-OECD markets and into domestic price cuts, while the OECD pays a protected price for the same good. 2018-2026 is the observed form of this. Under that regime the correlation is ZERO to slightly POSITIVE: the SAME coupled state — China in a demographic-contraction/deleveraging trap, the OECD in a labour-scarce fiscal-dominance regime behind a trade wall — produces both conjuncts. Wave 1 treated them as two draws that compete; they are one state. THE STRONGEST UNEXPLOITED OBSERVATION IN THE ENTIRE WAVE-1 SET is P3's arithmetic advantage, which P1 and P2 both ignore and P3 himself under-prices. OBSERVED: OECD core 3.6% for three consecutive months (OECD, 6 Oct 2026); OECD headline 4.3% y/y Aug 2026; energy inflation stabilised above 10%; euro area core 2.5% and rising, headline flash 3.8%, highest since Sep 2023. The question averages TEN years starting Jan 2027. If 2027-29 lands at ~2.8% GDP-weighted (near-locked by momentum, energy, tariff pass-through and the care/construction wedge), the remaining seven years need only (25.0 - 8.4)/7 = 2.37% to clear 2.50% — barely above target, and a FULL RETURN TO TARGET STILL CLEARS NOTHING WORSE THAN A COIN FLIP. P1's 0.35 marginal is the clearest case of anchoring on a reference class (inflation-targeting-era 10-year windows) in preference to a near-determined first third of the actual window. MARGINAL A = 0.68. CONJUNCT B: I accept Wave 1's range and take the midpoint of P2 (0.66) and P3 (0.72) = 0.68; the Japan 1995-2020 persistence class plus the locked -60M and 4.4->2.8 worker/retiree is the strongest piece of Wave-1 reasoning and I do not dispute it. CORRELATION: +0.02 effective (tariff decoupling slightly reinforcing). JOINT = 0.68 x 0.68 x 1.03 = 0.476 -> 48. Note what this does NOT say: 48 is not a stagflation forecast. It is a statement that the first third of a ten-year average is already in the data and that Wave 1 priced the window as if it began today.
wave2.cq3_reasoning: THE DECISIVE SHARED ERROR, and it is arithmetic, not judgment: all three panelists treat the locked IMF aging drag as a SUBTRACTION FROM AN OBSERVED OR NEAR-OBSERVED GROWTH RATE. It is a COUNTERFACTUAL DECOMPOSITION over 2025-2050 against a no-aging world, and most of it is already realized in the data they start from. P2 commits the error in the cleanest possible form: "a frictionless China counterfactual of ~4.7%/yr less the locked -2.7 pp = 2.0%", where 4.7% is a figure already produced by an economy whose working-age population has been shrinking since 2012, whose property sector has already deleveraged, and whose pension subsidy is already 10.1% of fiscal expenditure. He then calls 0.38 x (-2.7) = -1.03 pp "larger in absolute value than every AI channel in this payload combined" and makes it the dominant arithmetic of his entire payload. P3 does the same in softer form ("aging alone -2.7pp/yr for China") while nonetheless landing China at 2.8%. P1 reaches 1.95% by extrapolating a monotone decline that is itself largely the same already-realized aging. The correct comparator is a forecast that already prices aging: official medium-term China projections in the ~3.0-3.5%/yr range for the early 2030s are NOT 5.7% minus 2.7%. I take China = 3.3%/yr. SECOND DOUBLE-COUNT: the Baumol composition wedge. P2 subtracts -0.03, P3 subtracts -0.15, P1 embeds it in the Hulten story. But 2A's locked "cuts baseline OECD real GDP per capita growth by ~40%, from 1.0 to 0.6, absent productivity offsets" IS the OECD's own aging-drag calculation, and sectoral reallocation into low-productivity care is the principal mechanism inside it. Subtracting it again on top of the locked 0.6% books the same effect twice. THIRD — THE LOCKED PRIOR'S WEIGHTING CONVENTION IS UNSTATED AND ALL THREE ANCHORED ON IT ANYWAY. "OECD real GDP per capita growth 1.0 -> 0.6%/yr" carries no weighting convention. CQ3 demands a PPP-WEIGHTED OECD-38 + China aggregate. ~26% of OECD-38 PPP GDP sits in members whose old-age ratio is nowhere near 39-41% — Mexico, Turkiye, Korea, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Israel — and the US alone is ~43% with the best large-member demographics and productivity. If the locked 0.6% is a member-average rather than a PPP-weighted aggregate, PPP-reweighting is worth +0.2 to +0.3 pp and NOT ONE Wave-1 panelist adjusted for it. MY OECD-38 LEG: 0.6 locked per-capita + 0.25 PPP-reweighting + 0.18 PPP-weighted population growth + 0.30 AI TFP (the locked AI-Q6 regime-mix EV, same number P2 and P3 compute) - 0.00 Baumol (double-count removed) - 0.03 fiscal consolidation = 1.30%/yr. BLEND at w_China 0.37: 0.63 x 1.30 + 0.37 x 3.30 = 0.82 + 1.22 = 2.04 -> P50 2.1%/yr. ATTACK ON P2'S USE OF THE SIMULATION. P2 is the only Fermi seat and he read the model correctly in refusing its level (2.95% baseline) and taking only its robot bound; his diagnostic is also the sharpest thing in Wave 1. But his conclusion that the model is "labour-insensitive by construction" is over-read, and his claimed weight agreement is a coincidence that hides a composition disagreement. (i) gamma = 0.55 on useful energy against a mainstream cost-share gamma of 0.05-0.08 means every growth number in that model is a second-law-efficiency forecast wearing growth-accounting clothes; serviceEfficiencyGrowth is documented as the dominant GDP dial (~1.8x per plausible range). Any bound read off it is a bound on an energy-efficiency parameter, in EITHER direction, not evidence about demography. (ii) The UN WPP LOW demographic path biases its labour path DOWN, so its 2.95% is a LOWER bound conditional on its own closure — P2 says this, then uses the model's 2.95% only as something his 1.5% must be defended against, which is the wrong direction of inference. (iii) THE REGIONAL PROXY IS NOT THE QUESTION'S OBJECT AND ITS BIAS IS AMBIGUOUS, NOT NEUTRAL: the adapter proxies OECD-38 by us + oecd-ex-us, which EXCLUDES Japan, Korea and Turkiye (seasia/mena) and Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica (latam) while INCLUDING non-OECD states inside oecd-ex-us. Dropping Japan biases the proxy's growth UP; dropping Turkiye, Mexico and Korea biases it DOWN. P2's "the adapter's own weights (0.629/0.371) agree to within 1 pp despite a different regional partition, so the weighting is not where the model and I diverge" is exactly backwards as a reassurance: identical weights over non-identical country sets is where an unexamined composition error hides, not where it is ruled out. (iv) The model's China at 3.81%/yr — which P2 dismisses as "simply does not implement the locked -2.7pp" — is, under my first attack, approximately the RIGHT ORDER for an aging-inclusive China path, and its agreement with official medium-term projections is the one place the model corroborates rather than contradicts. P2 rejected the model's China number for the same reason his own China number is wrong. PREMORTEM, UPSIDE: it is Dec 31 2036 and coupled growth printed 3.1%/yr, far above the Wave-1 centre of 1.68%. What happened: the locked healthy-aging capacity gain ("70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000", 41 countries, N ~ 1M, +0.4 pp/yr to global growth) was treated by every Wave-1 seat as a rounding term inside an hours calculation (+0.25%/yr participation in P2) rather than as the growth contribution 2A actually states — and it arrived as a participation surge in the 60-74 band once statutory retirement ages extended with life expectancy, because the binding constraint on older-worker participation was never capability, it was pension-accrual cliffs, which fiscal strain forced countries to flatten. The labour-scarcity demand pull that ALL THREE Wave-1 seats conceded (every one of them moved AI-Q2 up) showed up in measured TFP after all, because the 2015-22 TFP baseline they all used as the counterfactual was itself depressed by the slack labour market that aging then removed. China did not get the -2.7 pp subtracted twice. Tariff-walled OECD manufacturing investment and the grid build raised measured capital deepening above the +0.35 pp everyone assumed. Coupled growth cleared 2.6% and CQ6-A resolved. PREMORTEM, DOWNSIDE: it printed 0.9%/yr, below every Wave-1 P10 but P1's. What happened: the AI-Q4 impairment landed in 2029-31 and the digestion ran through the entire resolution window; the grid interconnection and transformer queues that were supposed to be the bottleneck turned out to be the CAUSE, because the electricity needed for the buildout was never built and the write-down took the capital stock with it; China's pension-subsidy claim went from 10.1% of fiscal expenditure to a hard financing event; the eroding sovereign convenience yield from 2A became a funding cost that killed the long-duration capital formation on both legs at once; and the BIS Box C demand shortfall was realized exactly as written — displaced cognitive labour income never recovered, the care transfer was refused, and the rationed care hours showed up as forgone output in the measured aggregate. P10 1.0 / P90 3.3 is deliberately WIDER than every Wave-1 interval on the upside because the above-tail is the one all three structurally suppressed.
wave2.cq4_reasoning: Wave 1 clusters tightly (2.0 / 2.1 / 2.2) and P2 found the one measurement error that matters: the locked 2.60% TIPS print is US-ONLY, and the G7 GDP-weighted object the question asks for is ~1.71-1.90% today. I go materially higher, to 2.5%, on three grounds Wave 1 either suppressed or got backwards. (1) MY OWN CQ3 FORCES IT, AND THIS IS A CONSISTENCY CONSTRAINT WAVE 1 ESCAPED BY FORECASTING LOW GROWTH. 2A locks global (r - g) worsening by ~+1.0 pp. P3 is the only seat that checks it, and he checks it the easy way: OECD g ~0.95 with r = 2.2 gives r-g ~ +1.25, which "matches rather than contradicts". P90 3.9 is deliberately above every Wave-1 P90 (3.1 / 3.3 / 3.4) because the fiscal-dominance tail is the one the locked priors describe most concretely (3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117% of GDP, +2.4 pp under a 20% AI-led equity shock, basis-trade absorption replacing price-insensitive convenience-yield demand) and because that tail is convex — the term premium and the convenience-yield erosion compound. P10 1.2 holds the downside premortem: the capex bust plus BIS demand deficit plus a repression response, which is where my own numbers are most vulnerable. I take P2's directional reading off the simulation and accept his refusal of its level: a model whose rate moves +0.87 pp for fiscal/political stress and +0.09 pp for the strongest technology regime says to put the variance in the fiscal and term-premium terms, which is what the 2.7 pp span between my P10 and P90 does.
wave2.cq5_reasoning: Wave 1 (22 / 18 / 15) converges on one genuinely good insight — that the modal >=25% drawdown generator in this prior set (AI-Q4 at 66%) is DISINFLATIONARY and therefore fails the bond leg — and on one shared measurement error. THE ERROR: all three evaluate the bond leg as if it asked "did bonds hedge over the episode", when it asks whether G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominals FAIL TO FALL 50 bp (or rise 25 bp) DURING THE EQUITY DRAWDOWN WINDOW, i.e. measured from the equity PEAK to the equity TROUGH. P1 classifies 1987, 1990, 2000-02, 2008-09 and 2020 as flight-to-quality and gets 3 of 8. But peak-to-trough yield change dated off the EQUITY peak is a different statistic from the one that reference class encodes: in a regime where a yield shock is the trigger, nominals are higher at the equity peak's far side for most of the window and the eventual rally arrives after the trough. 1987 is the canonical case — yields rose from the August equity peak through early October. Re-dating raises P1's conditional from 0.38 and raises P2's branch-weighted 0.43. SECOND: P2's own branch table contains the escape hatch he then discounts. He gives the hybrid branch (yield-up shock then later rally) weight 0.20 and P(B2) = 0.50. Under peak-to-trough dating the hybrid branch resolves TRUE much more often than half the time, because the yield-up leg is what dates the equity peak. I take P(B2|B1) = 0.33 against his 0.43 only because I simultaneously raise B1. THIRD: CONJUNCT A IS UNDER-ESTIMATED, worst by P3 (0.30) and P1 (0.35). MOVE is 1-month implied Treasury yield vol in annualized bp and scales roughly as k x yield level x path dispersion. At my CQ4 P50 of 2.5% real the G7-weighted nominal 10y is ~4.7-5.1%, materially above the level P2 used (4.3-4.7) and far above the 2015-19 regime that anchors P1's and P3's sub-105 means. MARGINAL A = 0.55. B1 = 0.62 (I accept P2's mechanism build: AI names ~35-40% of MSCI World cap, ~$1.4T circular commitments on ~$300B equity, plus the non-AI triggers 2A names separately). P(B) = 0.62 x 0.33 = 0.205. CORRELATION +0.50, as all three agree and for the reason all three give. P(B|A) = 0.205 x 1.5 = 0.31. JOINT = 0.55 x 0.31 = 0.169. I then add a 9 pp uplift for one thing no Wave-1 seat priced: the two conjuncts are generated by the SAME fiscal-dominance state in a way that makes the correlation uplift larger than a multiplicative 1.5 tilt captures — conditional on a decade averaging MOVE >=105, the probability that at least one of ~1.4 expected drawdowns is a bond-non-hedging episode is better modelled as a Poisson over a changed regime than as a single conditional. 0.169 -> 0.26 -> 26. Above all three, and the whole deviation is in the dating convention and the level arithmetic, not in the story.
wave2.cq6_reasoning: CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED EXPLICITLY, in lexical-priority order, against my own CQ3 and CQ2. INFLATION MARGINAL FOR THE 2032-36 SUB-WINDOW: I side with P3 against P2 on the PROFILE. hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the entire failure, and here Wave 1 (5/7/6) is right for the right reasons; a red team that inflates this score to be different is being contrarian rather than adversarial. The plank requires a flow identity to hold with a conversion rate near 1 across a stock-flow discontinuity: a 45-year-old displaced paralegal and a nursing entrant are different people, and the measured cross-occupational reallocation elasticity into health/social care from displaced-worker cohorts is ~0.05-0.10, i.e. one care entrant per 10-20 displaced cognitive workers. Add a 1-4 year licensing queue whose binding capacity is clinical placement slots and faculty (~7% faculty vacancy, nearly 1,700 unfilled), an ~85-90% female care workforce against a ~55-60% male displaced pool, and nursing-assistant injury rates ~3x the all-worker rate. But note what "smoothly" being false does NOT imply, and where I split from Wave 1: a non-smooth supply response is a PRICE event, not only a shortfall. The plank's failure is evidence FOR my CQ1 wage conjunct, not against it, which is why I score (a) at 6 and CQ1 at 26 while Wave 1 scored (a) at ~6 and CQ1 at ~12. Wave 1 treated the same fact as doubly bearish.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail, in opposite directions, and Wave 1 (14/12/14) got the right answer by an incomplete route. "BLOCKS" is simply false as a mechanism claim: AI compresses the VIRTUAL leg on the elasticity margin (revenue per head rising faster than headcount: India IT-BPM +6.1% revenue vs +2.3% headcount; Philippine CC-BPM still growing +4% to ~1.68M) while the PHYSICAL leg is expanding under policy and demographic pressure that has nothing to do with AI (Japan ~250k FY2026 care shortfall heading to ~570k FY2040 against only 28,400 specified-skilled-worker caregivers at end-2023, "just over half the government's target"; ~122k Indian-trained nurses already in the OECD; one in six nurses in high-income countries trained abroad; remittances at a record $35.634B in 2025 with BSP forecasting $36.6B for 2026). A channel growing in headcount is not blocked. "SEVERELY" fails on the net and also on a term Wave 1 omitted: Indian IT-BPM is the supplier of AI-enabled delivery, so part of the counterfactual virtual loss is recaptured as AI-services revenue inside the same firms — the compression is a margin and mix event, not a volume collapse. I score 8, below all three, because Wave 1 priced "blocks" as merely overstated when it is directionally wrong for the physical leg and mechanically wrong for the virtual one. The honest residual risk that keeps it above 3: the physical leg is policy-rationed (OECD foreign-born nurse share moved only ~14% -> ~16% over 2010-2020 despite shortages), so the net income gain is small even though the sign is positive — and the COMPOSITION shift from high-wage virtual work to lower-wage physical migration is a real welfare loss that the plank describes badly rather than falsely.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, and this is where I split hardest from P2 (15) and P3 (33) and land near P1 (42). The plank's first half is nearly observed, not forecast: OECD core at 3.6% for three consecutive months, headline 4.3% y/y, energy inflation above 10%, euro area core 2.5% and rising with headline flash at 3.8% — "runs hot for the next few years" is the present tense. The second half is where it breaks, and it breaks on a LANDING ZONE rather than a direction. Inflation does decline from the 2027-29 shelf; it does not "fall" in the sense a reader takes — back to or below target — because the terms that decline are the front-loaded ones (energy base effects, tariff level shifts, Chinese goods pass-through) while the ones that persist are administered care wages under ratio mandates, the Baumol relative-price wedge, non-tradable labour scarcity under a shrinking denominator, and the fiscal tolerance that a net interest claim going 2% -> 3% of GDP buys. My 2032-36 central of ~2.40% is a fall of ~0.4 pp from the shelf that still sits above target for the whole decade. P2's 15 is the clearest case in this effort of a seat's own build contradicting its plank score: he computes a 2027-36 mean of 2.54% on a RISING profile, which makes plank (c) almost definitionally false, yet the observed 3.6% starting print makes a rising profile the less likely shape. 46.
hypothesis_critique.d: TWO words fail and they fail in different registers. "EVENTUALLY" makes the plank unresolvable inside the Dec 31 2036 horizon — it is a claim about a limit, scored against a window, so any score is a statement about the scorer's horizon rather than about the world; this alone caps it. "WINS" is worse, because it names the wrong relation: AI does not need to outrun population decline. Output is not population. The test that matters is output per worker and output per hour, and a shrinking workforce with constant technology already raises measured labour productivity by composition, which is why the plank's framing — exponential technology racing demographic subtraction — is a category error rather than an empirical question. "OUTRUNS" is the same error restated. I score 22, above all three (18/14/11), because my own coupled P50 of 2.1%/yr with 30 points on CQ6-A says the growth leg does hold up far better than Wave 1's 1.5-1.95% allows, and because the two double-counts I identified are exactly what made Wave 1 score the demographic subtraction as larger than it is. But 22, not 50, because the plank as WORDED would be scored true by a reader on evidence that does not bear on it, and because "exponential" is doing undeclared work: nothing in the locked 2B marginals is exponential — AI-Q6 puts 36.5% on a Hulten ceiling below +0.15 pp/yr.

key_drivers: THE CHINA DOUBLE-SUBTRACTION. All three Wave-1 seats subtract the locked -2.7 pp/yr China aging drag from a growth rate that already embeds a shrinking working-age population, a deleveraged property sector and a 10.1%-of-expenditure pension subsidy. P2 does it explicitly ('frictionless counterfactual 4.7% less 2.7 = 2.0%') and makes the resulting -1.03 pp the dominant arithmetic of his whole payload. The -2.7 pp is a 2025-2050 counterfactual decomposition against a no-aging world, not an adjustment to an aging-inclusive forecast. Correcting it moves China from 2.0-2.8% to ~3.3% and is worth roughly +0.4 pp of coupled growth on its own — the single largest driver of every number I give.

THE BAUMOL DOUBLE-COUNT. 2A's locked 'cuts OECD real GDP per capita growth by ~40%, 1.0 -> 0.6%/yr' IS the OECD's aging-drag calculation, whose principal mechanism is reallocation into low-productivity care. P3 subtracts a further -0.15 pp wedge, P2 -0.03, P1 embeds it in a Hulten story. Booking it twice on top of the locked 0.6% is worth +0.03 to +0.15 pp and, more importantly, is what drove two of three seats to push AI-Q1 DOWN when the correction pushes it up.

RATIO MANDATES AS THE PRICE-CLEARING MECHANISM WAVE 1 NEVER CONSIDERED. The 25-year record of care shortages not clearing through wages is a record of a regime in which running short was LEGAL. Statutory minimum staffing — CMS nursing-home minima, EU and national nurse-patient ratios, Japanese/Korean kaigo rules — converts a quantity constraint into a price obligation that does not relax in a downturn, because the alternative (closing beds) is politically unavailable against a 40%+ rise in the 80+ cohort. This is the whole reason my CQ1 is 26 against a Wave-1 centre of 12.

THE ONE-SIDED COMPOSITION ARGUMENT. P2 and P3 both make 'AI removes the bottom of J+K+M so the surviving median rises' their decisive point, then apply the symmetric logic to F+Q only downward (migrant inflow). Within-F+Q composition runs upward over 2025-36: the licensing queue they invoke GUARANTEES the marginal Q hire is credentialed rather than an aide, acuity shifts toward skilled hours as 80+ grows fastest, and the electrification build is skilled-trade heavy (construction +5.2% y/y vs +3.2% private, ~32% data-centre premium). A median-of-median differential is a composition race run with one leg handicapped.

THE 2027-29 ARITHMETIC ADVANTAGE ON CQ2, UNDER-PRICED BY P1 AND P2. OECD core is observed at 3.6% for three consecutive months with energy above 10%; the ten-year window starts Jan 2027. With 2027-29 near-locked at ~2.8% GDP-weighted, the remaining seven years need only ~2.37% to clear 2.50% — a full return to target still clears. P1's 0.35 marginal is anchoring on an inflation-targeting-era reference class in preference to a near-determined first third of the actual window. Plus a correlation sign error: tariff walls and de-risking DECOUPLE Chinese producer deflation from OECD core, so the required divergence is a mechanism rather than a coincidence.

r-g AS A BINDING CONSTRAINT ON CQ4 THAT LOW-GROWTH FORECASTS ESCAPE. 2A locks global (r-g) worsening by ~+1.0 pp. Raising g without raising r quietly IMPROVES r-g, which the locked prior forbids. My OECD g of 1.30 therefore forces r to ~2.5% — 30-50 bp above all three Wave-1 seats — compounded by treating the financial-repression wedge as a regime artifact of central banks that WANTED duration (1940s-50s, 2010s) rather than a standing capacity available to a central bank running down a balance sheet into the duration supply 2A locks.

wave2.coupling_tension: THE COUPLING TENSION I REPORT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE ONE ALL THREE WAVE-1 SEATS REPORTED, and the disagreement is diagnostic rather than stylistic. All three converge on a scissors: endogenous demographics push AI-Q2 (firm adoption) UP (P1 to 28-31%, P2 to 26-29%, P3 to 30-34%) and AI-Q1 (TFP lift) DOWN (P1 'flat-to-down', P2 to 19-21%, P3 to 18-20%). I accept the AI-Q2 leg — the demand-pull argument is correct, one-directional, and the one place Wave 1 genuinely resisted the drag framing; I would also move AI-Q2 to ~30%, since a firm-count adoption measure quadrupling in twelve years is near a coin flip on comparable diffusion curves before labour scarcity is added. I REJECT the AI-Q1 leg, on two grounds. (1) THE BAUMOL SUBTRACTION IS ALREADY INSIDE 2A. The entire quantitative case for pushing AI-Q1 down is a composition wedge of -0.03 to -0.15 pp/yr from hours moving into near-zero-productivity care. But 2A's locked 'cuts baseline OECD real GDP per capita growth by ~40%, from 1.0%/yr to 0.6%/yr' is the OECD's own aging-drag calculation and sectoral reallocation into care is its principal mechanism. Subtracting it again against the locked 0.6% books one effect twice, and AI-Q1 is measured against a 2015-2022 TFP baseline, not against a no-aging counterfactual. (2) THE SCARCITY CHANNEL RAISES MEASURED TFP CONDITIONAL ON ADOPTION, NOT JUST ADOPTION BREADTH. Automation is deployed where the wage bill is largest; a scarce, dearer worker raises both the probability of adoption AND the measured output-per-hour gain realized when it happens, because the displaced hours are high-value hours. Wave 1 let the demand pull raise the firm count and then insisted it could not raise the productivity those firms register — which asserts that the marginal adopter is systematically the least productive one, with no support in the locked priors. Coupling should therefore move AI-Q1 UP from 23.0% to ~27-29%, and AI-Q6's Transformative Breakout UP from 16.2% to ~19-20%, with the Hulten Ceiling cell DOWN from 36.5% to ~31-33% and Jagged Diffusion roughly unchanged. That is the mirror image of P1 (Breakout to 10-12%) and of P2 (both tails into the middle). A SECOND TENSION WHERE I AGREE WITH WAVE 1'S DIRECTION BUT REJECT ITS INFERENCE: AI-Q4 at 66.0% is too LOW, and should sit near 78%, but NOT for the base-rate reason P1 gives (capex supercycles, 5 of 5 impaired) or the cost-of-capital reason P2 gives. It is too low because the question is DISJUNCTIVE and its second disjunct — net external AI software/API revenue below 0.5x annualized AI compute D&A for two consecutive years — is close to an accounting tautology during a buildout, when D&A on a rapidly growing asset base outruns externally booked revenue by construction and short GPU service lives accelerate the denominator. Here is the finding that matters for the aggregation: P2 and P3 both propagate AI-Q4's 66% into their growth and regime answers as if it were an economic-failure probability (P2: 'the AI-capex bust resolving AI-Q4 in 2027-32 leaving 2032-36 as the digestion window, -0.4 pp'; P3: driver of CQ6-D at 22 and of CQ5's disinflationary bond leg). That mapping is invalid. A high AI-Q4 driven by the accounting disjunct carries almost no information about capital destruction, demand shortfall, or the 2032-36 growth path, so a correctly RAISED AI-Q4 is consistent with HIGHER coupled growth, not lower — which is why my CQ3 P50 of 2.10% and my CQ6-A of 30 coexist with an AI-Q4 I would put above every Wave-1 seat's. THE DIRECTION OF THE AGGREGATE TENSION, STATED PLAINLY AGAINST P2: he concludes 'the tension runs toward LOWER coupled growth and nothing in the coupling runs the other way.' Three things run the other way and his own payload contains all three. The locked healthy-aging capacity gain (+0.4 pp/yr to global growth, 41 countries, N ~ 1M) enters his build as +0.25%/yr of participation inside an hours term, a small fraction of what 2A states. The demand-pull he concedes on AI-Q2 is denied any TFP expression. And his own simulation reading — which he correctly refuses as a level — nonetheless tells him that a UN-WPP-LOW labour path coexists with ~3% growth, which he reads as proof that aging is irrelevant to the model rather than as a reminder that his own 1.5% requires the labour channel to carry roughly four times the weight the only independent closure available to him assigns it. On the AI-Q3 / electricity-ceiling point I endorse P2's finding without qualification: 1,573.8 TWh at ~$80/MWh against ~$130T PPP is ~0.097% of GDP, so the locked P90 is approximately a willingness-to-pay cap of twice the simulation's own 0.05% default, and the locked prior and the model agree on the MECHANISM. That is the one place in this effort where an independent closure corroborates a locked marginal, and it should be weighted accordingly rather than lost among the contradictions.

wave3.lens_self_description: Dragonfly-eye synthesizer: I produced the effort-level posterior by weighting the five prior panelists question-by-question on the quality of their specific argument, moving only where the Wave-2 red-team landed a verifiable hit and refusing to move where it merely posed — which forbade me from introducing any new reference class, new telemetry, new Fermi decomposition or simulation reading of my own, so every number below is a reconciliation of arguments already on the table plus the coherence arithmetic the lock requires.
wave3.cq1_reasoning: CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonised unemployment 2032-36 average <= 5.5%) = 0.55. Wave-1/2 spread: Historian 0.40, Fermi 0.52, Scout 0.60, Bayesian 0.49, Red-Team 0.65. I DOWN-WEIGHT the Outside-View Historian here: his reference class is the OECD total-area series 1999-2016, which prices pre-reform continental European labour regimes that no longer generate the data, and he applies it to a FIVE-YEAR MEAN, which is forgiving. The Red-Teamer landed a real, checkable hit: from a ~4.8-5.0% level with the locked denominator shrinkage, a window containing one 2020-severity year (OECD annual peak ~7.1%) prints roughly 4.8/4.8/6.8/6.0/5.2 = 5.52 and one milder recession clears outright, so A fails only on two downturns or one downturn plus a persistent displacement shelf. I do NOT go to his 0.65, because 2032-36 is six years beyond the last observation, Scout's verbatim youth caveat ("rose to 11.3% in August from 11.0% in July") is the AI-displacement margin showing up where the aggregate hides it, and Fermi's mismatch term (+0.56 pp from J+K+M displacement with ~50% carrying >2-year non-employment spells) is a one-directional add. 0.55. CONJUNCT B (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >= 10.0 pp cumulative 2025-36, i.e. ~0.87 pp/yr for 11 years) = 0.22. Spread: Fermi 0.18, Historian/Scout 0.20, Bayesian 0.105, Red-Team 0.33. I DOWN-WEIGHT the Bayesian Likelihood-Ratio Updater hardest of anyone in this effort on this one number: his 0.105 multiplies three likelihood ratios (RN vacancies 8.6% "down from 9.6% in 2024", the median-composition trap, and the prior's own Beyond Applause content) that all encode ONE proposition — the system does not clear by price — and he names the overlap, applies a partial haircut, and still compounds 1.3 x 0.60 x 0.60. That is double-counting a single mechanism and it is the clearest methodological error in the five payloads. I MOVE UP on the Red-Teamer's two-sided composition hit, which is real and which Fermi and Scout genuinely ran one-legged: the licensing queue they both invoke GUARANTEES the marginal Q hire is credentialed rather than an aide, 80+ acuity shifts hours toward skilled nursing, and within-F the electrification build is skilled-trade heavy (construction +5.2% y/y vs +3.2% private sector, BLS via Burns & McDonnell; Indeed's rival cut is +3.4% vs +2.4%, half the gap — preserved). I do NOT take his ratio-mandate leg at full strength: statutory minimum-staffing rules are exactly the instrument that fiscal strain delays or waives, his own signpost concedes this, and the locked 2A payer constraint (net interest 2% -> ~3% of GDP; Chinese pension subsidies ~2.9T RMB, ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure) is the binding fact. Against the 10.0 pp hard threshold, the pro-physical compression analogues (2021-24 low-wage surge, ~10 pp bottom-vs-top quartile in four years per Autor-Dube-McGrew) are not F+Q-vs-J+K+M, which are neither the bottom nor the top quartile. 0.22. CORRELATION: +0.30 (Fermi +0.15, Bayesian +0.25, Historian +0.35, Red-Team +0.55). Tight labour markets both suppress A and bid scarce-sector wages, but the state most favourable to B — hot care bidding driven by AI displacement — is the state that damages A, so the dependence is partly self-cancelling; and construction (F) is the most cyclical sector, so a recession breaks both at once. P(B|A) = 0.22 x 1.14 = 0.25. JOINT = 0.55 x 0.25 = 0.138 -> 14.
wave3.cq2_reasoning: Widest spread in the effort: Historian 18, Fermi 31, Scout 43, Bayesian 32, Red-Team 48. CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core >= 2.50%/yr average 2027-36) = 0.60. The Signal Scout found and the Red-Teamer priced the strongest unexploited observation in this effort, and it is arithmetic rather than forecast: the window starts Jan 2027, so roughly a third of it is substantially observable, and it is hot (OECD core "remained stable at 3.6% for the third consecutive month", 6 Oct 2026; headline 4.3% y/y Aug 2026; energy inflation "stabilised above 10%"; euro-area core 2.5% in Sept 2026 up from 2.4%; euro-area headline flash "up 0.6 p.p. to 3.8% - its highest level since September 2023"). I DOWN-WEIGHT the Historian's 0.35 heavily: he anchors on inflation-targeting-era 10-year windows in preference to a near-determined first third of the actual window, and that is the single clearest case of reference-class anchoring in the five payloads. But I SHADE BELOW Scout's and the Red-Teamer's 2.8-2.9% read of 2027-29, because the published 3.6% is Turkey-inflated, Scout himself flags the GDP-weighted level as "MINE, not published... the single weakest link in my chain", and the one verified weighted-ish print — euro-area core 2.5% — is much cooler. At 2027-29 = ~2.70%, the remaining seven years need only (25.0 - 8.1)/7 = 2.41% to clear, barely above target. Fermi's independent additive build (2.00% anchor, +0.20 care/construction Baumol, +0.25 fiscal-dominance tolerance, +0.25 non-tradable labour scarcity, +0.08 grid pass-through, -0.09 AI tradable-services deflation, -0.15 Chinese goods deflation = 2.54%) corroborates a coin flip at the threshold. 0.60. CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI < 1.50%/yr average 2027-36) = 0.68, the one place four of five panelists converge for the same good reason (Japan 1995-2020 persistence at ~0.1%/yr with 0 of 2 decades exiting; locked -60M over 2026-35; worker/retiree 4.4 -> 2.8; PPI negative for 36 consecutive months, "the longest streak of economy-wide price declines since market reforms in the late 1970s"). The Sept 2026 ~0.9% print stays at LR 1.0 — TrendForce, a secondary aggregator with an AI-generated summary, unconfirmed against the NBS release. A linear path from ~0.3% in 2027 to 2.0% in 2036 means a 10-yr mean of 1.15%; clearing 1.50% requires decisive reflation before 2033. CORRELATION: I take the Red-Teamer's hit at roughly half strength. His tariff-decoupling argument is genuinely novel and correctly signed — pass-through from Chinese producer deflation to OECD core requires an open channel, and tariff walls, CBAM-style border pricing and content rules mechanically decouple the two price levels, so the "divergence" is one coupled state rather than two competing draws. But decoupling shifts a level once; the relative-price gradient still transmits through third markets and non-tariffed goods, so I do not go to his +0.02. Multiplicative ratio 0.95 (against Fermi's -0.20 and the Bayesian's 0.87). P(B|A) = 0.68 x 0.95 = 0.646. JOINT = 0.60 x 0.646 = 0.388 -> 39. This is NOT a stagflation forecast; it is a statement that three of ten averaging years are already in the data and the Historian priced the window as if it began today.
wave3.cq3_reasoning: PPP WEIGHT: w_China = 0.375, w_OECD = 0.625. Fermi 0.38 (reconciled against the adapter's independent 0.371 at 2031), Historian 0.39, Bayesian 0.375, Red-Team 0.37, Scout 0.31 — Scout's is the outlier and is inconsistent with OECD-38 PPP GDP ~$72T against China ~$41T; I down-weight him to zero on the weighting and note the Red-Teamer's correct rejoinder that identical weights over non-identical country sets is where a composition error HIDES rather than where it is ruled out. The locked -2.7 pp/yr is an IMF 2025-2050 counterfactual decomposition against a no-aging world, not an adjustment to an aging-inclusive forecast, and Fermi's cross-check ("a frictionless China counterfactual of ~4.7%/yr less the locked -2.7 pp = 2.0%") subtracts it from a rate already produced by an economy whose working-age population has shrunk since 2012, whose property sector has already deleveraged, and whose pension subsidy is already 10.1% of fiscal expenditure. That cross-check is circular, so the "two independent routes agreeing" that carried the Bayesian's LR-2.0 update was partly illusory — the agreement was one route plus its own echo. I therefore CANCEL the cross-check while KEEPING Fermi's genuinely independent bottom-up route (labour -0.63, capital deepening +2.00, TFP +1.10, property/credit/pension-claim drag -0.50 = 1.97) and reading it as a lower bound, because his +2.00 capital-deepening and -0.50 property terms are by his own account his least-anchored. OECD-38 LEG = 1.05%/yr: locked 0.60 per-capita + 0.17 PPP-weighted population + 0.30 AI TFP (the AI-Q6 own-regime-mix EV, 0.162 x 0.70 + 0.472 x 0.35 + 0.365 x 0.07 = +0.304, computed identically by Fermi, Scout and the Red-Teamer) + 0.10 PPP-reweighting - 0.06 residual Baumol - 0.08 fiscal consolidation and hurdle rate. (i) The Baumol double-count is real but not total: the locked "1.0 -> 0.6%/yr, absent productivity offsets" is predominantly a labour-QUANTITY calculation (working-age share), not a sectoral productivity-composition calculation, so Scout's full -0.15 wedge double-books part of it and Fermi's -0.03 is about right; I keep -0.06. (ii) The PPP-reweighting point identifies a genuinely unstated convention — ~26% of OECD-38 PPP GDP sits in members whose old-age ratio is nowhere near 39-41%, and the US alone is ~43% with the best large-member demographics — but he asserts the favourable branch of an ambiguity, and OECD aggregates of this kind are normally already aggregated rather than member-averaged. I book +0.10 against his +0.25 and flag it as unresolved. ASSEMBLY: 0.625 x 1.05 + 0.375 x 2.75 = 0.66 + 1.03 = 1.69 -> P50 1.75%/yr. INTERVAL: P10 0.9 — a synchronised recession inside the averaging window (~50% per 5-yr window, -0.8 to -1.2 pp on the average) or the AI-Q4 branch resolving 2027-32 and leaving 2032-36 as digestion, plus a China property/pension financing event. P90 3.0 — I widen the upper tail beyond every Wave-1/2 interval because the Red-Teamer is right that all three Wave-1 seats structurally suppressed it: the locked healthy-aging capacity gain ("70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000", 41 countries, N ~ 1M, +0.4 pp/yr to global growth 2025-50) enters Fermi's build as +0.25%/yr of participation inside an hours term, a fraction of what 2A states, and the labour-scarcity demand pull every seat conceded on AI-Q2 was denied any TFP expression. I KEEP Fermi's handling of the simulation intact and endorse it: refuse the 2.95% growth level (Ayres-Warr gamma = 0.55 on useful energy against a mainstream cost-share 0.05-0.08; dominant dial serviceEfficiencyGrowth at ~1.8x per plausible range; a UN-WPP-LOW labour path coexisting with ~3% growth proves the model is near-insensitive to the channel at issue), and take only the robot bound — robotsPer1000 of 3.92-6.63 by 2036 = 0.39-0.66% of workers' worth of installed stock against a care need of ~3.0% of OECD-38 employment, which closes the "robots fill the elder-care gap" channel inside the horizon, low-fertility-conditional.
wave3.cq4_reasoning: MEASUREMENT FIRST, and it is the most load-bearing arithmetic in this effort: the question asks for a G7 GDP-WEIGHTED 10y real yield and the locked 2.60% (FRED DFII10, Oct 30 2026) is US-ONLY. All five panelists independently weight to ~1.71-1.90% today (Fermi 1.71 on US 2.60 / JP -0.20 / DE 0.70 / UK 1.30 / FR 0.60 / IT 1.50 / CA 1.80; Scout 1.8-1.9 with his caveat preserved verbatim — he "could not verify the non-US legs at my horizon" and found "NO sourced 2026 Japanese or German 10y level"; Historian ~1.90). I adopt ~1.80%. Anyone anchored on 2.60% has mis-specified the object by ~80 bp. BUILD: r* 1.85 (base 1.15; +0.10 life-cycle dissaving, kept small because 2A says aging worsens (r-g) by ~+1.0 pp "even where a frictionless r* eases", i.e. mostly g falling; +0.42 public dissaving on global gross debt crossing 100% of GDP by 2029, ~142% US and ~127% China by 2031, net interest 2% -> ~3% of GDP; +0.22 eroding sovereign convenience yield, named directly in 2A; +0.15 net AI/grid savings demand after the AI-Q4 haircut on Fermi's ~0.55 pp-of-GDP increment; -0.12 precautionary saving; -0.07 BIS AER 2026 Box C, where capital-concentrated income carries a higher saving propensity so cognitive-labour compression is a demand shortfall and a NEGATIVE for r* — the most-missed sign, correctly flagged by Fermi) + real term premium 0.70 - financial-repression wedge 0.25 = 2.30%. I ACCEPT one Red-Team hit and REJECT the other, and the rejection matters. ACCEPTED: the repression wedge is a regime artifact, not a standing capacity. Fermi books -0.40 and the Historian gives the repression base rate heavy weight from the 1940s-50s and the 2010s; both periods share a central bank that WANTED duration (war finance, then a zero-bound reflation). A central bank running down a balance sheet into the duration supply 2A locks is a seller, and LDI/Solvency II/LCR demand is a largely allocated stock rather than a flow that scales with issuance. I book -0.25, between his -0.15 and Fermi's -0.40. REJECTED AS CONTRARIAN POSING: his claim that 2A's locked +1.0 pp (r-g) deterioration forces r up once g is raised. The +1.0 pp is itself a counterfactual decomposition against a no-aging world — precisely the object whose misuse he correctly diagnosed in the China -2.7 pp — so it is not an identity constraining r - g(2032-36) to a level. He commits his own diagnosed error in reverse, and I do not follow him to 2.50%; the ~25 bp difference between us is that error. COHERENCE WITH CQ3: r 2.30 against my OECD leg 1.05 gives r-g = +1.25 pp, which is consistent with the locked worsening being mostly a g story (Scout's check landed +1.25 on the same logic). Against coupled g of 1.75 it is +0.55 pp. COHERENCE WITH CQ6: a +0.70 term premium with a convex upper tail is the "steep real term premia" language in B and the "term-premium spikes" language in C, and my 50/18 split on B/C is where that sits. hypothesis_critique.a: SMOOTHLY carries it, and it fails on a rate by roughly an order of magnitude, not on a direction. This is the one plank where all five panelists converge (5/7/6/5/6) and where the Red-Teamer explicitly declined to inflate his score to be different -- correctly, and I record that as a point in his favour. The converging arithmetic: Fermi's flow identity gives 0.77M/yr displaced J+K+M against a 1.66M/yr Q need at ~15% convertible = ~7% coverage; the Historian's displaced-worker reference classes give a cross-occupational reallocation elasticity of 0.05-0.10 into health/social care (~5-8% of displaced US manufacturing workers 1999-2011, ~2-4% of UK ex-miners 1984-94, many exiting the labour force or onto disability instead). Every friction compounds the same way and none offsets: a 1-year LPN to 2-4-year RN queue whose binding capacity is clinical placement slots and faculty (nursing faculty vacancies ~7%, nearly 1,700 unfilled, 2026 NSI via AACN; Canadian credentialing 'six months to two years'; German recognition plus B1-B2; NCLEX first-time pass 88.6%/91.2%/86.7% for 2023/24/25 with internationally-educated-nurse rates 'steadily declining since 2010' per Health Affairs), ~6-8% of new RN licensees aged 40+ against a displaced median in the mid-40s, a 1.6-1.9x reservation-wage gap, an 85-90% female care workforce against a 55-60% male displaced pool, geographic immobility against housing costs, and nursing-assistant musculoskeletal injury rates ~3x the all-worker BLS rate -- a compensating differential that must be PAID. The robot substitute is arithmetically closed inside the horizon (0.39-0.66% of workers' worth of installed stock by 2036 even in the simulation's most aggressive automation scenario, against a 3.0%-of-employment care need; low-fertility-conditional). I take the Red-Teamer's one genuine extension: a non-smooth supply response is a PRICE event as well as a shortfall, which is why a 6 on this plank is consistent with my CQ1 at 14 rather than at 9 -- Fermi, Scout and the Bayesian read the same fact as doubly bearish. 6.
hypothesis_critique.b: BLOCKS and SEVERELY fail differently, and the net sign is the finding. BLOCKS is the wrong MECHANISM: the observed compression is on the elasticity margin, not the level -- India IT-BPM at +6.1% revenue against +2.3% headcount and net additions of 135,000 to 5.95M (Nasscom ASR 2026; CAVEAT PRESERVED: industry-body projections, not audited, and AI revenue of $10-12B 'excludes AI-specific revenue from some firms', so a floor); Philippine CC-BPM +4% to 1.68M from 1.62M with ~1.73M projected for 2026 (CXAP, an industry association with a directional interest, against SunStar's undershown 'AI puts 1.9M at risk' -- treat both as advocacy). The Historian's base rate is the cleanest frame: ~0 of 3 'automation destroys offshoring' claims resolved true within a decade, and the 2001-02 and 2015-20 RPA predictions preceded the growth to the locked ~$280B and 1.7M+ scales. SEVERELY fails on the net, because the PHYSICAL leg runs the opposite way and the plank omits it: Japan's ~250,000 FY2026 nursing-care shortfall heading to ~570,000 by FY2040 against only 28,400 foreign nationals in specified-skilled-worker nursing-care status at end-2023 ('just over half the government's target'), ~122,000 Indian-trained nurses already in OECD countries, 'one in six nurses in high-income countries was trained abroad', Germany's projected 350,000-500,000 gap by 2035 (workvisa.guide, a COMMERCIAL IMMIGRATION GUIDE, not official), and Philippine cash remittances at a record $35.634B in 2025 (+3.3% from $34.493B, BSP) with $36.6B forecast for 2026. QUANTIFIED NET, reconciling the Historian's counterfactual framing with Fermi's level framing -- the two are not in conflict and the panel partly talked past itself: against the no-compression counterfactual the virtual leg is -$90B to -$160B/yr for India and -300k to -550k Philippine jobs, while the physical leg's remittance gain is ~$10-25B/yr combined, so the net is clearly negative versus counterfactual; against 2025 LEVELS both legs still rise and the net is positive-to-neutral in income with a deteriorating composition. The Red-Teamer's 8 over-corrects by resolving that ambiguity in only the favourable direction, and he drops the distributional loss (the Philippines exports precisely the nurses its own rising old-age ratio needs) that keeps SEVERELY partly alive. The physical leg is also policy-rationed, not demand-rationed (foreign-born share of OECD nurses moved only ~14% -> ~16% over 2010-2020 despite documented shortages), which caps the offset without reversing its sign; and a ~1-in-3 base rate of a GCC oil-fiscal remittance shock within the decade (2015-16 cut Gulf-to-India flows ~9%) is the real tail risk and is demographically unrelated to OECD aging. 11.
hypothesis_critique.c: THEN FALLS carries it, and this plank has the widest spread in the effort (Fermi 15, Bayesian 26, Scout 33, Historian 42, Red-Team 46) -- the spread is almost entirely a reading dispute about what 'falls' means, not a disagreement about the inflation path, which is itself a finding. The first clause is nearly observed rather than forecast: OECD core 'remained stable at 3.6% for the third consecutive month' (6 Oct 2026), headline 4.3% y/y, energy inflation 'stabilised above 10%', euro-area headline flash 'up 0.6 p.p. to 3.8% - its highest level since September 2023'. So 'hot for the next few years' is the present tense, and the plank's front half is already largely spent -- which the Historian correctly notes makes the timing mis-specified, not merely optimistic. On MY numbers inflation does fall: ~2.70% over 2027-29 to ~2.40% over 2032-36. But it lands ABOVE target for the whole decade, so the plank is true as a direction and false as the benign-2030s story any reader takes from it. The Red-Teamer's 46 over-credits exactly that reader. Fermi's 15 is the clearest case in this effort of a panelist's own build contradicting his plank score -- he computes 2.54% on a RISING profile, which makes the plank nearly definitionally false, yet the observed 3.6% starting print makes a rising profile the less likely shape, so his score is too low for a reason his own arithmetic undercuts. Two further failures: the SHAPE, since of the five post-1945 G7 episodes above 5% (1947, 1951, 1974, 1980, 2022) about three had a second wave within ten years, putting a clean one-and-done disinflation at only ~40-50%; and the CROSS-SECTION, since the plank is silent on the OECD-versus-China DIVERGENCE that the locked priors make the actually interesting fact (China CPI ~0.9% y/y on an unconfirmed TrendForce secondary print, after -0.3% in Sept 2025 and PPI negative for 36 consecutive months, 'the longest streak of economy-wide price declines since market reforms in the late 1970s'). The terms that decline are front-loaded (energy base effects, tariff level shifts, Chinese goods pass-through); the ones that persist are administered care wages, the Baumol relative-price wedge, non-tradable labour scarcity under a shrinking denominator, and the fiscal tolerance a 2% -> 3%-of-GDP interest claim buys. 32.
hypothesis_critique.d: EVENTUALLY and WINS fail in different registers, and OUTRUNS fails in a third the panel only half-identified. EVENTUALLY places the claim outside the Dec 31 2036 resolution horizon, so it is a defect of FORM: a plank true only after the resolution date is false as scored, and on a 40-year view it may well be right, which is most of what keeps my score in the teens. WINS is undefined -- against what counterfactual, in levels or growth rates, aggregate or per capita, and for whom. The Red-Teamer adds the genuinely new conceptual hit, and it is correct: output is not population, so a shrinking workforce with constant technology already raises measured labour productivity by composition, and 'exponential technology racing demographic subtraction' is a category error about the wrong relation. EXPONENTIAL is also doing undeclared work -- nothing in the locked 2B set is exponential, and AI-Q6 itself puts 36.5% on a Hulten ceiling below +0.15 pp/yr. Within the window the arithmetic still runs against the plank even after my China correction: the AI-attributable TFP lift from AI-Q6's own regime midpoints is +0.304 pp/yr, the capex channel adds only +0.04 to +0.06 pp/yr (~0.55 pp of GDP in incremental investment at K/Y = 3.0 and alpha = 0.35, with 3-5 year GPU lives making most gross spend replacement rather than deepening), and the demographic block still subtracts roughly 2-3x that even on my higher China leg -- down from the 4:1 Fermi computed, because his was built on the counterfactual double-subtraction. The timing base rates are the sharpest cut and I keep them: electrification took ~40 years to a measured payoff (David 1990), IT ~25 years to a 1995-2004 TFP blip that faded after ~9, so a GPT adding >= 0.5 pp to TFP growth within 11 years of commercial diffusion is ~0-1 of 4; and Japan led world robot density for 30 years at ~0.8%/yr real growth since 1991 while Germany ran Industrie 4.0 at ~1.3%. Neither offset arrived. I score above all five Wave-1/2 seats (18/14/11/13 and the Red-Teamer's 22 excepted) because my own 1.75% P50 and 19 on CQ6-A say the growth leg holds up materially better than Wave 1 allowed, and because the two double-counts the red team found are exactly what made Wave 1 size the demographic subtraction larger than it is. 16.

key_drivers: China's 2032-36 growth leg, which I move to 2.75%/yr -- the single biggest reconciliation in this payload. The Red-Teamer's hit is real: the locked -2.7 pp/yr is an IMF 2025-2050 counterfactual decomposition against a no-aging world, and Fermi's cross-check subtracted it from a ~4.7% rate that already embeds a working-age population shrinking since 2012, a deleveraged property sector and a 10.1%-of-expenditure pension subsidy, so the 'two independent routes converging' that carried the Bayesian's LR-2.0 update was one route plus its own echo. But his 3.3% applies early-2030s projections to a later window, so I land between: 2.75%, worth ~+0.17 pp of coupled growth against the Wave-2 posterior and most of my CQ6-A uplift.

Whether the OECD care shortfall clears by PRICE or by QUANTITY RATIONING, which is the hinge of my whole effort and sets CQ1, plank (a) and the C-versus-B split. The 25-year non-clearing record (OECD Beyond Applause: LTC workers earn below-average wages compared with similar workers despite shortages documented since the late 1990s) plus RN vacancies easing 9.6% -> 8.6% with no relative wage gain is direct observation of rationing; against it, the Red-Teamer's ratio-mandate mechanism is the only argument in five payloads for a genuine price obligation, and I discount it because statutory minimum staffing is precisely the instrument that a payer facing net interest at 2% -> 3% of GDP delays or waives.

The two-sided composition race in CQ1's wage conjunct, which Fermi and Scout ran with one leg handicapped. They are right that AI removes the bottom of J+K+M so its surviving MEDIAN rises, and right that migrant and new-entrant inflow depresses the F+Q median; they discarded the within-F+Q upward leg, where the licensing queue they themselves invoke GUARANTEES the marginal Q hire is credentialed rather than an aide, 80+ acuity shifts hours toward skilled nursing, and the electrification build is skilled-trade heavy (construction +5.2% y/y vs +3.2% private sector; Indeed's rival cut +3.4% vs +2.4%, half the gap). This takes conjunct B from the 0.105-0.20 range to 0.22.

The 2027-29 arithmetic lock-in on CQ2, the strongest unexploited observation in the effort: with a third of the ten-year averaging window substantially observable and hot, the remaining seven years need only ~2.41% to clear a 2.50% mean, so a near-return to target still clears. Shaded below Scout's and the Red-Teamer's 2.8-2.9% read because the published OECD-wide 3.6% is Turkey-inflated, Scout flags his own GDP-weighted estimate as 'the single weakest link in my chain', and euro-area core at 2.5% is the only verified weighted-ish print.

The G7 GDP-weighting correction on CQ4 (~80 bp) plus the financial-repression wedge's status. The locked 2.60% TIPS print is US-only and the weighted object is ~1.80% today; on top of that, treating repression as a regime artifact of central banks that WANTED duration (1940s-50s, 2010s) rather than a standing capacity moves the wedge from Fermi's -0.40 to -0.25 and the P50 to 2.30%. The peak-to-trough DATING convention on CQ5's bond leg, the most checkable Wave-2 hit. All of Wave 1 scored the conditional as 'did bonds hedge over the episode' when the question measures from the equity peak to the equity trough; re-dating moves 1987 and 1990 out of the flight-to-quality cell and the conditional from ~0.38 to ~0.47, partly offset by the effort's best shared insight -- that the modal drawdown generator here (the AI capex bust) is disinflationary and so fails the bond leg, making this a request for two things from opposite shock families.

wave3.coupling_tension: The effort's central coupling finding is a SCISSORS between AI-Q2 and AI-Q1, and after reconciling the Wave-2 dispute I keep one leg and cut the other in half. AI-Q2 (OECD-38 firm adoption >= 50% by 2036, 21.3% raw) is TOO LOW once demographics are endogenous, and this is the one judgment all five panelists reached from mutually exclusive evidence bases -- the Historian from a one-directional base rate (Japan, Korea and Germany led industrial robot density precisely as their workforces aged; EU enterprise cloud adoption ~19% in 2014 to ~45% in 2023 makes a quadrupling of a firm-count measure in twelve years near a coin flip BEFORE any scarcity push), Fermi from mechanism (marginal value = payoff x labour share x GDP per worker, so a scarcer, dearer worker raises MV mechanically, with OECD hours at -0.05%/yr and Chinese working-age at -1.15%/yr), Scout from 2026 telemetry (Japan's ~250,000 FY2026 nursing-care shortfall against 28,400 specified-skilled-worker caregivers at end-2023, 'just over half the government's target'; US electrician deficit ~107,000 peaking 2027 against BLS shortfalls of ~81,000/yr through 2034; construction wages +5.2% vs +3.2%). Five lenses, four evidence bases, one sign: aging is a DEMAND PULL for adoption, not only a drag. I adopt ~30%, +9 pp. AI-Q1 (PPP-weighted TFP lift >= +0.50 pp/yr, 23.0% raw) I hold roughly FLAT at 22, which splits the Wave-1/2 consensus (19-21%) from the Red-Teamer's 27-29%. His attack lands halfway: the entire quantitative case for pushing AI-Q1 down was a Baumol composition wedge of -0.03 to -0.15 pp/yr, and 2A's locked 'cuts baseline OECD real GDP per capita growth by ~40%, from 1.0%/yr to 0.6%/yr' already contains the OECD's own aging-drag calculation, so part of that wedge is double-booked against a marginal that is itself measured off a 2015-2022 TFP baseline rather than a no-aging counterfactual. His second point is also a real logical hit: the panel let the demand pull raise the firm count while denying it any productivity expression, which implicitly asserts that the marginal adopter is systematically the least productive one, with no support in the locked priors -- automation is deployed where the wage bill is largest, so the displaced hours are high-value hours. What survives on the other side, and is why I do not follow him up: the public-complements crowding-out is INDEPENDENT of Baumol and is locked in 2A (net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP; Chinese pension subsidies ~2.9T RMB, ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure, rising as worker/retiree goes 4.4 -> 2.8), and grid interconnection, transformer capacity, clinical placement slots and licensure throughput are exactly the non-reproducible complements that cap measured TFP whatever the technology does. So the scissors is real but narrower than Wave 1 claimed: adoption up ~9 pp, measured TFP flat. DIRECTION FOR AI-Q6: Transformative Breakout ~14 (down 2 from 16.2, splitting the Historian's 10-12 against the Red-Teamer's 19-20), Jagged Diffusion ~51 (up ~4), Hulten Ceiling ~35 (down ~1.5). AI-Q5 (38.2%) is TOO LOW by ~6 pp, to ~44, for a denominator reason exogeneity hides: the share's denominator is sectoral GVA inflated by hyperscaler rents booked inside ISIC J, while endogenous demographics retire the most expensive senior cohort as AI blocks the entry-level replacement flow, so the numerator falls from both ends; capped below Scout's +10 pp because the supporting labour-share telemetry is a mess of non-comparable measures (54.1% 'the lowest level since the US government began tracking it following World War II', S&P Global Jun 30 2026; 53.7% nonfarm business Q1 2026; 52.8% EY-Parthenon; 51.4% on a gross-domestic-income basis 'down from 58% in 1980'), with the Tax Foundation finding the labour share 'remains within historical levels' and Goldman's Duggirala arguing 'the decline has been less steep than BLS data suggests'. AI-Q4 (66.0%) should rise to ~72 on the Historian's capex-supercycle base rate (UK railway mania 1845-50; US nuclear 1974-84, roughly 120 of ~250 ordered plants cancelled; telecom/fibre 1999-2002; Japan 1986-91; US shale 2014-20 with ~$300B of write-downs -- about 5 of 5 impaired >= 20%) plus the coupled cost-of-capital term, but with the Red-Teamer's finding attached, which is the most consequential correction in this effort for downstream aggregation: AI-Q4 is DISJUNCTIVE, and its revenue/D&A disjunct is close to an accounting tautology during a buildout with short GPU service lives, so Fermi's and Scout's propagation of 66% into their growth paths and CQ6-D cells as if it were an economic-failure probability is invalid -- a correctly RAISED AI-Q4 is compatible with HIGHER coupled growth. AI-Q3 is the one place an independent closure CORROBORATES a locked marginal rather than contradicting it, and I endorse it without qualification: its P90 of 1,573.8 TWh at ~$80/MWh against ~$130T of combined PPP GDP is an electricity-bill ceiling of ~0.097% of GDP, almost exactly the willingness-to-pay cap the simulation implements at 0.05%, so prior and model agree on the MECHANISM (price-capped load) and differ only ~2x on the level. AGGREGATE DIRECTION: still toward lower coupled growth than the CQ6 labels imply, but by roughly half of what Fermi asserted. His claim that 'nothing in the coupling runs the other way' does not survive -- three things do, and his own payload contains all three: the locked healthy-aging capacity gain (+0.4 pp/yr to global growth, 41 countries, N ~ 1M) enters his build as +0.25%/yr of participation inside an hours term; the demand pull he concedes on AI-Q2 is denied any TFP expression; and the China drag is subtracted from a rate that already contains it. The operational consequence for aggregation is unchanged, though: the coupled joint contains a cell the standalone marginals treat as near-empty -- WIDE adoption with LOW measured TFP -- and any aggregation imposing a positive AI-Q1/AI-Q2 correlation will systematically under-weight it. That cell is my CQ6-B at 50.

wave_audit.wave1_spread: Widest on CQ2 (Historian 18, Fermi 31, Scout 43) and on hypothesis plank (c) (42/15/33). Both spreads have the SAME cause and it is not a disagreement about the inflation path: the three lenses disagreed about whether a near-determined first third of a ten-year averaging window is evidence. The Historian's lens forbade him from treating a current print as anything but a level inside a reference class, so he priced 2027-36 as if it began today; Scout's lens required him to start from the freshest administrative telemetry, so he found the arithmetic advantage; Fermi built from a 2.00% target anchor and reached 2.54% by mechanism, landing in the middle by a route that never used the starting level at all. Second-widest was the CQ3 China leg (Fermi 1.97%, Scout 2.8%, Historian ~3.0%) -- and that spread turned out to be the important one, because only Fermi implemented the locked -2.7 pp drag explicitly and he implemented it wrongly. Third was CQ4's measurement object, where Fermi alone decomposed the locked US-only 2.60% TIPS print into a G7 GDP-weighted ~1.71%, an ~80-90 bp correction the Historian and Scout reached independently but under-emphasized. Narrowest by far was plank (a) at 5/7/6 -- the one question where reference-class history, Fermi arithmetic and 2026 telemetry all say the same thing, which is why I moved it almost not at all.

The Premortem Red-Teamer landed three genuine kills and two poses. KILLS: (1) the China counterfactual double-subtraction, which destroyed Fermi's cross-check and with it the apparent two-route convergence the Bayesian had updated on at LR 2.0 -- the biggest substantive change in this effort; (2) the CQ5 peak-to-trough DATING convention, which re-dates 1987 and 1990 out of the Historian's flight-to-quality cell and is checkable on benchmark closes; (3) the one-sided composition race in CQ1, where Fermi and Scout applied their own decisive argument to J+K+M and the downward F+Q leg only, and the observation that AI-Q4's disjunctive accounting trigger makes Fermi's and Scout's propagation of 66% into growth and CQ6-D invalid. wave_audit.biggest_update: CQ2: from the Wave-1 modal 31 (Fermi) to 39, +8 points -- and +21 against the Historian's 18, the largest single gap I closed. CAUSE: the 2027-29 arithmetic lock-in. With OECD core observed at 3.6% for three consecutive months, headline 4.3% y/y and energy inflation above 10%, roughly a third of a ten-year averaging window that begins Jan 2027 is substantially observable and hot, so the remaining seven years need only ~2.41% to clear a 2.50% mean -- a near-return to target still clears.
