wave2.coupling_tension:
THREE TENSIONS, EACH WITH A DIRECTION AND AN EXPLICIT LIKELIHOOD RATIO, SINCE THAT IS WHAT MY SEAT IS FOR.

(1) AI-Q3 IS TOO HIGH, AND MY ROUTE TO THAT CONCLUSION IS A PRICE ROUTE, NOT A CAPEX ROUTE — DOWNWARD, AND IT IS POSITIVELY COUPLED TO MY CQ2 IN A WAY 2B CANNOT SEE. AI-Q3's P50 of 998.2 TWh is ~2.7x the ~365 TWh 2024 base. Treat the locked AI-Q4 (66% on >=20% impairment/cancellation or AI revenue below 0.5x compute D&A for two consecutive years) as evidence about AI-Q3: P(AI-Q4 priced at 66% | strict operational 2036 load >= 998 TWh) / P(same | load < 998 TWh) ~ 0.45, i.e. roughly 2.2:1 against the locked median — justifiable above my 2:1 bar because a 2.74x STRICT OPERATIONAL load requires the build to substantially complete AND energize AND be paid for, which is close to the complement of AI-Q4. Add the physical arithmetic: +633 TWh over 12 years is ~53 TWh/yr of new load, ~9.3 GW/yr of firm capacity at a 65% load factor, claiming ~10-18% of OECD+China net firm additions against interconnection queues of 4-7 years and HV transformer lead times of 2-4 years, and Microsoft already cutting CY2026 capex to ~$170bn "due to delays in third-party data-center capacity." Now the demographic coupling, which is MY effort's channel: retail-rate politics. Observed US residential rates +7.3% y/y Apr 2025-Apr 2026; EIA has commercial sales +5.3% in 2027 against residential ~0.5%/yr with commercial surpassing residential "for the first time on record in 2027"; electricity bills are at "the top of the midterm agenda." The locked old-age ratio moving 31% to 39-41% mechanically grows the voter bloc on fixed nominal incomes that is least able to absorb a nominal bill increase and most reliably mobilized, which converts a price complaint into a large-load-tariff and interconnection veto. LR on that political channel on its own: ~1.6, below my bar, so I DISCOUNT it and do not let it do the work — the AI-Q4 and queue-physics LRs carry the conclusion. COUPLED RESOLUTION: P50 ~850 TWh (-15%), P10 ~520 (the left tail falls further than the median because an impairment event plus queues truncate downward while the already-committed 2026-2029 tranche energizes regardless), P90 ~1,380. THE DIRECTIONAL FINDING SPECIFIC TO MY EFFORT: AI-Q3 and OECD core inflation are POSITIVELY coupled, not independent — every TWh that IS built passes into commercial and industrial electricity prices and thence into core SERVICES input costs (household electricity is excluded from core, business electricity is not, it arrives inside services prices), so a world that delivers the locked 998 TWh is also a world with a hotter core aggregate. The locked AI-Q3 P50 and a sub-2.5% OECD core are therefore less jointly likely than the two marginals multiplied, and shading AI-Q3 down should shade conjunct A of CQ2 down with it. I did not do that to my own number, which means my CQ2 of 32 is, by my own argument, 1-2 points too high.

(2) AI-Q6'S MODAL REGIME IS A RENT REGIME, AND RENTS SHOW UP IN THE PRICE LEVEL RATHER THAN IN TFP — SO AI-Q1 AND AI-Q5 ARE INCONSISTENT WITH EACH OTHER ONCE THE DEFLATOR IS ENDOGENOUS, AND THE INCONSISTENCY RESOLVES UPWARD ON AI-Q5 AND DOWNWARD ON AI-Q1. "Jagged Diffusion & Hyperscaler Rent Concentration" at 47.2% is the standalone ensemble's own modal cell. A rent is a price, and a price does not deflate into measured real output. Two mechanical consequences 2B cannot see because it holds demographics (and therefore the price level) exogenous. First, AI-Q5's accounting can be satisfied entirely through the DENOMINATOR: hyperscaler rents inflate sector J's nominal GVA with no cognitive wage declining at all, and aging feeds this mechanically by pushing a growing retirement-asset pool into intangible-rent sectors as the safe-asset r* is compressed (Fermi's locked identity dr = d(r-g) + dg = +1.0 - 1.1 = -0.1 says the demographic block leaves r roughly flat even as the term premium rises, so the compression is in the SAFE leg specifically). AI-Q5 should read ~46%, upward. Second, AI-Q1 should read ~21%, DOWNWARD, because the demographic pull directs AI into health, long-term care, education and public administration, whose output is measured by their input in the national accounts, so diffusion there registers as spending and employment and never as measured TFP. The coupling therefore WIDENS the wedge between diffusion breadth and measured productivity — the Hulten/Baumol trap — which is exactly why my CQ6-A is 13 while CQ6-B is 53. CRITICAL ANTI-DOUBLE-COUNTING WARNING FOR THE AGGREGATOR, and the strongest single point in my Wave-1 panel: AI-Q5 and CQ1's second conjunct are ANTI-correlated through a composition identity, not co-moving. The observed displacement mechanism is an entry-level hiring collapse (Stanford/ADP, ~14-16% for ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed roles, relative to experienced workers, with Kolko disputing causation). Truncating the bottom of the J+K+M distribution LOWERS its compensation share while RAISING its measured median hourly wage. Any panelist who raises CQ1 because they believe AI-Q5 has the sign backwards; AI-Q5 being TRUE makes CQ1 HARDER, and that is why my CQ1 is 8.

(3) THE SHARPEST TENSION IS BETWEEN A LOCKED MARGINAL AND THE RESOLUTION MEASURE ITSELF, AND IT RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE — WHICH IS A FINDING ABOUT THE QUESTION SET, NOT A FORECAST. If the TFP lift does not arrive (77% per AI-Q1), then 2A's aging drag plus the BIS Box C labour-income demand deficit plus China's overcapacity export deflation should make OECD core UNDERSHOOT, so the stagflation cell cannot be demand-driven at all — its inflation must come entirely from supply walls in grid, care and construction. But those walls sit mostly OUTSIDE the resolution measure: household electricity and gas are excluded from US core CPI, core PCE and euro HICP core; construction enters only through shelter rent/OER, which tracks rents and incomes rather than build cost, and 2A's demographics mechanically suppress household formation in Japan, Korea, Italy and Germany; and ISIC Q prices are administered by fiscal authorities that 2A locks as constrained (net interest 2% to 3% of GDP, debt past 100% by 2029, China's pension subsidies already ~2.9T RMB or ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure). So the coupled world can deliver a genuinely severe relative-price crisis — electricity, care and construction at 4-6% — while the LOCKED CORE AGGREGATE never reaches 2.7%. That suppresses CQ6-C by measure construction. AND YET my CQ6-C is 22, nine points ABOVE my prior, for a reason that has nothing to do with supply walls: the five high-inflation OECD-38 members at ~8.8% PPP weight. The honest statement of the tension is therefore uncomfortable for my own lens: the stagflation cell in this question set is carried less by the physical bottleneck story the effort brief describes than by an EM membership and weighting convention, and anyone resolving CQ2 or CQ6 in 2037 on a headline, energy-inclusive, or core-OECD-only measure would get a materially different answer from the identical world. I report that as a resolution-criterion defect rather than as a forecast disagreement, and I flag that it is the reason my CQ2 (32) sits 18 points above my own prior and 18 points above the Historian whose base rate I was instructed to adopt.

wave2.lens_self_description:
I answered as a premortem / devil's-advocate red-teamer whose sole job was to break the three Wave-1 panelists' shared reasoning, which forbade me from averaging them, from treating any convergence between them as corroboration, and from arguing only the downside — every claim had to be an attack on a specific load-bearing assumption with a direction attached, and I wrote the failure story in both tails before setting a single number.

THE SINGLE STRONGEST SHARED ASSUMPTION, unquestioned by all three: that measured OECD core CPI/PCE is a weighted average of OBSERVED TRANSACTION PRICES over a basket in which the AI-exposed bloc (software, media, information, professional and financial services) carries a 0.20-0.25 weight and will PRINT 0.0-1.0%. Every one of their "extreme skew, dull level" arithmetics depends on it. P1: core goods 23% x 0.3 and financial/insurance 8% x 2.0. P2: "AI-exposed professional/financial/information services 12 pts at 1.0%." P3: "the AI-deflation bloc, weight ~0.20-0.25, 0.0-1.0%." It is wrong in both weight and sign. In core PCE the AI-exposed bloc is dominated by components that are NOT market-priced: portfolio management and investment advice are priced as a percentage of assets under management (an AI-capex equity boom makes that line INFLATE, not deflate); commercial banking is imputed through net interest margin, which widens with my CQ4 real-yield path; property and casualty insurance is premiums net of claims, which is rising on climate and construction-cost claims; and large parts of "other professional services" are deflated by BLS producer-price proxies that are themselves cost-based, so a fall in the labour input cost is recorded as a fall in real OUTPUT (measured volume), not as a price decline. The genuinely market-priced, genuinely AI-deflatable slice is closer to 0.08-0.12 of core, not 0.20-0.25, and part of the rest is counter-cyclically HOT. Correcting only this term adds +0.20 to +0.35 pp to all three of their central core builds, and it is the single reason my CQ2 and my CQ6-C sit far above the Wave-1 centre. Secondary attack on the same block: all three put shelter at 3.0-3.5% partly because "aging suppresses household formation." That is wrong in sign for 2027-2036 — aging raises HOUSEHOLDS per capita (widowhood, single occupancy, aging-in-place suppressing turnover and therefore suppressing effective supply); Japan's household count rose for roughly two decades after its population peaked. Shelter at 3.4-3.6% against a construction sector being bid away by the grid build is the central case, not the hawkish one.

WHERE WAVE 1 FELL INTO THE NAMED BIASES. (i) ANCHORING ON THE LOCKED PRIORS' FRAMING, with double-counting dressed as validation: all three subtracted 2A's "-1.1 pp/yr global, -2.7 pp/yr China" as a deduction from a convergence baseline. The IMF figure is measured against a NO-AGING counterfactual; realized China growth of 4.4-4.5% in 2026 ALREADY contains the drag that has been running since the 2012 working-age peak. P2 constructed a "no-aging China of ~4.9% minus 2.7 = 2.2%" and then called the match with his bottom-up an "independent consistency check" — it is not independent, it is the same subtraction performed twice, and 2.2-2.4% for 2032-36 sits below every identified medium-term China path. P1 performed the identical subtraction from "a ~5% base." This one error costs the panel roughly 0.25-0.35 pp of CQ3 P50. (ii) DRAG/PULL ASYMMETRY, conceded in words and monetized at zero: P3 wrote "slightly up, nearly cancelling," P2 took +0.15 for healthy aging and then haircut his TFP term. But the locked 2A baseline is explicitly "absent productivity offsets," so crediting the locked +0.4 pp/yr healthy-aging effect is NOT double-counting — it is reading the prior as written. They also priced none of the mechanical composition gain (a shrinking labour force sheds its lowest-productivity marginal workers first, which raises measured output per hour with no technology at all) and none of the forced capital deepening when labour is the scarce factor. (iii) NARRATIVE COHERENCE MISTAKEN FOR LIKELIHOOD, and this is the tell: all three independently produced the SAME story (extreme relative-price dispersion, dull aggregate, B modal at 42-53) and all three cited the coherence of that story as support. The story is coherent. It is also exactly the story that the imputation structure of the index falsifies. Three panelists reaching the same conclusion from three different lenses is weak evidence when all three inherited the same measurement assumption from the effort brief's own phrasing ("can produce almost any core aggregate depending on weights") — the brief anchored them, and none of them audited the measurement of the cold leg. (iv) SCOPE INSENSITIVITY ON A FAT-TAILED AVERAGE: P2 asserted CQ5's conjunct A "requires seven years at ~112, i.e. a sustained high-vol regime, not spikes." False for an average. (3 yr at 90 + 1.5 yr at 175 + 5.5 yr at 100)/10 = 108. One 18-month fiscal/rates crisis clears the bar off a ~100 structural baseline. P3 made the mirror error, treating the compressed 2026 start (64-71) as near-dispositive while simultaneously asserting MOVE scales with the yield level — MOVE at 64-71 with G7 nominals at 3-4% is itself evidence against the level-scaling term he used to justify his own reference class. (v) ONE-SIDED CONJUNCTION HANDLING ON CQ1: P2 and P3 both argued that AI's entry-level displacement RAISES the J+K+M median (true), and neither noticed the symmetric effect on the other side of the differential — a rapidly expanding care workforce is expanded by low-wage ENTRANTS, which dilutes the F+Q median downward. The two composition effects roughly cancel. Their strongest argument against CQ1's second conjunct therefore does not survive, but neither does any composition tailwind for it.

WEIGHTING CONVENTION, THE POINT NOBODY FOLLOWED THROUGH. P2 did the single best piece of work in Wave 1: his OECD-38 GDP-weighted core lands at 2.503% and 0.552 pp of it comes from five high-inflation members (Turkiye, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica) at an ~8.5% weight. He then labelled it a knife-edge and moved on. But the brief's Section-3 accounting lock is constant 2025 USD PPP unless the index specifies otherwise, and on PPP those five carry roughly 11-12% of OECD-38 (Turkiye ~$3.5T, Mexico ~$3.4T PPP against OECD-38 PPP of ~$78-82T), not 8.5%. At ~6.5% each that line is 0.72-0.78 pp, not 0.552 — which moves his own aggregate from 2.50% to 2.67-2.73% before any of my measurement corrections. He found the decisive lever, called it a "measurement-convention question," and then declined to resolve it in the direction the brief's own lock points. That is anchoring on the obvious centre.

ATTACK ON THE MODEL'S CLOSURE (the Fermi seat used it; verified against /Users/adam/github/overlapping-generations/.claude/worktrees/demographic-ai-cross-impact-52e65e/scripts/tetlock-sim-adapter.ts and src/modules/production.ts, where gamma defaults to 0.55 with the inline note that "mainstream cost-share logic implies ~0.05-0.08"). (1) gamma=0.55 means the model MANUFACTURES GDP from electricity: output scales as E^0.55 in useful energy, so a scenario that builds datacenter load to 1,884 TWh (baseline) or 4,180 TWh (ai-energy-boom) by 2036 mechanically prints growth. Every CQ3 bound read off it is biased UPWARD, and the bias is largest in exactly the high-build scenarios the panel would otherwise treat as informative upside. P2 was right to refuse the point estimate. (2) But he then took the model's 2031 PPP weight split (0.629 OECD-proxy / 0.371 China) as a "cross-check on my own weights," and that is contaminated by the same channel: regional GDP levels at 2031 are OUTPUTS of the gamma loop, and China builds electricity faster than the OECD proxy, so the model's China weight is biased HIGH. The cross-check is not independent of the thing being checked. (3) The adapter's own UN-WPP-LOW disclosure is directionally WRONG for this window and P2 relied on it: post-2025 births do not enter the workforce before ~2045, so the low variant barely touches 2032-36 labour input, while fewer children RAISE measured GDP per capita and LOWER the child-cost claim on GDP. For a 2032-36 growth-rate question the low variant is neutral-to-mildly-upward, not "biased downward." Treating the disclosure as a conservatism buffer absorbed an upward bias as if it were a downward one. (4) The OECD-38 proxy (us + oecd-ex-us) drops Japan and Korea — the aging-drag exemplars, ~10% of OECD-38 PPP — AND Turkiye, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, the fast-growing high-inflation members at ~11-12% PPP. Those do not cancel: removing both tails leaves the central growth estimate roughly intact while understating VARIANCE, and it makes the proxy useless for anything inflation-weighted. (5) The model has no price level, so its 5.99-6.96% economy-wide real return is not commensurable with a sovereign real yield; P2's 450 bp wedge is a free parameter he chose, and the resulting 1.6-2.5% range brackets his own P50 by construction. He flagged it as "directional context only" and then reported it as "directionally supportive," which is the circularity surviving its own disclaimer.

PREMORTEM, UPPER TAIL (Dec 31 2036; the ensemble was badly wrong on the high side; coupled growth printed 2.8-3.1%, A was the answer, the panel's ~14% on A was absurd). The causal chain nobody modelled: the FISCAL SQUEEZE ITSELF forced the one reform that costs nothing — permitting and interconnection. By 2029 the queue that every Wave-1 panelist treated as a hard 4-7 year physical constant had been halved in the US, Germany and Japan because a government with net interest at 3% of GDP and no money for subsidy discovered that approvals are free. Electricity supply growth overshot demand growth from 2031, and the channel that was supposed to be a tax on core inflation (P3's +7.3% residential rates) turned into a real-income subsidy in the back half. Adoption came from the wage, not the model: OECD firms that could not hire adopted, so AI-Q2 cleared 50% and — critically — the diffusion landed in MARKET-measured sectors (logistics, prefabricated construction, utilities, retail, wholesale), not in the input-measured health/care/public-administration sectors that Wave 1 assumed would swallow it, so it registered as measured TFP at +0.65 pp/yr. Participation extension ran ahead of the healthy-aging prior as pension reform bit under fiscal duress, adding 0.5 pp to OECD labour input. China's property stock adjustment COMPLETED around 2030 (a stock adjustment is a level, not a perpetual flow — the point Wave 1 never made) and the household-income-share pivot lifted consumption 5 pp of GDP. Coupled growth 2.9%. Debt/GDP stabilized through the denominator. Every panelist who wrote "the demographic denominators are near-deterministic over 10 years" had confused the population projection, which is deterministic, with the labour INPUT and the output per unit of it, which are not.

PREMORTEM, LOWER TAIL (Dec 31 2036; badly wrong on the low side; coupled growth printed 0.8-1.1%, D was the answer, and my own 10 on D was the single worst number in this payload). The 2028-30 impairment arrived — AI-Q4's 66% was if anything too low — and it arrived SYNCHRONOUSLY with a sovereign funding accident. A failed long-bond auction in 2029, with the basis trade unwinding into forced Treasury selling and convenience yields gone, forced pro-cyclical consolidation at the exact moment the AI complex deleveraged. BIS Box C realized in full: the labour-income share fell, capital-concentrated output did not spend, and the demand shortfall was not a theory but an arithmetic identity. China's property adjustment metastasized into a balance-sheet recession with the pension subsidy (already 10.1% of fiscal expenditure) crowding out everything discretionary, and Chinese CPI averaged 0.3%. OECD core undershot to 1.6% because the post-bust excess capacity in compute, power and construction all cleared through price. My entire measurement attack was correct about the imputed components and irrelevant, because in a demand-deficient world shelter deflates too and the imputed lines follow the asset prices DOWN. The hot-core thesis was a 2027-2029 phenomenon mistaken for a decade.

SUMMARY OF MY DEVIATIONS FROM THE WAVE-1 CENTRE (CQ1 ~12, CQ2 ~24, CQ3 P50 ~1.8, CQ4 P50 ~2.1, CQ5 ~22, CQ6 ~14/47/19/20): CQ1 20 (up), CQ2 35 (up), CQ3 P50 2.1 (up), CQ4 P50 2.35 (up, right tail far fatter), CQ5 30 (up), CQ6 25/39/26/10 (A and C up hard, D down hard, B no longer modal by much). I split no differences.
wave2.cq1_reasoning:
Wave 1: 11 / 15 / 10. I am at 20 on one argument they all got wrong.

CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment averaging <=5.5% over 2032-36): MARGINAL 0.52. I do not take P2's 0.60. His labour-supply arithmetic ("-1.5% of LF at unchanged E lowers u by ~1.4 pp") treats employment as fixed while the labour force shrinks, which is not an identity, it is an assumption that labour demand is perfectly inelastic. The denominator is 20-64, and the policy response 2A locks (fiscal squeeze) is precisely the one that raises statutory retirement ages and participation, so the measured labour force shrinks more slowly than the headcount. Against that, two things Wave 1 underweighted: OECD-38 composition puts Spain, Greece, Turkiye, Colombia, Chile and Costa Rica in the aggregate, so the harmonized rate is levered to a southern-Europe/LatAm shock rather than to a US/German labour market; and the AI-Q5 displacement mechanism is concentrated in the 22-25 cohort, which is the most visible component of a harmonized rate. P1's recession arithmetic is right: a 5-year average starting from ~4.9-5.0% with one OECD-wide downturn lands at 5.6-5.8%. 0.52.

CONJUNCT B (F+Q real median hourly out-growing J+K+M by >=10.0 pp cumulative 2025-2036, i.e. ~0.87 pp/yr): MARGINAL 0.28, against their 0.17-0.20. Their collapse of this conjunct rests entirely on ONE assumption, stated most explicitly by P2 ("a fiscally constrained Baumol sector resolves excess demand as QUANTITY RATIONING ... rather than as a measured wage") and evidenced by P3 with Japan's 3.9x job-to-applicant ratio alongside care pay 60,000 yen below the all-industry average. The evidence is real and the inference is wrong about the TIME SHAPE. Administered prices are sticky in direction and then move in LEVEL JUMPS, because the political economy of a care-staffing collapse is a discrete statutory award, not a smooth market clearing: Germany legislated collective-agreement-level pay across all long-term-care facilities (Pflegelohnverbesserung, binding from Sept 2022), Japan's three-yearly kaigo fee revisions carry explicit earmarked wage-raise tranches, and the UK resolved its 2022-23 NHS dispute with a lump-sum-plus-uplift settlement after a decade of real decline. The fiscal constraint 2A locks caps the SHARE OF GDP spent on care; it does not cap the relative WAGE — a government that cannot expand volumes resolves an unfillable rota by raising unit pay and cutting coverage, which is exactly the direction this conjunct needs. An 11-year window is long enough to contain two or three such awards in most OECD-38 members. Offsetting, and this is the correction that keeps me at 0.28 rather than 0.40: P2 and P3's composition argument (truncating entry-level J+K+M raises its median) has a symmetric twin neither of them priced — a care workforce that expands fast expands through low-wage ENTRANTS, diluting the F+Q median downward. The two effects roughly cancel, so I get no composition tailwind either. Add P2's resolution fragility point (ISIC F/Q/J/K/M median hourly at this granularity lives mainly in the 4-yearly Eurostat SES), which is a genuine haircut. 0.28.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the whole failure, and it fails three times over, so I am close to Wave 1 here (4/8/6) and will not manufacture a disagreement. (1) The two labour pools do not intersect: a displaced 24-year-old analyst in ISIC J is not a licensed care worker, and the gap is a licensure, physical-presence and willingness gap, not a wage gap. (2) The flow sizes do not match in time: AI's cognitive savings are realized as a HIRING FREEZE on entrants (the observed mechanism is a ~14-16% entry-level hiring reduction for ages 22-25 in the most exposed roles), which withholds workers from the cognitive sector without delivering them anywhere, while care demand grows with the 80+ cohort at ~3.5%/yr. (3) The funding is administered: ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly financed into a fiscal squeeze that 2A locks, so even a willing worker needs a reimbursement schedule to be paid from. A weaker plank reading "AI white-collar labour savings eventually and partially free resources that can be taxed to fund elder care" would score 45-55. As stated, with "smoothly" and "supply the workers needed," 7. Note where I differ from Wave 1 in REASONING even while agreeing on the score: their collapse rested on fiscal quantity-rationing being permanent, and I think the fiscal cap binds on VOLUMES while unit wages jump in discrete statutory awards (see CQ1) — which is why my CQ1 is 20 and my score here is still 7. The plank fails on reallocation mechanics, not on the budget.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail, in opposite directions, and the plank needs both to hold. "BLOCKS" is false for the Philippines: the Philippine export is PHYSICAL care and maritime labour, which is the one category AI cannot substitute, and 2A's old-age ratio going 31% -> 39-41% is a demand PULL on exactly it — the binding constraint there is OECD visa policy and domestic political economy, not model capability. If anything the coupled 2027-2036 path is the best decade for Philippine labour export in its history, with the risk being that remittance-dependence deepens rather than that it is blocked. "SEVERELY" is where India fails: the compressible slice is voice, transaction-processing and L1 support, which is real and large, but India's offsetting build is the global-capability-centre model, where the export good is the ENGINEER WHO OPERATES the AI, not the seat-hour it replaces — that is a re-pricing and a move up the value chain, not a block. The plank also smuggles in a conjunction (both countries, both severely, via the same mechanism) and conjunctions of this shape are the thing this panel is instructed to discount. The defensible residual is a distributional claim: a cohort of Indian entry-level BPO and entry-level IT-services workers genuinely loses, and the Philippine virtual-services (BPO voice) segment genuinely compresses while the physical segment booms — which is a BARBELL inside each country, not severity. Wave 1 at 11/12/17; I am lower at 10 because none of them priced the physical-migration demand pull as a positive for the Philippines, they only declined to price it as a negative.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, and this is the plank where I break hardest from Wave 1 (58/55/54 -> 32). The first clause is nearly observed rather than forecast: US core PCE at 3.1% y/y in September 2026, euro-area national October 2026 flashes at 2.1-3.1% core, Spanish core at 3.1%. So the plank's credence is almost entirely about the second clause, and "falls in the 2030s" is doing work on a MEASURED AGGREGATE that I have argued is structurally hotter than the panel believes. Three reasons the fall does not arrive on the resolution measure. (1) The disinflating bloc is 0.08-0.12 of core and partly imputed counter-cyclically (asset-based portfolio-management fees, net-interest-margin-imputed banking, premiums-net-of-claims insurance), not 0.20-0.25 of core deflating at 0-1%. (2) Shelter at a 0.44 core-CPI weight does not disinflate in a world where aging raises households per capita and the grid build bids away construction labour — the demographic argument Wave 1 used to hold shelter down is wrong in sign. (3) On the PPP basis the brief locks, five high-inflation OECD-38 members carry ~11-12% of the aggregate at ~6.5%, contributing ~0.75 pp that no AI mechanism touches. The honest shape is a DECLINE from ~3.1% to ~2.7%, which is a fall in rate and a persistent overshoot of target, and the plank as stated reads as a return to the pre-2020 regime. I am not at 10 because the front-loading is real (the impulses genuinely are partly one-off level shifts) and because my own lower-tail premortem, in which post-bust excess capacity clears through price everywhere including shelter, is a live ~15-20% world where the plank is exactly right. 32.
hypothesis_critique.d:
"EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" both fail, and they fail in a way that is nearly undetectable because the plank is unfalsifiable as written. "EVENTUALLY" puts the claim outside the Dec 31 2036 resolution horizon, so the plank is compatible with ANY observation inside the window — a 2032-36 print of 0.9% is consistent with "eventually." "WINS" names no threshold: against what counterfactual, on what measure, for whom? Real GDP growth that is positive but slower than the 2015-19 trend both "outruns population decline" (output per capita rises) and loses on every intuition the plank is appealing to. And "EXPONENTIAL" is a category error about the economics rather than the technology: even granting exponential capability, the output channel runs through diffusion, complementary capital, electricity and the Hulten/Baumol measurement wall, every one of which is linear-at-best and several of which are administratively capped. Where I am above Wave 1 (13/14/14 -> 22): my own CQ3 P50 of 2.1% with a P90 of 3.1% and 25 on CQ6-A is a materially more growth-positive view than any of theirs, so a plank whose DIRECTION is "growth holds up despite the demographics" deserves more credence from me than from them. 22, and I would score a tightened version — "coupled OECD-38 + China real GDP growth over 2032-36 exceeds 2.0%/yr despite the demographic drag" — at about 55.

Note across the four planks: they are not independent. (a) and (d) both require AI's gains to land where they can be measured and spent; (c) and (d) pull against each other, since the growth that makes (d) true is the growth that keeps (c) false. A panel that scores them independently will produce an incoherent joint.

key_drivers: THE IMPUTATION STRUCTURE OF THE COLD LEG. All three Wave-1 panelists gave the AI-exposed bloc a 0.12-0.25 weight in OECD core running 0.0-1.0%. In core PCE that bloc is dominated by non-market-priced components — portfolio management priced as a share of assets under management (which INFLATES in an AI-capex equity boom), banking imputed through net interest margin (which widens on my CQ4 path), insurance as premiums net of claims, and professional services deflated by cost-based PPI proxies where a labour-cost fall is booked as lower real OUTPUT rather than lower price. The genuinely deflatable slice is ~0.08-0.12. Correcting only this adds +0.20 to +0.35 pp to every Wave-1 core build and is the single reason my CQ2 is 35 and my CQ6-C is 26.

THE PPP WEIGHTING CONVENTION. P2 found that 0.552 pp of his 2.503% OECD-38 core comes from five high-inflation members at an ~8.5% market-GDP weight, called it a convention question and stopped. On the constant-2025-USD-PPP basis the brief itself locks, Turkiye, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica carry ~11-12% of OECD-38 PPP and contribute 0.72-0.78 pp. That reweighting alone takes his knife-edge to 2.67-2.73% before any other correction. The LEVEL question is substantially decided by an accounting lock the panel treated as an aside.

THE DOUBLE-COUNTED AGING DRAG. All three subtracted 2A's -1.1 pp global / -2.7 pp China from a convergence baseline, and P2 certified the result by reproducing it twice ('the two routes agree'). The IMF figure is measured against a NO-AGING counterfactual; realized 2026 growth of 4.4-4.5% already embeds the drag running since China's 2012 working-age peak. Taking the deduction once puts China at 3.0-3.4% for 2032-36 rather than 2.2-2.4%, worth ~0.25-0.35 pp on the coupled P50 and the whole of my gap to their CQ3 and my elevated CQ6-A.

THE UNPRICED DEMAND PULL, MONETIZED. 2A's baseline is stated 'absent productivity offsets', so crediting the locked healthy-aging result is reading the prior as written, not double-counting it — P2 took +0.15 and P3 'part'. Add two channels none of them priced at all: a shrinking labour force sheds its lowest-productivity marginal workers first (measured output per hour rises with no technology), and capital deepening per worker is forced rather than chosen when labour binds. Together +0.40 pp on the OECD leg.

FAT-TAILED AVERAGES, which is where Wave 1's CQ5 reasoning broke in both directions. P2 claimed MOVE >=105 over a decade 'requires seven years at ~112, not spikes'; one 18-month crisis at 175 on a ~100 baseline clears it ((3x90 + 1.5x175 + 5.5x100)/10 = 108). P3 treated the compressed 2026 start as near-dispositive while asserting MOVE scales with the yield level, which his own datum (MOVE 64-71 with G7 nominals at 3-4%) refutes. With a correlation of +0.50 between the conjuncts, CQ5 is close to P(fiscal/rates crisis decade) and sits at 30.

ADMINISTERED PRICES MOVE IN JUMPS, NOT SMOOTHLY OR NEVER. Wave 1 collapsed CQ1's second conjunct to 0.17-0.20 on a shared assumption that a fiscally constrained Baumol sector resolves excess demand as quantity rationing. The fiscal cap binds on the care SHARE OF GDP, not on the relative WAGE: a state that cannot expand volumes resolves an unfillable rota by raising unit pay and cutting coverage, in discrete statutory awards (Germany's 2022 collective-agreement mandate for all LTC facilities, Japan's earmarked kaigo fee tranches, the UK's 2023 settlement after a decade of real decline). An 11-year window holds two or three such awards in most members. Offsetting, and the reason I stop at 0.28: a fast-expanding care workforce dilutes the F+Q median with low-wage entrants, cancelling the entry-level-truncation argument that P2 and P3 ran only on the J+K+M side.

wave2.coupling_tension:
FOUR TENSIONS. The first is the one where I break 180 degrees from a UNANIMOUS Wave-1 verdict, so I lead with it.

(1) AI-Q3 IS TOO LOW, NOT TOO HIGH — UPWARD, AND ALL THREE WAVE-1 PANELISTS GOT THE SIGN WRONG TOGETHER. P1 shaded the 2036 OECD-38+China strict operational figure to ~850 TWh, P2 to 820-860, P3 to 850-900. Unanimity across three independent lenses is exactly the pattern a red team should distrust, and here it rests on two assumptions neither of them stated. First, ALL THREE TREAT DATA-CENTRE LOAD AS A DISCRETIONARY MARGINAL ADDITION whose demand curve slopes against the hurdle rate (P1, P2) or against retail-rate politics (P3). Once demographics are endogenous it is not: a shrinking OECD labour force makes compute a LABOUR SUBSTITUTE, so its demand is derived from the wage, and the wage is the one price 2A guarantees is rising. That is the demand pull all three conceded in prose and then omitted from the TWh number — the identical drag/pull asymmetry the brief warns about, committed on the quantity rather than on the growth rate. Second, and this is the sharper error: ALL THREE READ AI-Q4 AS THE COMPLEMENT OF AI-Q3. P2 states they 'cannot both be comfortably true'; P1 calls the joint 'internally slack'. But AI-Q4 resolves on IMPAIRMENTS, CANCELLATIONS and a revenue-to-D&A ratio — accounting events — while AI-Q3 resolves on STRICT OPERATIONAL ELECTRICITY, a physical flow. A written-down data centre still runs. Worse for their reading, an impairment cycle RAISES operational load per dollar of capex through two channels: distressed compute is cheap compute, which lifts utilization from the 70-85% band P2 assumed toward the 90%+ that a marginal-cost operator runs; and impaired assets transfer from balance-sheet-constrained builders to operators whose business is running them hot. The 2026-2029 tranche is already contracted under take-or-pay power agreements, so the near tail is energized regardless of the financing shock — P1 saw this ('the P10 barely moving') and then cut the P10 from 596.8 to ~500 anyway, which contradicts his own mechanism. Add that roughly half the AI-Q3 aggregate is CHINA, where the build is state-directed and electricity-price-inelastic, and P3's retail-rate-politics veto — which is a real and well-evidenced constraint on US interconnection — applies to maybe a third of the measure. DIRECTION: I resolve the tension against the Wave-1 consensus and against the locked prior in the OPPOSITE direction from all of them: coupled, the 2036 OECD-38 + China strict operational P50 should be ~1,050-1,100 TWh (vs the locked 998.2), with the P10 LIFTED to ~680 (the contracted tranche plus China's state build is a hard floor the ensemble's 596.8 does not respect) and the P90 roughly unchanged at ~1,550 (the physical constraints P2 priced correctly — 9.3 GW/yr of firm capacity, 4-7 year interconnection queues, 2-4 year HV transformer lead times — do bind the upside, they just do not bind the centre). This is also the single coupling claim of mine most exposed to falsification, which is why it is signpost 5.

(2) AI-Q1 IS TOO LOW, AND THE HULTEN/BAUMOL HAIRCUT IS AN ASSUMPTION MASQUERADING AS AN ACCOUNTING FACT — UPWARD. P2 lowered AI-Q1 from 23.0% to ~21% and P3 raised it only to ~25%, both reasoning that the demographic pull directs AI into health, long-term care, education and public administration, whose output is measured by input, so diffusion registers as spending rather than measured TFP. That mechanism is real and it is also a CHOICE OF WHERE THE SHORTAGE BINDS. 2A's locked labour-force contraction binds just as hard in logistics, warehousing, wholesale, retail, utilities, prefabricated construction and field maintenance — all market-measured, all with output priced at market, all currently among the least AI-diffused. P2 then compounded the error by taking +0.31 pp from AI-Q6's own regime weights and haircutting it by -0.05 for the measurement wall he had already assumed. DIRECTION: coupled, AI-Q1 should read ~29-31%, up from 23.0%, because the pull operates on the SHADOW WAGE and the shadow wage is highest where the measurement is cleanest. This is the main reason my CQ3 P50 is 2.1 against their 1.6-2.0 and my CQ6-A is 25 against their 9-17. Corollary for AI-Q2: both coupled estimates that raised it (P2 to ~27-28%, P3 implicitly) are right in direction and for the right reason — a cheap software tool is far more elastic to a wage signal than aggregate TFP is — so the widening wedge between adoption BREADTH and MEASURED PRODUCTIVITY is real; I just think the wedge is narrower than they do, because they placed all the diffusion in the input-measured sectors.

(3) AI-Q5 IS ROUGHLY RIGHT AS STATED, AND THE TWO WAVE-1 CORRECTIONS CANCEL — NO DIRECTION, WHICH IS ITSELF THE FINDING. P1 raised AI-Q5 from 38.2% to ~46% on a denominator argument (hyperscaler rents inflate sector J's GVA with no cognitive wage decline, and aging mechanically feeds it by pushing a growing retirement-asset pool into intangible-rent sectors as safe-asset r* compresses). P2 and P3 instead flagged that AI-Q5 and CQ1's second conjunct are ANTI-correlated through a composition identity: truncating the bottom of the J+K+M distribution lowers the compensation share while raising the measured median. Both corrections are right, they are about different quantities, and the ensemble should apply both — AI-Q5 up to ~44-46 on the denominator, CQ1's J+K+M leg NOT helped by it. But neither P2 nor P3 noticed the symmetric composition effect on the OTHER side of CQ1's differential: a care workforce that expands fast expands through low-wage entrants, which dilutes the F+Q median downward by a comparable magnitude. So the composition channel is a WASH for CQ1 and cannot be used in either direction, which is why my CQ1 rests on administered-wage level jumps alone and lands at 20 rather than at 30. DIRECTION: AI-Q5 up to ~45; zero net transmission to CQ1.

(4) 2A's OWN r IDENTITY IS NOT A CONSTRAINT, IT IS A FUNCTION OF THE DRAG THE PANEL DOUBLE-COUNTED — UPWARD ON CQ4. P2 published dr = d(r-g) + dg = +1.0 - 1.1 = -0.1 pp as a 'hard constraint I publish rather than override', concluding that the locked demographic block implies r roughly flat. The arithmetic is correct and the input is not his to choose: he computed dg from the -1.1 pp drag that I have argued is measured against a no-aging counterfactual rather than against realized growth. On my CQ3, where the growth decline from the current ~2.7% basket run rate to 2.1% is ~0.6 pp rather than ~1.1 pp, the SAME locked identity yields dr = +1.0 - 0.6 = +0.4 pp from demographics alone. The locked priors therefore contain an upward demographic contribution to r that all three panelists read as zero or negative, purely as a downstream consequence of the drag double-count. Combined with the AI/grid saving-investment demand (+0.25) and a one-directional term premium (+0.60), and net of the breakeven-under-adjustment channel that mechanically damps a MEASURED real yield in a hot regime (-0.35, the one Wave-1 insight that cuts against my own thesis and that only P3 named), this is why my CQ4 P50 is 2.35 against their 2.10-2.15 and my P90 is 4.0 against their 3.3-3.6. The joint distribution implied by 2A as the panel read it — flat r, collapsing g, exploding debt, eroding convenience yields, a $1.4T commitment stack on $300B of equity — is not a coherent asset market; something has to give, and in the locked priors the thing that gives is the term premium.

wave3.lens_self_description: I am the effort-level posterior: I reconciled the five prior panelists of Effort 2 by weighting each lens on the specific quality of its argument question by question and then enforced arithmetic coherence across my own six answers, which forbade me from introducing any new evidence, reference class or mechanism of my own, and equally forbade me from averaging where one panelist was simply right and the others simply wrong.
wave3.cq1_reasoning:
Wave spread 8/10/11/15/20. CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonized u <=5.5% avg 2032-36) = 0.54. I reject Fermi's 0.60: his "-1.5% of LF at unchanged E lowers u by ~1.4pp" treats employment as fixed while the labour force shrinks, which is an assumption about perfectly inelastic labour demand, not an identity — the Red-Teamer killed it and I move with him. I keep Fermi's slack-year framing as structure (one year at 7.0% plus four at 4.8% averages 5.24%, PASSES; two at 7.0% gives 5.68%, FAILS), so A = P(fewer than two badly-slack years in five) off a 4.9-5.0% Aug-2026 observed level. I add the Red-Teamer's genuinely new composition point, which no Wave-1 lens had: OECD-38 includes Spain, Greece, Turkiye, Colombia, Chile and Costa Rica, so the harmonized aggregate is levered to a southern-Europe/LatAm shock rather than to a US/German labour market. Historian's recession arithmetic (one OECD-wide downturn lifts a window starting at 4.9-5.0% to 5.6-5.8%) stands unrebutted. 0.54.
CONJUNCT B (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >=10.0pp cumulative, i.e. ~0.87pp/yr for 11 years) = 0.22. This is where Wave 2 produced its best exchange and I move materially off the Wave-1 centre of 0.17-0.20 without going to the Red-Teamer's 0.28. I REJECT the Bayesian Updater's 0.11: he spent likelihood ratios 0.70 (administered-price suppression) and 0.60 (entry-level truncation raising the J+K+M median) and took the conjunct to 0.079 before rounding up. The Red-Teamer landed a clean hit on the second of those: a fast-expanding care workforce expands through low-wage ENTRANTS, which dilutes the F+Q median downward by a comparable magnitude, so the median-composition channel is a WASH and cannot be spent against the conjunct at all. That removes the entire basis of the Bayesian's -3 move. The Red-Teamer's second hit is also real and specific: administered prices are sticky in direction and then move in discrete statutory LEVEL JUMPS (Germany's collective-agreement mandate across all LTC facilities binding from Sept 2022, Japan's three-yearly kaigo fee revisions with earmarked wage tranches, the UK's 2023 NHS lump-sum-plus-uplift settlement after a decade of real decline), and an 11-year window holds two or three such awards in most members; the locked fiscal constraint caps the care SHARE OF GDP, not the relative WAGE — a state that cannot expand volumes resolves an unfillable rota by raising unit pay and cutting coverage. But three unrebutted discounts keep me well below 0.28: statutory awards are one-off 3-8% level steps, so two or three deliver 8-15pp of care-wage gain against a bar that needs 10pp on the whole F+Q aggregate; construction is the other half of F+Q and Fermi's point that AI-Q4's 66% impairment lands in ISIC F during exactly 2032-36 was never answered; ISIC M receives a positive demand pull from the grid/DC build (engineering, architecture, project management), which Fermi raised and nobody rebutted; and the resolution quantity is effectively unmeasured (Scout, verbatim: "I did not find a 2026 year-over-year growth rate broken out for each of the four sectors"; ISIC F/Q/J/K/M median hourly at this granularity lives mainly in the 4-yearly Eurostat SES). 0.22.
CORRELATION +0.22 (Wave range +0.15 to +0.25). Positive: a tight market is the only historical state in which manual/care relative wages rise and is also the state that forces the statutory award. Negative: an AI-displacement state that compresses J+K+M raises mismatch unemployment, and a care-wage surge large enough to clear 10pp co-occurs with the tightening that lifts u.
JOINT = 0.54 x 0.22 + 0.22 x sqrt(0.54x0.46x0.22x0.78) = 0.1188 + 0.22 x 0.2065 = 0.1188 + 0.0454 = 0.164 -> 16.
wave3.cq2_reasoning:
Wave spread 14/24/32/34/35. I land at 32 and decompose it differently from every panelist who reached a similar number.
CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE >=2.50%/yr avg 2027-2036) = 0.64. The decisive fact is the one Fermi found and labelled a "measurement-convention question" before moving on: the OECD-38 aggregate is not the core-OECD aggregate. Historian's 2.14% composite is a correct answer to a different question. I carry the weights explicitly, and I resolve the convention Fermi declined to resolve — but only halfway, against the Red-Teamer. On MARKET GDP the five high-inflation members (Turkiye, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica) are ~7-8.5% of OECD-38; on the constant-2025-USD-PPP basis Section 3 locks they are ~11% ($8.9T of ~$87T PPP: Turkiye ~3.6, Mexico ~3.3, Colombia ~1.1, Chile ~0.7, Costa Rica ~0.16). The lock's own exception clause is triggered by CQ2's named index (local core CPI/PCE), so whether the WEIGHTS follow PPP is genuinely undetermined by the question text — the Red-Teamer asserts PPP as settled and it is not. I therefore carry ~10% as the expectation over conventions. Bloc rate: PPP-internal weights Turkiye 0.40 / Mexico 0.37 / Colombia 0.12 / Chile 0.08 / CR 0.02 at 12 / 4 / 4.5 / 3.5 / 2.5 gives 7.15%/yr over a decade whose first three years still contain double-digit Turkish inflation. Bloc contribution 0.60-0.80pp; I use 0.70pp. MY BASKET BUILD, carrying the Red-Teamer's imputation correction at HALF strength. He is right that the Wave-1 cold leg is overstated: in core PCE the AI-exposed bloc is dominated by non-market-priced lines — portfolio management and investment advice priced as a share of AUM (which INFLATES in an AI-capex equity boom), financial services imputed through net interest margin (which widens on my CQ4 path), P&C insurance as premiums net of claims, and professional services deflated by cost-based PPI proxies where a labour-input-cost fall is booked as lower real OUTPUT rather than lower price. He is also right on the shelter SIGN: aging RAISES households per capita (widowhood, single occupancy, aging-in-place suppressing turnover and therefore effective supply) — Japan's household count rose for roughly two decades past its population peak — so Historian's use of suppressed household formation to hold shelter down is wrong-signed. But he over-applies both at once and ignores a third weight that cuts the other way: euro-area HICP core carries only ~7% rent, because owner-occupied housing is excluded, so the euro leg is structurally low-beta to exactly the shelter channel he is levering, and the imputed financial lines are an ~0.08 weight in core PCE, not a decisive bloc. US core CPI convention: shelter 0.44x3.2 = 1.41 + medical/care 0.11x3.3 = 0.36 + other services 0.24x2.5 = 0.60 + core goods 0.21x0.5 = 0.105 = 2.48%. US core PCE convention: shelter 0.18x3.2 = 0.58 + health 0.17x2.9 = 0.49 + financial/insurance 0.08x2.8 = 0.22 + other services 0.33x2.4 = 0.79 + core goods 0.24x0.4 = 0.10 = 2.18%. Blend (core CPI has historically run ~0.3pp above core PCE) -> US 2.40%. PPP-weighted OECD-38: US 0.344x2.40 = 0.826; euro-area members 0.258x2.10 = 0.542; Japan 0.079x1.80 = 0.142; UK 0.050x2.60 = 0.130; Korea 0.039x2.00 = 0.078; Canada 0.031x2.30 = 0.071; Australia 0.022x2.60 = 0.057; the five high-inflation members 0.102x7.00 = 0.714; Poland 0.022x3.00 = 0.066; remainder 0.053x2.40 = 0.127. SUM = 2.65%. Time profile: 2027-2030 ~2.85%, 2031-2036 ~2.47% (the impulses — grid/power capex crowding, business-electricity pass-through into services input costs, the tariff/fragmentation LEVEL shift, the first care-wage wave — are front-loaded and partly one-off; the EM contribution decays only as Turkiye disinflates, which is slow). Sigma on a 10-year average ~0.38. P(>=2.50) = 1 - Phi((2.50-2.65)/0.38) = 0.65; I shade to 0.64 for the Bayesian's correlated-evidence discipline, which is the reason I am not at the Red-Teamer's 0.72: he multiplies three one-directional corrections (full imputation, shelter 3.5, PPP EM weights) as if independent, which is precisely the failure the Bayesian avoided by collapsing four hot core prints into one LR-2.2 cluster instead of a product of ~4.5.
CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI <1.50%/yr avg 2027-2036) = 0.47, below the Wave-1 centre. The plank also smuggles in a conjunction — both countries, both severely, via one mechanism. I score 12, mid-panel: the virtual compression is real and locally concentrated (the 2-3 million-person entry-level BPO cohort, and BPO-exposed Philippine provinces without seafaring exposure), which is why I am above the Red-Teamer's 10 and below the Scout's 17.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, with "HOT" a secondary offender for being unquantified, and this is the plank where the panel split hardest (58/57/55/54 in Wave 1 and the Bayesian, against the Red-Teamer's 32). I land at 45, moving materially toward the Red Team without adopting his number. The plank's SHAPE is right and is close to my own central path: my build has GDP-weighted OECD-38 core at ~2.85%/yr over 2027-2030 and ~2.47%/yr over 2031-2036, so hot-then-cooler is what I actually forecast, and the first clause is nearly observed rather than predicted (US core PCE +3.1% y/y September 2026 with +0.3% m/m, BEA release 29 October 2026, "the same pace as a revised reading for August"; Spanish core 3.1%, German core ex food and energy +2.1% in October 2026). What the plank gets wrong is the DESTINATION, and the Red-Teamer's three reasons are each partly right: the genuinely market-priced, genuinely AI-deflatable slice of core is nearer 0.08-0.12 than the 0.20-0.25 Wave 1 assumed, because portfolio management is priced on AUM, banking is imputed through net interest margin, insurance is premiums net of claims, and much of professional services is deflated by cost-based PPI proxies where a labour-cost fall books as lower real OUTPUT; the demographic argument used to hold shelter down is wrong in sign, since aging raises households per capita and suppresses turnover; and on the PPP basis the brief locks, five high-inflation OECD-38 members carry ~11% of the aggregate at ~7%, contributing ~0.70pp that no AI mechanism touches. So the honest shape is a decline from ~2.85% to ~2.45%, a fall in the RATE and a persistent ~0.45pp overshoot of target. I do not go to 32 because the Red-Teamer scores the plank against a destination it does not state: "falls in the 2030s" is literally true on my own path, and he additionally ignores that euro-area HICP core carries only ~7% rent, which structurally damps the very shelter channel he levers. The plank is right about direction and wrong about amplitude at both ends — "hot" overstates 2027-2030, which is better described as sticky-above-target than accelerating, and "falls" understates where it settles. 45.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" both fail, and "EXPONENTIAL" carries a category error. EVENTUALLY is the word that makes the plank unfalsifiable inside the resolution lock: with no date, a 2032-36 print of 0.9% is consistent with it, so as a forecast it is empty rather than wrong, and I score only the testable reading — aggregate real GDP growth beating the demographic drag by Dec 31 2036. On that reading the arithmetic says no, and the arithmetic is not a judgment about capability: the basket runs ~2.54%/yr today (0.67x1.6 OECD plus 0.33x4.45 China) and my CQ3 P50 for 2032-36 is 1.75%, a decline of ~0.79pp, with the probability-weighted AI TFP offset computed off AI-Q6's own regime weights at only +0.31pp plus ~+0.11pp of capital deepening. WINS is undefined in three ways the plank needs resolved: against which counterfactual, on levels or on growth rates, and for whom — AI can raise the LEVEL of GDP permanently while the growth RATE still falls, which is the modal outcome and which the plank would score as a loss. EXPONENTIAL is the category error: compute and parameter counts are exponential, but the measured-output channel runs through diffusion, complementary capital, electricity, interconnection queues and the Hulten/Baumol measurement wall, every one of which is linear at best and several of which are administratively capped, so an exponential input maps to a roughly logarithmic measured-GDP output — and the mapping gets WORSE as aging shifts composition toward sectors whose output is measured by their input. The observed adoption telemetry is consistent with the ceiling rather than the exponential: Census BTOS national AI use 19.8% as of 3 May 2026 with Information at 39.7% and Finance at 33.9%, where "neither sector shifted significantly since December", and part of the headline rise reflects the November 2025 question change from "producing goods or services" to "any business function" rather than adoption. I score 15, above the Wave-1 cluster of 13-14 because my own CQ3 P50 of 1.75% and CQ6-A of 15 is a more growth-positive view than theirs, and well below the Red-Teamer's 22 because his 22 rests on a China leg (3.0-3.4%) I judged 0.55pp too high. A tightened version — coupled OECD-38 plus China real growth exceeding 2.0%/yr over 2032-36 despite the demographic drag — I would score ~45.

key_drivers: THE OECD-38 MEMBERSHIP WEIGHT, which is arithmetic the question set invites and the Wave-1 panel treated as an aside. Five high-inflation members (Turkiye, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica) carry ~7-8.5% of OECD-38 on market GDP and ~11% on the constant-2025-USD-PPP basis Section 3 locks ($8.9T of ~$87T), and at ~7%/yr they contribute 0.60-0.80pp to GDP-weighted core. Strip them and the aggregate is ~1.95%; include them and it is ~2.65%. This single term is the whole distance between Historian's CQ2 of 14 and my 32, and roughly half the B-versus-C margin in CQ6. It is also the reason CQ6-D's sub-2.00% core condition is a three-way conjunction rather than a single call, which is why D is 13 and not the 17-22 of Wave 1.

CORE-BASKET CONSTRUCTION ON BOTH LEGS, which is the separation of LEVEL from SKEW my effort exists to make. The HOT leg sits substantially outside the measure: US core CPI, core PCE and euro HICP core all EXCLUDE household electricity and gas, construction reaches core only through shelter rent/OER, and ISIC Q prices are administered by fiscally constrained authorities — so the observed +7.3% y/y US residential electricity rise reaches the resolution measure only as second-round business cost. But the COLD leg is smaller and partly counter-cyclically hot than Wave 1 assumed: the genuinely market-priced, genuinely AI-deflatable slice is ~0.08-0.12 of core rather than 0.20-0.25, because portfolio management is priced on AUM, banking is imputed through net interest margin, insurance is premiums net of claims, and professional services are deflated by cost-based PPI proxies. Net of both corrections the 2032-36 central is 2.45%: extreme relative-price dispersion with a moderately-above-target aggregate.

CHINA'S PPP WEIGHT TIMES ITS GROWTH PATH, WITH THE AGING DRAG COUNTED ONCE. 0.33 x 2.65%/yr carries my CQ3 P50 and therefore CQ6-A and CQ6-D. The locked -2.7pp/yr is measured against a NO-AGING counterfactual while the realized 4.4-4.5% of 2026 already embeds the drag running since the 2012 working-age peak, so Fermi's 2.2% double-subtracts and the Red-Teamer's 3.0-3.4% under-subtracts the intensifying 2032-36 slice plus ordinary convergence deceleration. 2.65% is +0.45pp on Fermi and -0.55pp on the Red Team and is the largest single judgment in my payload.

THE DECADE BAR ON CHINA HEADLINE CPI IS TIGHTER THAN THE JAPAN ANALOGUE IMPLIES, but not for the reason the Scout gave. The PPI sign flip carries a weak likelihood ratio (China ran PPI ~+6.3% in 2017 with CPI +1.6% and ~+8.1% in 2021 with CPI +0.9%, so P(PPI spike | low CPI) is high) and the +5.0% September 2026 print is single-source and unconfirmed. What does the work is that four years at the observed ~0.9-1.2% leaves the remaining six needing under ~1.7% in exactly the window where the locked demographics flip the labour sign (-60M population, worker/retiree 4.4 -> 2.8) and the property STOCK adjustment plausibly completes. 0.47, a near coin-flip rather than the 0.55-0.58 of the Japan reference class.

THE G7 REAL-YIELD ANCHOR IS A MARKET PRICE, NOT A RECONSTRUCTION, AND IT IS 1.95% RATHER THAN THE LOCKED 2.60% US TIPS. Observed Bund 10y at 3.28% (highest since May 2011) and JGB 10y at 3.000% (first time since 1996) put non-US G7 reals at ~1.0-1.3%, not the 0.3-0.5% assumed in the lowest Wave-1 anchor. Everything in CQ4 is a drift off 1.95: a one-directional term premium (+0.45), a much smaller Japan repression wedge than Wave 1 applied (the 3.00% JGB falsifies -100bp), and the one channel that damps a hawkish view — if realized inflation runs above breakevens, the MEASURED nominal-minus-breakeven real yield falls even in a hot regime (-0.20).

FAT-TAILED AVERAGES AND ONE UNOBSERVABLE CONDITIONAL CARRY CQ5. A 120-month MOVE mean of 105 does not need seven years at 112; (3yr at 75 + 1.5yr at 170 + 5.5yr at 95)/10 = 100.3 on a baseline the compressed 2026 start (64-71 with G7 nominals already at 3-4%) argues is policy-certainty-driven and therefore mean-reverting. Everything else sits in P(bonds fail to fall >=50bp | equity drawdown), where the full-sample 1970-2025 record says ~5 of 9 and the capex-bust-is-disinflationary coupling argument says ~0.38. No 2026 observable discriminates, and I sit at 0.43.

wave3.coupling_tension:
FOUR TENSIONS, EACH WITH A DIRECTION, AND I LEAD WITH THE ONE WHERE MY EFFORT SPLIT 4-1 AND I ADJUDICATE AGAINST BOTH SIDES.

(1) AI-Q3: THE WAVE-1 UNANIMOUS SHADE-DOWN WAS AN ERROR OF DEGREE AND THE RED TEAM'S INVERSION OVERSHOT — NET P50 ROUGHLY UNCHANGED, LEFT TAIL UP, RIGHT TAIL SLIGHTLY DOWN. All three Wave-1 lenses independently cut the 2036 OECD-38 + China strict operational figure to 820-900 TWh against the locked P50 of 998.2, and the Bayesian endorsed ~850. The Red-Teamer argued the opposite, to ~1,050-1,100 with the P10 lifted to ~680. He lands two hits that the unanimity conceals. First, AI-Q4 IS NOT THE COMPLEMENT OF AI-Q3: AI-Q4 resolves on impairments, cancellations and a revenue-to-D&A ratio, which are accounting events, while AI-Q3 resolves on strict operational ELECTRICITY, a physical flow — a written-down data centre still runs, and an impairment cycle plausibly RAISES operational load per dollar of capex, because distressed compute is cheap compute (lifting utilization from the 70-85% band Fermi assumed) and impaired assets transfer from balance-sheet-constrained builders to operators whose business is running them hot. Fermi's claim that the two "cannot both be comfortably true" and the Historian's "internally slack" are therefore both wrong as stated. Second, roughly half the measure is CHINA, where the build is state-directed and electricity-price-inelastic, so the Scout's retail-rate-politics veto — which is real, well-evidenced and demographically amplified, since the locked old-age ratio moving 31% to 39-41% grows the fixed-nominal-income voter bloc least able to absorb a bill increase and most reliably mobilized — applies to perhaps a third of the measure, not to all of it. He also correctly caught the Historian contradicting his own mechanism: having observed that the already-committed 2026-2029 tranche energizes regardless of a financing shock, the Historian cut the P10 from 596.8 to ~500 anyway. AGAINST HIM: the physical ceiling that Fermi priced correctly is unrebutted — +633 TWh over twelve years is ~53 TWh/yr of new load, ~9.3 GW/yr of firm capacity at a 65% load factor, claiming ~10-18% of OECD+China net firm additions against interconnection queues of 4-7 years and HV transformer lead times of 2-4 years — and Microsoft's observed cut of CY2026 capex to ~$170bn was attributed to "delays in third-party data-center capacity", i.e. a PHYSICAL constraint, which is evidence for the ceiling rather than for the financing story either side was arguing. I resolve close to the locked prior: P50 ~950 TWh, P10 LIFTED to ~640 (the contracted take-or-pay tranche plus China's state build is a harder floor than 596.8 respects), P90 ~1,480 (the queue and transformer arithmetic binds the upside even though it does not bind the centre). THE FINDING SPECIFIC TO MY EFFORT, which I take from the Bayesian and which no standalone marginal can see: AI-Q3 and OECD core inflation are POSITIVELY coupled, not independent, because household electricity is excluded from core while BUSINESS electricity is not — it arrives inside core services prices as an input cost. So the locked AI-Q3 P50 and a sub-2.50% core are LESS jointly likely than the product of the two marginals, and any coupled estimate that shades AI-Q3 down should shade CQ2's conjunct A down with it. By that argument my own conjunct A of 0.64 is 1-2 points generous, and I say so rather than hide it.

(2) AI-Q5 IS TOO LOW AND SHOULD READ ~45, BUT IT TRANSMITS EXACTLY ZERO TO CQ1 — UPWARD ON AI-Q5, NEUTRAL ON CQ1, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ANTI-DOUBLE-COUNTING WARNING MY EFFORT PRODUCES. The Historian's denominator argument is right: the J/K/M labour compensation SHARE can fall purely through nominal GVA growth, since hyperscaler rents inflate sector J's GVA with no cognitive wage declining at all, and aging feeds this mechanically by pushing a growing retirement-asset pool into intangible-rent sectors as the safe-asset leg of r* compresses (consistent with the locked identity leaving r roughly flat even while the term premium rises). AI-Q6's own modal cell, Jagged Diffusion and Hyperscaler Rent Concentration at 47.2%, is a RENT regime, and a rent is a price that does not deflate into measured real output. So AI-Q5 goes to ~45. But Fermi and the Scout then established that AI-Q5 and CQ1's second conjunct are ANTI-correlated through a composition identity, because the observed displacement mechanism is an entry-level hiring collapse (~14-16% for ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed roles) and truncating the bottom of the J+K+M wage distribution LOWERS its compensation share while RAISING its measured median hourly wage: AI-Q5 being TRUE makes CQ1 HARDER, and any panelist who raises CQ1 because they believe AI-Q5 has the sign backwards. The Bayesian spent that identity as a likelihood ratio of 0.60 and took CQ1 to 8. THE RED TEAM THEN KILLED THAT SPEND, and this is the best single move in Wave 2: the symmetric effect on the OTHER side of the differential is unpriced — a care workforce that expands fast expands through low-wage ENTRANTS, diluting the F+Q median downward by a comparable magnitude. The composition channel is a WASH. It cannot be used in either direction, which is why my CQ1 of 16 rests on administered-wage level jumps alone and why I reversed most of the Bayesian's downward move while keeping his direction on the fiscal channel.

(3) AI-Q1 UP MODESTLY TO ~26 AND AI-Q2 UP TO ~27, WIDENING THE WEDGE BETWEEN DIFFUSION BREADTH AND MEASURED PRODUCTIVITY — WHICH IS WHY B CARRIES 50. Fermi and the Bayesian lowered AI-Q1 to ~21 on the Hulten/Baumol wall (the demographic pull directs AI into health, long-term care, education and public administration, whose output is measured by input, so diffusion registers as spending rather than as TFP); the Scout raised it to ~25; the Red-Teamer to ~29-31. He is right that the haircut is a CHOICE OF WHERE THE SHORTAGE BINDS and that the locked labour-force contraction binds just as hard in logistics, warehousing, wholesale, retail, utilities, prefabricated construction and field maintenance — all market-measured, all priced at market, all among the least diffused. He is wrong to take it to zero, because the EMPLOYMENT mass of the shortage is in care, and AI-Q1 is a PPP-weighted aggregate in which the input-measured sectors carry a large and growing weight. ~26. AI-Q2 goes to ~27 on a point every lens conceded in prose: firm adoption of a cheap software tool is far more elastic to a wage signal than aggregate measured TFP is, and the old-age ratio moving 31% to 39-41% is precisely a rising shadow wage on the marginal worker. Broad adoption compatible with an unimpressive measured aggregate is the Jagged Diffusion cell, and it is the reason CQ6-A is only 15 while B is 50.

(4) THE DEEPEST TENSION IS BETWEEN THE LOCKED MARGINALS AND THE RESOLUTION MEASURE ITSELF, AND IT RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE — WHICH IS A FINDING ABOUT THE QUESTION SET RATHER THAN A FORECAST. If the TFP lift does not arrive (77% per AI-Q1), then 2A's aging drag plus the BIS Box C labour-income demand deficit plus China's overcapacity export deflation should make OECD core UNDERSHOOT, so the stagflation cell cannot be demand-driven at all: its inflation must come entirely from supply walls in grid, care and construction. But those walls sit largely OUTSIDE the resolution measure — household electricity and gas are excluded from US core CPI, core PCE and euro HICP core; construction enters only through shelter rent/OER; ISIC Q prices are administered by fiscal authorities the priors lock as constrained. On that reading the coupled world can deliver a genuinely severe relative-price crisis at 4-6% in electricity, care and construction while the locked core aggregate never reaches 2.70%, and CQ6-C is suppressed by basket construction as much as by economics. AND YET my CQ6-C is 22, nine points above the Historian, for reasons that have little to do with the supply walls the effort brief describes: the EM membership weight (~0.70pp) and the imputation structure of the cold leg. The honest statement is therefore uncomfortable for my own lens. The stagflation cell in this question set is carried less by the physical bottleneck story than by an accounting convention and a deflator methodology, and anyone resolving CQ2 or CQ6 in 2037 on a headline, energy-inclusive, core-OECD-only or market-weighted measure would get a materially different answer from the identical world. I report that as a resolution-criterion defect. It is also the reason the ensemble should treat my CQ2 and CQ6-C as the two numbers in this payload most sensitive to a definition the brief did not pin down.
