hypothesis_critique.a: The stated trap is SMOOTHLY, but the panel converged on a better answer and the red-teamer stated it best: the failing word is SUPPLY. Even granting a large white-collar labour saving, no stock of redeployable workers exists. Stanford/ADP 'Canaries' finds the adjustment runs through 'hiring volume rather than pay cuts' — 22-25 year olds in the most AI-exposed jobs down ~6% (13% relative after firm controls) while older workers in those same jobs GAINED 6-9%. A cohort that never entered J/K/M is not a saving to redeploy; it is an entry cohort that chose differently, and the mid-career workers who could plausibly retrain are precisely the ones NOT displaced. Caveats preserved verbatim in substance: US-only, ADP panel, late-2022 to Jul-2025, and the circulating magnitudes (6%, 13%, 13-16%, ~20%) are different measures that must not be pooled; the Yale Budget Lab's contemporaneous read is that the broader labour market shows no 'discernible disruption' 33 months after ChatGPT's release. SMOOTHLY then fails on the second leg: the receiving sector's constraint is licensure, clinical placements and an administered wage below the displaced cohort's reservation wage, not a wage gradient, and the Atlanta Fed tracker shows a dead heat (Education and Health 4.2 in Sep-2025; Finance and Business Services 4.2 in Feb-2026) with no reallocation premium at all. Caveat: those are 12-month moving-average unweighted medians by broad industry group, NOT ISIC F/Q/J/K/M. Third and decisive: AI savings accrue to firms and capital owners while care demand is a public fiscal claim inside the budgets 2A squeezes (net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP), so even a real saving does not finance a care wage bill — the BIS AER 2026 Box C point. Rewrite it as 'after a decade of licensure reform, wage subsidy and large unfilled-vacancy stocks' and it becomes defensible. 5.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail, in opposite directions, and the plank also collapses a distinction the scope lock deliberately draws. BLOCKS is false on mechanism-scope: AI compresses the PRICE of routine VIRTUAL services export (seat-priced IT services, voice BPO, back office) and does not touch PHYSICAL labour migration, which the 2A demographics make MORE valuable — an OECD-38 old-age ratio reaching 39-41% by 2036 with licensed care hours as a binding constraint is a standing bid for migrant care, construction and logistics labour in OECD and Gulf destinations alike. The Philippine comparative advantage PIVOTS from BPO seats to nursing, caregiving and seafaring; remittances from physical migration exceed virtual-services value added there, so the net demographic coupling is plausibly POSITIVE for the economy the plank names as most exposed. BLOCKS is also wrong on its own channel: AI-Q2 at 21.3% says fewer than half of OECD firms will use AI directly in production by 2036, and the integration labour that closes that gap is exactly what Indian services firms sell — partial substitution alongside a complementary demand pull, not a block. SEVERELY fails on magnitude at the national level: India's IT-BPO is ~7-8% of GDP and ~1.5% of employment, India has a large domestic absorber, and the base rate for a cost-arbitrage services-export niche being eliminated by an automation wave within a decade is essentially zero (Indian BPO grew through the 2001 bust, 2008-09, the IVR wave and the 2016-2020 RPA wave, each forecast to end it). SEVERELY is defensible for ONE segment of ONE named economy — Philippine voice BPO — which is why this scores above hypothesis (a) rather than with it. 15.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failing element is THEN — the implied clean two-phase sequencing — and underneath it the MEASURE. Clause one is nearly free and close to already-observed (US core CPI 2.6% Sep-2026, euro-area core 2.5% Sep-2026, US core PCE ~3.0-3.1% Aug-2026 with the Sep actual unverified), so the plank's entire content is the reversion, and the reversion is where it fails. First, the time derivative is backwards: the disinflationary forces are FRONT-loaded (the capex boom's own supply, the AI-Q4 digestion, imported Chinese goods deflation with China CPI at +0.9% and core 1.0% per the NBS release of 14 Oct 2026), while the inflationary legs INTENSIFY into the 2030s — fiscal dominance as net interest climbs 2% -> 3% of GDP at >100% debt/GDP, the Baumol care and grid supply wall whose scarcity eventually clears through administered price increases once rationing becomes politically untenable, and the datacentre electricity bid (PJM wholesale +76% in Q1 2026; US retail electricity ~+7% YoY and +16% YoY in Illinois — caveat preserved from the RBC note: 'the sharpest increase in prices occurred before data center construction really began to accelerate'). Second and decisively, on the measure that actually resolves — GDP-weighted OECD-38 core, with Türkiye, Mexico, Colombia, Chile and Costa Rica inside it at roughly 11% of PPP GDP — the aggregate does not fall to a target-like number even if the G7 converges to target. My own CQ2 puts 0.76 on that aggregate averaging >= 2.50% across 2027-2036 and 0.44 on >= 2.70% in the LATER 2032-36 subwindow, so 'falls in the 2030s' fails on COMPOSITION, not on dynamics. The plank is a G7-shaped claim applied to an OECD-38 measure. It scores 26 and not lower only because a near-term plateau with partial reversion is a genuinely live path and because clause one is close to unfalsifiable. 26.
hypothesis_critique.d: TWO words fail, and the second is fatal. EVENTUALLY is unfalsifiable at a Dec 31 2036 horizon — it exempts the claim from the very window being scored, which is a category error in a dated question, and the Fermi CES arithmetic shows the exemption is doing real work: with sigma = 0.5 and an 0.8/0.2 automatable split the Baumol weakest-link LEVEL cap is hard (Y_max ~5x) but binds in the 2040s-50s, costing the OECD only ~0.15-0.30 pp/yr by 2036. WINS is undefined and smuggles in an unstated metric: aggregate real GDP growth and real GDP PER CAPITA growth come apart precisely when population shrinks, so a shrinking denominator can deliver a per-capita 'win' alongside falling aggregate output, or the reverse; and an aggregate win is fully consistent with the labour-income share collapsing, which is the whole content of the BIS Box C demand-shortfall warning and of regimes B and D. EXPONENTIAL is the third error but the least important here: exponentiating a subset of complementary tasks yields a BOUNDED aggregate, and in any case the binding margin inside THIS window is diffusion (AI-Q2 at 21.3%) and physical energization (transformers >160 weeks, turbines five years, 36-84 month lead-time-to-power), neither of which compounds at a capability rate. I score 17 — above the three Wave-1 seats (14-18 was their range, mostly 14) and below the red-teamer's 22 — because my own A at 18 and P50 at 1.9% give the AGGREGATE growth claim more partial vindication than Wave 1 allowed, while the probability-weighted AI TFP lift of +0.31 pp against a coupled aging drag of roughly -1.1 pp says the offset is about a quarter of the drag, not a multiple of it. Directionally right about the sign, wrong about the functional form, the arrival time and the metric. 17.

key_drivers: OECD-38 GDP-WEIGHTED CORE INFLATION COMPOSITION, MY HIGHEST-VARIANCE AND MOST LOAD-BEARING INPUT. Türkiye ~4.7%, Mexico ~4.0%, Colombia/Chile/Costa Rica ~2.4% of OECD-38 PPP GDP — together ~11% — hold the aggregate roughly 0.4-0.9 pp above a G7 core. This single accounting fact carries CQ2 at 44, makes CQ6-C's >=2.70% gate reachable at 0.44, and starves CQ6-D of its <2.00% condition (D = 12, versus a 0.73 impairment prior that taken alone implies D > C). It is a resolution-definition risk, not a forecasting risk: on a market-FX or G7-proxy read, C and D roughly swap and the long-nominal-bond row of my matrix inverts.

CHINA'S PPP WEIGHT (0.34, drifting from 0.322) TIMES A MEASURED CHINA GROWTH OF ~3.25%, SUPPLYING 1.11 pp OF MY 1.9% COUPLED P50 — more than the entire OECD-38 leg's 0.73 pp. Two red-team corrections move this +0.4 pp against the Wave-1/Wave-2 centre: the aging-drag double count (the locked -2.7 pp is a 2025-2050 no-aging-counterfactual average and China's current print already embeds a working-age peak in 2013 and total decline since 2022; the Fermi seat's implied 5.4%/yr counterfactual made the double count auditable) and measured-versus-true growth (CQ3 resolves on official PPP real GDP via IMF WEO, a smoothed administrative series). I took +0.25 and +0.3 pp respectively, not his full +0.8.

CQ4 AS A TERM-PREMIUM AND NON-US-CONVERGENCE STORY WITH A NET-ZERO DELTA r*. The Fermi ladder's non-obvious result holds: demographic dissaving plus fiscal supply almost exactly cancel precautionary saving, cognitive compression and lower g. What moves the answer is +0.40 pp of real term-premium widening (price-sensitive levered basis-trade accounts as the marginal duration holder, eroding convenience yields, Debt-at-Risk P95 117% +2.4 pp under a 20% AI equity shock, a positive equity-bond correlation) plus +0.20 pp of Japan/Germany/France/Italy convergence (0.365 of G7 weight at 0.30-1.90% real, JGB at a 30-year high) minus a repression wedge cut to -0.14 because the 1945-1980 captive machinery (closed capital accounts, central-bank bid) is not installed. Result: r - g ~ +1.0 pp against G7 g ~1.2%, matching the locked 2A figure and denying CQ6-A its 'stabilizes via growth' clause even inside the growth gate.

RATIONING RATHER THAN PRICING AS THE CLEARING MECHANISM FOR THE TWO BINDING 2036 INPUTS — licensed care hours and HV interconnection / transformer / switchgear capacity. Q wages are reimbursement-set inside budgets that 2A squeezes and interconnection is queue-allocated, so scarcity clears as waiting lists, unfilled rosters and multi-year queues, all invisible to every wage-based resolution criterion in the question set. Combined with the Stanford/ADP finding that the AI labour adjustment runs through hiring volume rather than pay, this drives CQ1 to 9 and hypothesis (a) to 5, and it produces the counter-intuitive healthcare-operator ordering in my matrix: regime C has the most care scarcity and is the WORST regime for care operators (+1.5), because scarcity arrives as input-cost inflation against administered prices.

MOVE's SUB-LINEAR BUT REAL LEVEL-SCALING, THE RED-TEAM'S BEST INDEX-DEFINITION HIT. MOVE is normalized basis-point yield vol, so for a given proportional vol it scales with the yield level; the 75-85 decade averages Wave 1 anchored on were generated at 1.5-2.5% nominal 10y yields against a locked 4-5% nominal / 2.60% real start. But the correct analogue decade is 1998-2007 at 4-5% nominals, where MOVE averaged ~90-100, NOT 105+ — which is the empirical check the red-teamer skipped. Conjunct A lands at 0.50, between Wave 1's 0.32-0.45 and his 0.62, and that is the whole of my CQ5 move from 19-22 to 26.

IMPAIRMENT AS A BOOK-VALUE EVENT, WITH A CANCELLATION EXCEPTION. A written-down GPU still computes and a written-down substation still delivers electrons, so AI-Q4 at 66%+ does not subtract from measured capital services or measured GDP — the Fermi halving (+0.14 -> +0.07) and the Scout's zeroing were a category error worth ~+0.06 pp on my CQ3. Partial only, because CANCELLED buildouts do subtract from investment flow and the revenue-shortfall limb bears on AI-sector output. The impairment therefore routes into CQ5, CQ4's term premium, and the private-credit (-7.0 in D) and AI-complex (-9.0 in D) rows of my asset matrix rather than into CQ3.
wave3.lens_self_description: I answered as the effort-level dragonfly-eye posterior: my only method was to re-weight the five prior panelists question by question on the quality of each specific argument, move where the Wave-2 red-team landed a mechanism or measurement hit and refuse to move where it merely posed, then force internal coherence across my own six answers (CQ6 derived from CQ3 and CQ2 under the lexical lock, CQ4 checked against r-g and CQ6's term-premium language, CQ5 bounded by CQ4's variance and CQ6-C/D mass) — which forbade me from averaging, from importing any outside number not already argued inside this effort, from running the project simulation or web searching, and from treating the three Wave-1 seats' convergence at CQ3 1.8-1.9% as evidence of anything beyond a shared framing.

wave_audit.biggest_update: CQ2: Wave-1 modal 30 (the three seats were 41 / 30 / 26) -> my reconciled 44, a +14-point move and the largest single revision in the effort. CAUSE: a pure accounting identification that the red-teamer forced into the open and that two Wave-1 seats had buried. The Fermi and Scout seats built the OECD-38 GDP-weighted core aggregate on market-FX weights with Türkiye, Mexico, Colombia, Chile and Costa Rica priced inside a 'rest x 0.13 x 2.5%' residual — assigning a decade of Türkiye at 2.5% core, which is an erasure rather than a forecast. On PPP-GDP weights the five are ~11% of the aggregate (Türkiye ~4.7%, Mexico ~4.0%, others ~2.4%) and the arithmetic gives ~2.73% against a 2.50% gate, i.e. the composition carries the question with the G7 block at or slightly below target. I verified robustness (it still clears at Türkiye disinflating to 6%, and it clears on market-FX weights too at ~2.65%, which is why I priced the basis explicitly at 0.70/0.30 rather than adopting the red-teamer's 48). RUNNER-UP: CQ4 P10, Wave-1 modal ~0.9 -> 1.15, driven by the Bayesian seat's 3:1 likelihood ratio on the locked 2.60% TIPS print, which showed that a FIVE-YEAR AVERAGE at the Historian's 0.40% needs a sustained -140 bp fall with no Japanese or German normalization at all. That correction is smaller in points but larger in diagnostic value, because it killed an anchor the Historian himself called a coincidence.
wave_audit.unresolved: THREE things, all resolution-criterion rather than forecasting questions, and they dominate my residual variance. (1) THE WEIGHTING BASIS FOR 'GDP-WEIGHTED OECD-38 CORE'. PPP-GDP, market-FX, or an OECD-published aggregate? I priced it 0.70/0.30 toward a PPP-type read on the Section-2 accounting lock, but no amount of forecasting settles it. It moves CQ2 from 44 to ~30, swaps C and D in CQ6, and inverts the G7-long-nominal row of my matrix from worst conditional holding (-6.5 in C) to best (+6.0 in D). The single highest-variance input in my payload, and the ensemble should treat it as such. (2) WHETHER CQ3 SCORES MEASURED OR 'TRUE' CHINESE GROWTH. Worth ~0.3 pp on my P50 and ~5-6 points on CQ6-A. I took a +0.3 pp measurement uplift, which is between Wave 1's implicit zero and the red-teamer's implicit +0.6-0.8. Unresolvable inside this effort. (3) WHETHER THE F+Q 'REAL MEDIAN HOURLY WAGE' IS A POOLED WORKER MEDIAN OR A COMPOSITE OF SECTOR MEDIANS. This determines whether the red-team's care-aide dilution mechanism is worth ~10 points on C2 or ~2; I gave it half credit and landed C2 at 0.14 between his 0.12 and the Wave-1 0.14-0.25. FOURTH, SUBSTANTIVE RATHER THAN DEFINITIONAL: whether the flight-to-quality bid survives its first test in the new fiscal regime. It is one switch and it sets CQ5's second conjunct, CQ4's right tail, and the entire C-versus-D split of the matrix. All five seats landed between 0.38 and 0.46 on P(bid fails | -25% drawdown) and the honest reason none went higher is a tension nobody resolved: the modal drawdown cause in every panelist's own distribution is an AI capex bust, which is a growth/deflation shock and therefore the shock LEAST likely to break the bid. I held 0.42. That tension is genuinely open.
wave_audit.wave1_spread: THE SPREAD WAS NOT WHERE IT APPEARED TO BE. On CQ3 the three Wave-1 seats looked convergent (P50 1.9 / 1.8 / 1.8) but got there through materially different and partly offsetting routes — China PPP weights of 0.33 / 0.38 / 0.295, China growth legs of 3.0 / 2.70 / 2.8, and capital-services contributions of unstated / +0.07 / ~0 — so the convergence was coincidence, not corroboration. THE REAL DISAGREEMENT WAS CQ2 (41 / 30 / 26), AND IT WAS ONE QUESTION ONLY: at what weight do Türkiye, Mexico, Colombia, Chile and Costa Rica enter the OECD-38 GDP-weighted core aggregate? The Historian identified the composition effect and under-applied it; the Fermi and Scout seats built the aggregate on market-FX weights and priced the five EM members inside a 'rest x 2.5%' residual. That is an arithmetic identification, not a view on inflation dynamics, and it propagated into CQ6-C (27 / 18 / 16) and CQ6-D (11 / 15 / 19) — so the apparent regime-probability disagreement was downstream of a single measurement choice. The second real spread was CQ4 (P50 1.75 / 2.0 / 2.1 with P10s of 0.4 / 1.0 / 1.2), and its whole content was how much weight to give the Reinhart-Sbrancia financial-repression base rate versus the locked 2.60% TIPS anchor. The third was CQ5 conjunct A (0.40 / 0.45 / 0.32), where two seats wrote the correct sentence about MOVE being normalized basis-point vol and then declined to price it.
wave_audit.what_wave2_changed: KILLED, by the RED-TEAMER. (i) The Historian's CQ4 P50 justification — he called the coincidence of today's level with the 1960-2025 unconditional mean his 'single strongest justification' while his own Reference Class 2 said the base rate of a decade staying within +/-50 bp of its start is 25-30%. Dead; I give his CQ4 near-zero weight. (ii) The Fermi and Scout seats' translation of AI-Q4's 66% into a halved or zeroed capital-services contribution. An impairment is a book-value event; a written-down GPU still computes. Dead as stated, though I restored half of it for CANCELLED buildouts, which do reduce investment flow. (iii) The Scout's rule that CQ6-A must sit below the standalone 16.2% Transformative Breakout mass, which the Bayesian seat inherited at A = 11. Dead: A's lexical gate is a GROWTH threshold on an aggregate 34% weighted to a smoothed series, not a TFP gate, and coupling therefore makes A EASIER on the growth gate. This is worth +5 to +7 points of A on its own. (iv) The Fermi and Scout CQ5 conjunct-A levels, on the MOVE normalized-bp-vol point — though only partially, see below. RESCUED, by the BAYESIAN LIKELIHOOD-RATIO UPDATER. (i) The Historian's OECD-38 inflation composition arithmetic, which he restored to full weight against the two bottom-up market-FX builds. (ii) The PPP weight itself, re-identified at 0.322-0.335 by catching Fermi's $73T OECD-38 understatement AND the Scout's 46-47%-of-world overstatement — both wrong in opposite directions. (iii) The whole left tail of CQ4, by treating the locked TIPS print as 3:1 evidence rather than as scenery. He also correctly refused to rescue the Chinese PPI-to-CPI transmission story on the 2021 precedent (PPI near +13% with CPI near 1%), which is why I hold the Scout's reflation evidence at an effective LR of ~1.4 rather than 2.2-2.5. WHERE THE RED-TEAM MERELY CONTRARIAN-POSED, AND I DID NOT MOVE. (a) His measured-China uplift to 3.6% implies roughly +0.8 pp over a true ~2.8-3.0%, which the evidence does not support — China's own growth target is declining through the 2030s, and the 2018 census revision and 2023-24 deflator episodes are counterexamples to a pure upward-smoothing prior. I took +0.3 pp. (b) His CQ6-D of 6 pushes the composition argument past where it can carry: D needs sub-2.0% core only over a five-year SUBWINDOW in a world where a capex bust has already landed, so his 0.18 conditional is too low; I used 0.30 for D = 12. (c) His MOVE conjunct A of 0.62 skips the decisive empirical check — the 1998-2007 decade ran 4-5% nominals with MOVE averaging ~90-100, so the scaling is sub-linear and 0.50 is the defensible level, not 0.62. (d) His C2 of 0.12 relies on a care-aide median-dilution magnitude that depends on an unresolved resolution convention; half credit only. (e) His repression wedge of -0.10 over-corrects: the regulatory-captive channel is real and the BoJ's YCC is a live modern instance of the mechanism he declared uninstalled.
